chapters.translation: I say: This is the eleventh issue (mas’alah) of this section. Know that the sifted treatise (al-Mankhūl) — so named because I have extracted therein the pure marrow of legal theory from the husks of superfluous annotations — now proceeds to address this issue with the discernment that distinguishes the sound principle from the corrupt one, and the decisive indicator (dalīl) from the mere conjecture. Let the reader attend to the following exposition, for therein lies the clarification of what the jurists have disputed, and the unveiling of that which the inattentive have overlooked.

chapters.title_en: The Obligation of the Broadly-Specified Command, the Status of the Commanded Act Before Capacity, and the Prohibitions (Al-Mankhūl, Section 15)
chapters.arabic_text:
الصلاة تجب بأول الوقت على التوسيع ولا يعصي بالتأخير وقال ابو حنيفة لا
يوصف بالوجوب إلى ان يضيق الوقت والكلام معه وقد ناقض في القضا والكفارات
والزكوات سهل فأما من أنكر الوجوب الموسع أصلا وقال اذا جاز الإعراض وتخير
الرجل فلا معنى للوجوب ولا يغني عن هذا الإشكال تصويرنا ولا قول السيد
لعبده أوجبت عليك خياطة هذا الثوب وجعلت الشهر متسعك لم فإن هذا لم يمنع
جواز التأخير وهو يقتضي الوجوب ولا يغني ما قاله القاضي ذبا عن الفقهاء ان
التأخير لا يجوز إلا بشرط العزم على الإمتثال فإن الفقهاء لا يوجبوب حدثنا
ذلك إذ لو ذهل جاز ولأن الأمر ليس فيه اشعار بوجوب العزم وترديد بينه وبين
الفعل لا على التعيين وهذا تحكم والمختار ان تبين الوجوب لا يتحقق إلا في
آخر الوقت لما ذكرناه من جواز
التأخير ولكن الشرع سماه واجبا توسعا كالكفارة وغيرها ودلت الامارات
عليها وهذا التجويز لا مانع منه فيتبع امارات الشرع في اطلاقه مسألة (12)
المأمور لا يعلم كونه مأمورا قبل التمكن
وإليه صار أبو هاشم خلافا للقاضي لأن التمكن شرط يقرر التكليف ويحتمل
اخترام المنية قبل التمكن فكيف يعلم مع احتمال ذلك وقد ثبت أن التكليف بما
لا يطاق محال عندنا والقاضي يعتقد ثبوت الأمر قبل التكليف وعلى هذا جوز
النسخ قبل التمكن وتمسك بأن البدار إلى الإقدام واجب ولا يجوز التأخير
لإرتقاب ابن الموت قبل الإقدام على الفعل فإذا تمكن وجب لأنه لو تكاسل لأدى
إلى خرم الشرع وأبطل غرض الشارع
فأما العلم فلا يثبت  مع الإحتمال مسألة عند المعتزلة المأمور يخرج عن
كونه مأمورا حال الإمتثال وحدوث الفعل المطلوب لأن الأمر طلب والكائن لا
يطلب كما قالوا يخرج عن كونه مقدورا لأن القدرة لا تتعلق بالموجود وخالفهم
أصحابنا في المسألتين جميعا وبنوا الأمر على القدرة ونحن نعتقد أن تعلق
القدرة بالمقدور حالة الوجود لو قدر مسلم وهو اعتقادنا فيجب القطع بأنه
يخرج عن كونه مأمورا لأن الكائن لا يطلب
وأما القدرة فهي سبب الوجود فإذا لم تقارنه لم يحصل الوجود
لأن العدم المستمر لا حاجة فيه إلى قدرة وكذلك الوجود المستمر وبينهما
حالة لطيفة هي أول حالة الحدوث ولا تحدث إلا بقدرة تقارنها فإنها في حكم
الموجد لها والمخرج لها عن العدم فأما الأمر فإنه ليس موقعا للفعل حتى تجب
مقارنته لها فإن قيل هو موقع لكونها طاعة قلنا يمكن إيقاعها بطلب سابق إذ
ليس وجود الفعل متعلقا به ووصفه بالطاعة ممكن بخلاف القدرة السابقة فيتنزل
الأمر مع الطاعة منزلة النظر مع العلم ثم العلم يحصل بتصرم النظر وإن كان
لا بد من تقدم النظر مسألة (14) قال شيخنا أبو الحسن الأشعري رحمه الله
المعدوم مأمور على تقدير الوجود إذ ثبت عنده الكلام القديم وثبت كون الباري
آمرا أزلا
وأبى المعتزلة له ذلك وقالوا الأمر طلب فكيف يتوجه على المعدوم والمجنون
يستحيل خطابه لأنه عديم الفهم فالمعدوم أولى بأن لا يخاطب ثم جعلوا هذا
ذريعة إلى رد الكلام ولا يغني في الجواب ما ألزمهم القاضي من كون المأمور
معدوما إذ ذلك من ضرورته فلا استحالة فيه ولا قوله إن النبي صلى الله عليه
وسلم إذا توفي فهو كالمعدوم في حقنا وقد بقي آمرا بعد العدم فإنه لا أمر
للرسول عليه السلام وهو سفير فالأمر لله تعالى
الذي لا يموت ولأن القاضي لا يجوز كون الآمر معدوما قطعا فلا معنى لهذا
الكلام فالوجه أن يقول لا يبعد من حيث التصور أن يقوم طلب بذات شخص لزيد
من ولده الذي لم يحدث تعلم العلم إذا حدث ويبقى  الطلب مستمرا فإذا وجد
اتصل الطلب الذي هو الأمر به فكذلك الباري تعالى كان الطلب الذي هو الأمر
قائما بذاته قديما ولم يتوجه الطلب على المعدوم ولكنهم إذا وجدوا صاروا
مأمورين بذلك الطلب السابق من غير تغير وتبدل والمعدوم لا يكلف قطعا وهذا
معنى قوله على تقدير الوجود فإن المعدوم إذا قدر وجوده لم يكن معدوما وحكى
عن عبد الله بن سعيد انه قال كلامه كان قائما بذاته قديما ولم يكن امرا
إنما صار أمرا عند الوجود فإن عني به ما ذكرناه وهو الظن فسديد وإلا فهو
قول بحدوث الأمر إذا الأمر إثما كان أمرا لعينه فلا يتغير بالأوقات وثبت
الكلام القديم بدليل آخر ووجه تصور الأمر قديما ذكرناه والله اعلم
القول في النواهي وقد اندرج معظم مقاصدها تحت الأمر فإنها تلوها
فمن توقف في صيغة الأمر توقف في صيغة النهي ومن حملة على الوجوب حمل
النهي على الخطر ومن حملة على الندب حمل هذا على الكراهية ومن حمل ذلك على
رفع الحرج في الفعل حمل هذا على رفع الحرج في ترك الفعل ومقصود الباب تحويه
خمس مسائل مسالة (1) النهي محمول على فساد المنهي عنه على معنى انه يجعل
وجوده كعدمه وهذا هو مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه ولكنا مع هذا نقضي بصحة
الصلاة في الدار المغصوبة خلافا لأبي هاشم فإنه قضى ببطلانها
واستدل بأن المكث منهي عنه والصلاة مكث في الدار بحركة أو سكون فقد تمكن
النهي من نفس الفعل فيستحيل وقوع النهي طاعة إذ ذلك يؤدي إلى وصف الشئ
الواحد بالوجوب والتحريم فأورد عليه البيع في وقت النداء وتحريم المودع
بصلاة وقد طولب بالرد واجناس لهذه المسالة فارتبك وقال اقضي بفساد كل عقد
تمكن التحريم منه ان ثبت التحريم وعورض استبعاده بوقوع فعل الذاهل في اثناء
صلاته طاعة مع عدم التقرب فقال لا بعد في هذا فإنه لم يكلف القصد إلا في
أول الوقت ثم حكمه منسحب كما ينسحب حكم الايمان في لحظة على جميع العمر
وانما البعيد  كون
الشئ الواحد مأمورا مطلوبا واجبا منهيا مطلوب الترك قال القاضي هذه
الصلاة لا تقع طاعة كما ذكره ابو هاشم ولكن يسقط الفرض عندها ولا يسقط بها
وهذا غير بعيد
كما قال ابو حنيفة رضي الله عنه يسقط قضاء الصلوات والزكوات بالرد وليس
ذلك طاعة وإمتثالا فقيل له ثبت جوازه عقلا فما الدليل على وقوعه قال ذلك
موكول إلى رأي الفقهاء فلينظروا فيه نظرهم وليتمسكوا بغلبة الظن ثم قال
يمكن اثبات وقوعه بالتمسك بمسالك الصحابة فانهم كانوا يأمرون الظلمة بتدارك
المظالم ورد المغصوب مع علمهم بأن عمر الظالم لا يخلو من اداء صلاة في دار
استولى عليها ولم يأمروا بإعادة الصلاة فتبين سقوط الفرض به والمختار ان
الصلاة واقعة طاعة لان افعاله تضمن مكثا في الدار واداء الفعل للصلاة فله
جهتان المقصود بالنهي جهة الكون والواقع طاعة اداء الصلاة ولا نظر إلى
اتحاد صورة الفعل إذ الأمر والنهي يتلقى من قصد المخاطب
وعن هذا قلنا الأمر بالشئ لا يكون نهيا عن ضده وان وقع من ضرورته ولو قال
السيد لغلامه لا تدخل هذه الدار وخط هذا الثوب فدخل الدار وخاط الثوب عد في
العرف ممتثلا في الخياطة مخالفا في الكون في الدار وان كان الكون من ضرورة
الخياطة ونحن نحمل النهي على الفساد اذا تمكن من الشئ مقصودا وكذا المودع
إذا طولب بالرد فتحرم بالصلاة صحت صلاته لأنه ليس مقصودا بالنهي وان تضمن
منع المالك من الأخذ وهو المنهي مسالة (2) اذا دخل عرصة مغصوبة وتوسطها وجب
عليه الخروج وانتحاء اقرب الطرق وقال الجبائي يحرم الخروج لأنه تخطى في دار
الغير قلنا والمكث أيضا كون في دار الغير والنهي عنهما جميعا تكليف مستحيل
فليجب الخروج إذ به الخلاص
فإن قال الساقط على انسان محفوف باناس صرعى اذا علم أنه لو مكث قتل من
تحته ولو انتقل قتل غيره فينهي عن المكث والانتقال جميعا قلنا قال القاضي
حظ الاصولي انه لا يجمع بين الأمر والنهي عنهما في المسالتين أما ما يؤمر
به  من الجانبين فذاك إلى رأي الفقهاء والمختار في صورة القتل ان يقال لا
حكم لله تعالى فيه فلا يؤمر بمكث ولا انتقال ولكن ان تعدى في الابتداء
انسحب حكم العدوان
وان لم يقصد فلا يعصي ولا تكليف عليه ونفي الحكم حكم لله تعالى في هذه
الصورة واما الخروج فمكن فانه لا يؤدي إلى اتلاف وهو اقرب من المكث مسالة 3
السجود بين يدي الصنم على قصد الخشوع يحرم وقال ابو هاشم المحرم هو القصد
إذ عين هذا الفعل يقع طاعة بقصد التقرب
وهذا فاسد فإنه إذا قصد اكتسب الفعل حكم القصد فصار محرما كما يكتسب حكم
النية فيصير طاعة وهذا يجره إلى نفي التحريم عن فعل الزاني واخراج الأفعال
عن وقوعها قربة وهو محال مسالة 4 أجمع القائلون بأن صيغة النهي للتحريم على
انه ان تقدمت صيغة عليه لا تغيره فأما صيغة الأمر بالشئ بعد تقدم النهي
عليه اختلفوا فيها قال القاضي في التفريغ على مذهبهم هو للوجوب لأن الصيغة
لم تتبدل وما سبق ليست قرينة مقترنة بها وصار آخرون إلى أنه للإباحة بدليل
قوله وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا وله الاعتضاد بالعرف أيضا والمختار
ان نتوقف فيه إذ يحتمل ان يكون تقدم النهي عنه قرينة تؤثر في هذه الصيغة
ويحتمل خلافه ولا تثبت فيه فيجب التوقف في فحواه إلى البيان مسألة 5 اذا
قال لا تلبس ثوبا من هذه الثياب الثلاثة وأنت بالخيار صح النهي خلافا لأبي
هاشم ومسلك الكلام ما ذكرناه في خصال الكفارة معه في الاوامر فلا نعيده هنا
chapters.anchors:
- Root: و-ج-ب (w-j-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be due, incumbent, necessary; a falling or sinking (as of a wall), hence what is firmly established and cannot be avoided.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theological obligation (wujūb) as that which the Lawgiver firmly attaches to the servant, entailing reward for compliance and blame for neglect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for what is fixed and unavoidable; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to a duty whose time is extended, since the act is not yet strictly due.
- Root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To forbid, prohibit, restrain; the opposite of command (amr).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine prohibition (nahy) as a demand for abstention (ṭalab al-tark), entailing corruption (fasād) of the prohibited act when it is the very object of the prohibition.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the speech-act of forbidding; metaphorical when extended to what is merely discouraged (karāhah).
- Root: ط-ل-ب (ṭ-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seek, demand, request; the pursuit of something not yet attained.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Command (amr) as a demand (ṭalab) directed to the capable agent; the already-existent cannot be the object of a demand.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for seeking what is absent; metaphorical for the eternal divine command, which is a standing attribute of the divine essence, not a temporal act of seeking.
- Root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure, determine, empower; capacity and power over a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine power (qudrah) and human capacity (istitāʿah); the Ashʿarī doctrine that capacity is concurrent with the act, not prior to it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for the power that produces the act; metaphorical for the divine decree (qadar) as the measure of all things.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of Concomitance (Ḥukm al-Luzūm) — When two predicates attach to a single subject from two different aspects (jihāt), the judgment is differentiated by the aspect intended by the speaker, not by the unity of the physical act. This governs the case of prayer in a usurped dwelling: the act is one in form but two in legal aspect (wajh al-kawn vs. wajh al-ṣalāh).
chapters.translation:
I say: The prayer becomes obligatory at the beginning of its time in the mode of extension (ʿalā al-tawsīʿ), and one does not sin by delaying it. Abū Ḥanīfah said: It is not described as obligatory until the time narrows. The discussion with him [proceeds thus]: He has contradicted [his own principle] regarding the making-up of missed prayers (al-qaḍā), expiations (al-kaffārāt), and alms (al-zakawāt). As for one who denies the extended obligation (al-wujūb al-muwassaʿ) entirely, saying: "If neglect is permissible and the man is given choice, then obligation has no meaning" — our conceptualization does not remove this difficulty, nor does the saying of the master to his slave: "I have made obligatory upon you the sewing of this garment and have made the month your extension." For this [command] does not prevent the permissibility of delay, and it entails obligation. Nor does what the Judge (al-Qāḍī) said suffice, defending the jurists: "Delay is not permissible except with the condition of resolving upon compliance." For the jurists do not make that resolution obligatory — indeed, if one were heedless [of it], it would still be permissible. And because the command contains no indication of the obligation of resolution, and [his claim] is a mere arbitrary distinction between it and the act, without specification — this is sheer caprice (taḥakkum).

The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that the realization of obligation is not verified except at the end of the time, for the reason we have mentioned — namely, the permissibility of delay. However, the Law (al-sharʿ) called it obligatory by way of extension (tawassuʿan), like the expiation and other things, and the indicators (al-amārāt) point to that. This permissibility [of calling it obligatory] is not precluded, so one follows the indicators of the Law in its application.

Issue (12): The commanded person does not know himself to be commanded before the attainment of capacity (al-tamakkun). This is the position of Abū Hāshim, contrary to the Judge, because capacity is a condition that establishes the obligation (al-taklīf). And it is possible that death may cut one off before capacity — so how can he know [himself to be commanded] given that possibility? It has been established that obligating what cannot be borne (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq) is impossible in our doctrine. The Judge holds that the command is established before the obligation, and on this basis he permitted abrogation (naskh) before capacity. He argued that rushing to undertake [the act] is obligatory, and delay is not permissible in anticipation of death before undertaking the act. So when capacity is attained, it becomes obligatory — for if one were sluggish, it would lead to a breach in the Law and nullify the purpose of the Lawgiver. But as for knowledge [of being commanded], it is not established in the presence of possibility.

Issue (13): According to the Muʿtazilites, the commanded person exits from being commanded at the moment of compliance and the occurrence of the sought act — because the command is a demand (ṭalab), and what already exists is not demanded. They likewise said he exits from being capable (maqdūr) because power does not attach to the existent. Our companions opposed them on both questions, building the command upon power. We hold that the attachment of power to the capable thing at the state of existence — if it were granted as sound, and this is our belief — then it necessarily follows that he exits from being commanded, because what exists is not demanded.

As for power (al-qudrah), it is the cause of existence. If it does not accompany [the act], existence does not occur — for continuous non-existence needs no power, and neither does continuous existence. Between the two there is a subtle state, which is the first state of origination (ḥudūth), and it occurs only through a power that accompanies it; for that power is, in effect, the one that brings it into existence and brings it out of non-existence. As for the command, it is not what effects the act such that its concurrence [with the act] would be necessary. If it is said: "It is what effects its being an act of obedience (ṭāʿah)," we say: It is possible to effect obedience through a prior demand, since the existence of the act is not dependent upon it, and describing it as obedience is possible — unlike the prior power. Thus the command stands in relation to obedience as reflection (naẓar) stands to knowledge: knowledge is obtained through the completion of reflection, even though reflection must precede it.

Issue (14): Our master Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī — may God have mercy on him — said: The non-existent (al-maʿdūm) is commanded on the supposition of existence (ʿalā taqdīr al-wujūd), since he established the eternal speech (al-kalām al-qadīm) and established that the Creator is a commander from eternity (āzalan). The Muʿtazilites refused this, saying: "The command is a demand — how can it be directed to the non-existent? The insane person cannot be addressed because he lacks understanding, so the non-existent is even more deserving of not being addressed." Then they made this a pretext for rejecting [the doctrine of eternal] speech.

It does not suffice as a response what the Judge imposed upon them — namely, that the commanded thing is non-existent, for that is a necessary consequence [of command], so there is no impossibility in it. Nor does his saying: "When the Prophet — peace be upon him — died, he was like the non-existent with respect to us, yet he remained a commander after death" — for the Messenger — peace be upon him — has no command; he is merely an envoy, and the command belongs to God, who does not die. And because the Judge does not permit the commander to be non-existent, categorically, this speech has no meaning.

The correct approach is to say: It is not far-fetched, in terms of conceptualization (taṣawwur), that a demand should subsist in the essence of a person for Zayd, his son who has not yet been born — [such that] he knows that when he comes into existence, the demand attaches to him, and the demand remains continuous. So when he exists, the demand — which is the command — attaches to him. Likewise for God — exalted — the demand, which is the command, subsisted in His essence eternally, and the demand was not directed at the non-existent. But when they exist, they become commanded by that prior demand, without any change or alteration. The non-existent is not obligated, categorically. This is the meaning of his saying "on the supposition of existence" — for the non-existent, if its existence is supposed, is not non-existent.

It is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿīd that he said: "His speech subsisted in His essence eternally, and it was not a command; it only became a command upon existence." If he means what we have mentioned — and this is the apparent [meaning] — then it is sound. Otherwise, it is a doctrine of the origination of the command (ḥudūth al-amr) — for the command, if it is a command by virtue of its essence, is not changed by times. The eternity of speech is established by another proof, and the manner of conceiving the eternal command is what we have mentioned. And God knows best.

The Discourse on Prohibitions (al-Nawāhī)

Most of its aims are subsumed under the command, for prohibitions follow upon it. Whoever hesitates regarding the form of the command hesitates regarding the form of the prohibition. Whoever interprets the command as obligation interprets the prohibition as prohibition-of-unlawfulness (taḥrīm). Whoever interprets the command as recommendation interprets the prohibition as disapproval (karāhah). Whoever interprets the command as removing restriction in the act interprets the prohibition as removing restriction in the abandonment of the act. The purpose of this chapter is encompassed in five issues.

Issue (1): The prohibition entails the corruption (fasād) of the prohibited thing — meaning that its existence is rendered like its non-existence. This is the doctrine of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him. Nevertheless, we judge the validity of prayer in a usurped dwelling (al-dār al-maghṣūbah), contrary to Abū Hāshim, who judged its invalidity. He argued that remaining [in the place] is prohibited, and prayer is a remaining in the dwelling, whether by motion or stillness. Thus the prohibition has attached to the very act itself, and it is impossible for the prohibited to be an act of obedience — for that would lead to describing one single thing as both obligatory and prohibited.

The objection was raised against him regarding the sale [made] at the time of the call [to prayer], and the prohibition upon the depositary (al-mūdaʿ) from praying [when the owner demands return], while he was required to return [the deposit]. He became entangled in the branches of this issue and said: "I judge the corruption of every contract to which prohibition attaches, if the prohibition is established." His improbability [claim] was countered by the occurrence of the heedless man's act during his prayer as obedience, despite his lack of intention (taqarrub). He said: "There is no improbability in this, for he was not obligated to intend except at the beginning of the time; then its ruling extends, just as the ruling of faith in a single moment extends over the entire lifetime. The improbable thing is only that one single thing should be commanded, sought, obligatory, and prohibited, sought-to-be-abandoned."

The Judge said: "This prayer does not occur as obedience, as Abū Hāshim mentioned, but the obligation falls [from him] by it, though not through it." This is not far-fetched — just as Abū Ḥanīfah — may God be pleased with him — said: "The making-up of prayers and alms falls by the return [of the usurped property], and that is not obedience or compliance." It was said to him: "Its permissibility is established by reason — what is the proof of its actual occurrence?" He said: "That is delegated to the judgment of the jurists; let them examine it with their examination and hold to preponderant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann)." Then he said: "Its occurrence can be established by following the practices of the Companions — for they used to command the oppressors to restore wrongfully taken properties and return what was usurped, while knowing that the life of the oppressor is not free from performing a prayer in a dwelling he had seized, and they did not command the repetition of the prayer. Thus it is shown that the obligation falls by it."

The chosen position is that the prayer occurs as obedience — because his acts include a remaining in the dwelling and the performance of the act of prayer. Thus it has two aspects (jihāt): the aspect intended by the prohibition is the aspect of mere location (al-kawn), while what occurs as obedience is the performance of the prayer. No consideration is given to the unity of the physical form of the act, for command and prohibition are received from the intention of the addressed person. On this basis we say: The command to a thing is not a prohibition of its opposite, even if it follows from its necessity. If a master said to his slave: "Do not enter this house, and sew this garment," and he entered the house and sewed the garment, he is counted in custom as compliant in the sewing and disobedient in the entering — even though the entering is a necessary concomitant of the sewing.

We interpret the prohibition as entailing corruption when it attaches to the thing as intended (maqṣūdan). Likewise, the depositary, when the owner demands return and he is prohibited from praying — his prayer is valid, because he is not the intended object of the prohibition, even though it entails preventing the owner from taking [his property], which is the prohibited thing.

Issue (2): If one enters a usurped courtyard and stands in its middle, it is obligatory upon him to exit, taking the nearest path. Al-Jubbāʾī said: "Exiting is prohibited, because it is a trespassing in another's dwelling." We say: Remaining is also a location in another's dwelling, and prohibiting both is an impossible obligation (taklīf muḥāl). So exiting must be obligatory, for through it deliverance is achieved.

If it is said: "Consider one who has fallen upon a person, surrounded by people who have fallen — if he knows that if he remains, he will kill the one beneath him, and if he moves, he will kill another — then he is prohibited from both remaining and moving." We say: The Judge said: "The share of the legal theorist (uṣūlī) is that command and prohibition are not combined regarding both in the two cases. As for what is commanded from both sides, that is delegated to the judgment of the jurists." The chosen position in the case of killing is to say: There is no ruling of God in it — he is neither commanded to remain nor to move. But if he transgressed in the beginning, the ruling of transgression extends. If he did not intend [the transgression], he does not disobey, and there is no obligation upon him. The negation of the ruling is a ruling of God in this case. As for exiting, it is possible, for it does not lead to destruction, and it is closer [to safety] than remaining.

Issue (3): Prostrating before an idol with the intention of humility (al-khushūʿ) is prohibited. Abū Hāshim said: "The prohibited thing is the intention, for this very act occurs as obedience by intending nearness [to God]." This is corrupt — for when one intends, the act acquires the ruling of the intention and becomes prohibited, just as it acquires the ruling of the intention and becomes obedience. This leads him to negate the prohibition from the act of the fornicator and to remove acts from occurring as acts of devotion (qurbah) — which is impossible.

Issue (4): Those who hold that the form of the prohibition indicates prohibition-of-unlawfulness are agreed that if a command-form precedes it, it does not change it. As for the command-form of a thing after a prior prohibition upon it, they differed. The Judge said in his al-Tafrīgh, according to their doctrine: It indicates obligation, because the form has not changed, and what preceded is not a contextual indicator (qarīnah) attached to it. Others held that it indicates permissibility (ibāḥah), by the proof of His saying: {«وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا»} ("And when you have completed the pilgrimage, then hunt" — Qurʾān 5:2), and it is also supported by custom. The chosen position is that we suspend judgment (natawaqqaf) regarding it — for it is possible that the prior prohibition is a contextual indicator that affects this form, and it is possible otherwise. Since neither is established, one must suspend judgment regarding its import until clarification (al-bayān).

Issue (5): If one says: "Do not wear any of these three garments, and you have the choice" — the prohibition is valid, contrary to Abū Hāshim. The path of the discussion is what we mentioned regarding the characteristics of the expiation with him in the section on commands, so we shall not repeat it here.

chapters.title_en: On the Uses of the Imperative Form and the Definitions of the Five Rulings; Introduction to the Book on General and Specific
chapters.arabic_text:
### | فصل فيما تستعمل فيه صيغة الأمر

تستعمل للوجوب كقوله اقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة
وللندب كقوله تعالى فكاتبوهم وللارشاد قوله كقوله تعالى واستشهدوا
وللاباحة له كقوله تعالى وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا وللتأديب كقوله عليه السلام
لابن عباس رضي الله عنه كل مما يليك وللامتنان ذلك كقوله تعالى كلوا مما
رزقكم الله وللإكرام محمد كقوله تعالى ادخلوها بسلام
وللتهديد كقوله تعالى اعملوا ما شئتم وللتعجيز إلى كقوله تعالى كونوا
حجارة أو حديدا
وللتسخير  كان كقوله تعالى كونوا قردة خاسئين وللإهانة أبو كقوله تعالى ذق
إنك أنت العزيز الكريم وللتسوية كقوله عز وجل اصبروا أو لا تصبروا وللإنذار
كقوله تعالى كلوا وتمتعوا قليلا وللدعاء كقوله عز وجل اهدنا الصراط وللتمني
كقول الشاعر ألا أيها الليل الطويل ألا انجل * بصبح وما الإصباح منك بأمثل
وقوله تعالى كن فيكون إخبار عن نهاية الاقتدار فظاهر الأمر الوجوب وما
عداه فالصيغة مستعارة فيه ومجموعه ثلاثة عشر ويرد النهي لسبعة معان للتحريم
كقوله تعالى ولا تقربوا الزنا وللكراهة كقوله لعائشة رضي الله عنه لا
تتوضئي بالماء المشمس وللتحقير كقوله تعالى ولا تمدن عينيك ولبيان العاقبة
كقوله تعالى ولا تحسبن الله غافلا
وبمعنى الدعاء كقوله تعالى ولا تحملنا ما لا طاقة لنا به
وللأياس أو كقوله تعالى لا تعتذروا اليوم وللإرشاد كقوله تعالى لا تسألوا
عن أشياء إن تبد لكم تسؤكم والله أعلم

### | باب بيان الواجب والمندوب والمكروه والمحظور

قيل في حد الواجب ما يستحق العقاب على تركه وهذا فاسد لأن الرب تعالى
يتعالى عن أن يستحق عليه ثواب أو عقاب وله أن يفعل ما يشاء لمن يشاء وقيل
ما ورد الوعيد على تركه ووجه فساده أنه لو ورد الوعيد قطعا لكان لا يتوقع
المغفرة والعفو فإن كلام الباري سبحانه حق وصدق ولا يمكن تحديده بخوف
العقوبة إذ الوجوب إنما يتميز عن الجواز باستحثاث عقل العاقل على فعله
لاجتناب أمر محظور مقطوع به واقتحام منفعة ناجزة لا يقطع بالعقاب عليه ليس
بعيدا عن العقل
فوجب تحديده بما ورد اللوم على تركه أو بما يعصي تاركه فإن العصيان اسم
ذم يقضي العقل باجتنابه وأما المحظور فكل يحده بنقيض ما حد به الواجب وأما
المندوب فكل مأمور لا لوم على تركه
وأما المكروه فقيل هو ترك المندوب وهو باطل بترك استغراق الأوقات في
العبادات فإنه ليس بمكروه وإن كانت العبادات مندوبا إليها وقيل ما يخاف
تحريمه أو يخاف عليه العقاب أو تضمن اقتحام الشبهة والكل فاسد فإنه مرتبط
بتردد والكراهية حاصلة مع  القطع بنفيها فالوجه أن يقال المكروه كل منهي لا
لوم على فعله وأما الإباحة فتخيير بين فعلين لا يتميز أحدهما عن الآخر بندب
ولا كراهية وأما التروك فعبارة عن أضداد الواجبات كالقعود عند الأمر
بالقيام ثم يعصي بترك القيام لا بالقعود
ووافقنا عليه أبو هاشم فسمي أبو هاشم الذمي من حيث أنه علق الذم بالمعدوم

### | كتاب العموم والخصوص

العام نوع من أنواع الكلام القائم بالنفس كما ذكرناه في الأمر وحده ما
يتعلق بمعلومين فصاعدا من جهة واحدة احتزازا عن قوله ضرب زيد عمرا ومقصود
الكتاب تحويه ثلاث عشرة مسألة

### | مسألة (1)
chapters.anchors:
- Root: أ-م-ر (amara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Command, affair, or matter; the root denotes an act of directing toward something with authority.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, the imperative (ṣīghat al-amr) signifies a demand (ṭalab) for an act from a superior station; its default (aṣl) is obligation (wujūb) unless contextual evidence (qarīnah) diverts it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): The imperative is literal (ḥaqīqah) in obligation; all other uses are metaphorical extensions (majāz) via rhetorical transfer (istiʿārah).
- Root: ن-ه-ي (nahā)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prohibition; forbidding an act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The prohibition (nahy) demands abstention; its default is unlawfulness (taḥrīm), with metaphorical uses for dislike (karāhah), supplication (duʿā'), etc.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Like the imperative, the prohibition is literal in prohibition and figurative in other senses.
- Root: و-ج-ب (wajaba)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be necessary, due, or incumbent; falling or settling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Obligation (wujūb) is that whose neglect warrants blame (lawm) or disobedience (ʿiṣyān) per rational judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Distinguished from permissibility (ibāḥah) by rational exigency, not by fear of punishment alone.
- Root: ع-م-م (ʿamma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To encompass, include, or generalize.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The general (al-ʿāmm) is a speech-type (khabar) subsisting in the self (nafs), relating to two or more known objects from one aspect.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Technical term in uṣūl for universal scope, contrasted with particular (khāṣṣ).
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-Maḥdhūf (Ellipsis Restoration) — In definitions and legal classifications, omitted predicates (e.g., "the obligatory is [that which]...") are restored contextually; also, the rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (appositional clarification) applies in enumerating the thirteen uses of the imperative.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the imperative form (ṣīghat al-amr) is employed for multiple meanings.

It is used for obligation (wujūb), as in His saying: {«أَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ»} ("Establish prayer and give alms"). And for recommendation (nadb), as in His saying: {«فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ»} ("Then write for them [a contract of manumission]"). And for guidance (irshād), as in His saying: {«وَاسْتَشْهِدُوا»} ("And call to witness"). And for permission (ibāḥah), as in His saying: {«وَإِذَا حَلَلْتُمْ فَاصْطَادُوا»} ("And when you have completed the pilgrimage, then hunt"). And for discipline (taʾdīb), as in his saying, peace be upon him, to Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him: "Eat from what is before you (kull mimmā yalīk)." And for bestowal of favor (imtinān), as in His saying: {«كُلُوا مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ اللهُ»} ("Eat from what God has provided you"). And for honoring (ikrām), as in His saying: {«ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ»} ("Enter it in peace"). And for threat (tahdīd), as in His saying: {«اعْمَلُوا مَا شِئْتُمْ»} ("Do what you will"). And for incapacitation (taʿjīz), as in His saying: {«كُونُوا حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيدًا»} ("Be stones or iron"). And for subjugation (taskhīr), as in His saying: {«كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ»} ("Be apes, despised"). And for humiliation (ihānah), as in His saying: {«ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ»} ("Taste! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble"). And for equalization (taswiyah), as in His saying, Glorified and Exalted: {«اصْبِرُوا أَوْ لَا تَصْبِرُوا»} ("Be patient or do not be patient"). And for warning (indhār), as in His saying: {«كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا»} ("Eat and enjoy yourselves a little"). And for supplication (duʿā'), as in His saying, Glorified and Exalted: {«اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ»} ("Guide us to the straight path"). And for wish (tamannī), as the poet said: "O long night, will you not clear away / With dawn, though dawn is no better than you?" And His saying: {«كُنْ فَيَكُونُ»} ("Be, and it is") is an account of the ultimate limit of divine power (nihāyat al-iqtidār).

Thus, the apparent (ẓāhir) meaning of the imperative is obligation, and whatever deviates from this, the form is therein metaphorical (mustaʿārah). The total is thirteen [meanings].

The prohibition (nahy) is likewise used for seven meanings: For unlawfulness (taḥrīm), as in His saying: {«وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَا»} ("And do not approach fornication"). For dislike (karāhah), as in his saying to ʿĀʾishah, may God be pleased with her: "Do not perform ablution with sun-heated water (lā tawaḍḍaʾī bil-māʾ al-mushammas)." For belittlement (taḥqīr), as in His saying: {«وَلَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ»} ("And do not extend your eyes"). For declaring the consequence (bayān al-ʿāqibah), as in His saying: {«وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللهَ غَافِلًا»} ("And do not think God is heedless"). And in the sense of supplication (duʿā'), as in His saying: {«وَلَا تَحْمِلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ»} ("And do not burden us with what we cannot bear"). And for despair (yaʾs), as in His saying: {«لَا تَعْتَذِرُوا الْيَوْمَ»} ("Do not make excuses today"). And for guidance (irshād), as in His saying: {«لَا تَسْأَلُوا عَنْ أَشْيَاءَ إِنْ تُبْدَ لَكُمْ تَسُؤْكُمْ»} ("Do not ask about things which, if made clear to you, would distress you"). And God knows best.

### | Chapter: Exposition of the Obligatory, the Recommended, the Disliked, and the Forbidden

It was said in defining the obligatory (al-wājib): "That whose neglect warrants punishment (ʿiqāb)." This is corrupt, because the Lord, Exalted, is far above having reward or punishment due upon Him; He may do as He wills with whom He wills. And it was said: "That upon whose neglect a threat (waʿīd) has been reported." The aspect of its corruption is that if the threat were definitively established, then forgiveness and pardon would not be expected — for the speech of the Blessed and Exalted is true and veracious. Nor can it be defined by fear of punishment, since obligation is distinguished from permissibility only by the rational mind's exigency (istihthāth ʿaql al-ʿāqil) toward performing it — namely, to avoid a definitively prohibited matter and to undertake an immediate benefit. What is not definitively punished is not far from reason [to undertake].

Therefore, it is necessary to define it as: "That whose neglect warrants blame (lawm), or that whose abandoner commits disobedience (ʿiṣyān)." For disobedience is a name of blame (dhamm) that reason deems obligatory to avoid.

As for the forbidden (al-maḥẓūr), each defines it as the contradictory of what defines the obligatory.

As for the recommended (al-mandūb), it is every commanded act whose neglect incurs no blame.

As for the disliked (al-makrūh), it was said: "It is the abandonment of the recommended." This is false, on account of abandoning the occupation of all times in acts of worship — for that is not disliked, even though acts of worship are recommended. And it was said: "It is that whose prohibition is feared, or upon which punishment is feared, or which entails venturing into ambiguity (shubhah)." All of this is corrupt, for it is tied to uncertainty (taraddud), whereas dislike is established even with certainty of its negation [of prohibition]. The correct view is to say: The disliked is every prohibited thing whose commission incurs no blame.

As for permission (ibāḥah), it is a choice between two acts, neither of which is distinguished from the other by recommendation or dislike.

As for omissions (al-turūk), they are expressions for the opposites of the obligatory acts — like sitting when commanded to stand. One then disobeys by abandoning the standing, not by the sitting itself.

Abū Hāshim agreed with us on this, and he was called "Abū Hāshim the Blamed (al-Dhammī)" because he attached blame to the non-existent (maʿdūm).

### | Book: On the General and the Specific

The general (al-ʿāmm) is a type of speech subsisting in the self (al-kalām al-qāʾim bil-nafs), as we mentioned in the chapter on the imperative. Its definition is: "That which relates to two or more known objects from one aspect" — as a precaution against His saying: "Zayd struck ʿAmr" (which is particular). The purpose of this book encompasses thirteen questions (masāʾil).

### | Question (1)

chapters.title_en: On the Semantics of General Terms (Ṣiyagh al-ʿUmūm) and Their Exceptions
chapters.arabic_text:
المتوقفون عبد في صيغة الأمر توقفوا في صيغة العموم وإليه صار شيخنا أبو
الحسن ولزمه ذلك من أسئلة الوعيدية الصائرين إلى أن المؤمن يعذب بالمعصية
وقول الجهمية المرجئة الذين يقولون إن المؤمن لا يعذب
بالمعصية والخوارج الذين صاروا إلى أن من ارتكب معصية خلد في النار مع
زعمهم أن لا صغيرة إذ مخالفة الأمر كيف كان فهي كبيرة ومنهم من أثبت
الصغيرة وقضي بإحباطها عليه إلا إذا وقع الإصرار عليها ثم اختلفت الواقفية
فمنهم من قال العام مشترك للواحد والجمع كلفظ العين ومنهم من توقف في ذلك
أيضا ووجه إبطال مذهبهم ما ذكرناه في صيغة الأمر على أنا نعلم تفرقه العرب
بين الرجل والرجلين والرجال وتمييز الواحد عن الجمع والجمع عن الثنية وقال
الشافعي رضي الله عنه العام نص في كل ما يصلح أن يكون متناولا له وعزي إلى
شيخنا أبي الحسن أنه قال وإن اقترنت به القرائن المؤكدة فهو متوقف فيه وهذا
النقل غير صحيح
وقيل لم يتوقف في أداة الشرط إذا اتصل بالكلام في قولهم من دخل الدار
فأعطه درهما
والمختار أنه نص في أقل الجمع كما ذكرناه ظاهر فيما وراءه ووجهه ظاهر
وغرضنا من صيغ الجمع يتبين بتقسيم فنقول العموم يتلقى من أدوات الشرط ومن
صيغ الجموع أما أدوات الشرط كقولهم من دخل الدار فأعطه درهما ومن أحيا أرضا
ميتة فهي له وكلمة من اسم تقتضي الإبهام  فتقتضي الإستغراق وقد يتلقى من ظرف
الزمان كقوله متى أكرمتني أكرمتك ومن ظرف المكان كقوله حيث كنت حضرتك قال
القاضي وكذا إذا قال إن أكرمتني لأن إن تقتضي إبهاما وعندنا إنه لا يقتضي
الاستغراق لأن الإبهام آيل إلى المصدر
ومعناه إن كان منك إكرام يكن مني إكرام فهذا نص في الإكرام الأول أما
الثانية والثالثة فنتوقف فيه وأما صيغة الجمع فتنقسم إلى جمع السلامة وهو
ما يسلم فيه بناء الواحد وإلى جمع التكسير وهو الذي لا يسلم فيه بناء
الواحد ثم جمع السلامة ينقسم إلى جمع الذكور كقولك مسلم ومسلمون والأصل فيه
زيادة الواو والنون وزيادة الياء والنون وإلى جمع الإناث وهو منقسم إلى ما
لا يظهر فيه علامة التأنيث
كقولك هند ودعد فيجمع بزيادة الألف والتاء وإلى ما يظهر فيه علامة
التأنيث بالتاء كقولك مسلمة فيجمع بزيادة الألف والتاء مع حذف تاء التأنيث
فتقول رايت المسلمات لان التاء لم تكن من وضع الاسم
ومنها ما تظهر فيه العلامة بالألف الممدودة كقولك صفراء وحمراء فالوجه
إبدال الألف الثاني وهي الهمزة بالواو وزيادة الألف والتاء وما يكون الألف
مقصودا كالحبلى والسكرى تبدل الألف الاخيرة بالياء وتزاد الألف والتاء واما
جمع التكسير وهو الذي ينكسر فيه بناء الواحد بزيادة حرف كقولك رجل ورجال او
نقصان كقولك كتاب وكتب او تبديل حركة كقولك أسد وأسد قال وجمع السلامة في
اللسان للتقليل وهو العشرة فما دونه وما كان من جمع التكسير على وزن
الأفعال كالأثواب او الافعلة أبي كالأرغفة او الافعل كالأكلب او الفعلة
كالصبية فهي للتقليل وما عداه للتكثير واما المؤمنون والكافرون حيث ورد في
القران فهو للتكثير قطعا ويحتمل ان يكون ذلك من احتكام الشرع كما احتكم على
لفظ الصوم والصلاة
ويحتمل ان يكون كما قاله سيبويه ان كل اسم لا تسمح العرب فيه
بصيغة التكثير فصيغة التقليل محمول على التكثير ابتغاء لكثرة الفوائد
كقولهم في جمع الرجل ارجل فهو للتكثير وعلى الجملة نعلم ان الصحابة رضي
الله عنهم لم يترددوا في  ذلك بل فهموا التكثير وليعلم ان الحرف والفعل لا
يجمعان وانما يجمع الاسم وقولك قاما وقاموا ليس جميعا للفعل انما هو تعديد
للفاعل فاذا اردت جمع الفعل ترده إلى الاسم فتقول قام قومتين مسالة 2 لفظ
المسلمين صالح لإندراج المسلمات تحته تغليبا للتذكير على التأنيث ولكنه في
الاصل غير موضوع له خلافا لبعض الناس كقوله تعالى وكانت من القانتين لانه
جمع المسلمين مختص بالرجال ولفظ الناس في وضعه يشتمل على النساء مع الرجال
إذ يقال لها انسان
وقد خولف فيه أيضا والعبيد يندرجون تحت لفظ المؤمنين في لسان الشارع ولا
بد من دليل في استثناثه (لانه يقال لآحادهم عبد مؤمن وقيل انه لا يندرج
لوقوعه مستثنى عن بعض الألفاظ وهو فاسد لأن ذلك لقيام الدليل على استثنائهم
مسالة 3 قال قائلون لا يندرج المخاطب تحت مطلق الخطاب بدليل قوله الله خالق
كل شئ وقول القائل من دخل الدار فأعطه
والمختار انه يندرج لان اللفظ عام والقرينة هي التي اخرجت المخاطب عن
قضية الخطاب فيما ذكروه ويعارضه قوله وهو بكل شئ عليم فإنه عالم بذاته
مسالة 4 اسم الفرد اذا اتصل به الألف واللام اقتضى الاستغراق كقولهم
الدينار افضل من الدرهم والمختار ان ما يتميز لفظ الواحد فيه عن اسم الجنس
بالهاء كالتمرة والتمر فإذا عري عن الهاء اقتضى الاستغراق للجنس وانكره
الفراء
واستدل بجواز جمعه على تمور ولكن هذا جمع على اللفظ لا على المعنى واما
ما لا تدخل الهاء فيه للتوحيد ينقسم إلى ما لا يتشخص ولا يتعدد كالذهب فهو
لاستغراق الجنس إذ لا يعبر عن ابعاضه بالذهب الواحد وما يتعدد كالدينار
والرجل فلا يتناول إلا الواحد والالف واللام فيه للتعريف ان اتصل بالرجل او
الدينار اقتضى تعريف الجنس ولا اثر له في تخصيص واستغراق وانما يفهم الجنس
من قولهم الدينار افضل من الدرهم بقرينة التسعير
مسالة 5 نكرة الوحدان في النفي تشعر بالاستغراق كقوله ما رأيت رجلا وفي
الاثبات تشعر بالتخصيص كقوله رأيت رجلا لان النفي عام لا  خصوص له بأقوام
مضبوطين والنكرة فيه ابهام فلا تقطع عموم النفي والاثبات خاص إذ الرؤية
يستحيل عمومها في كل مرئي والنكرة تقتضي تخصصا وابهاما ما فإذا اتصل
بالاثبات اقتضى تخصيصه بمبهم غير معين وان اتصل بالاثبات كلمة الشرط كقوله
من أحيا أرضا ميتة فهي
له كان للإستغراق لأن كلمة من فيه ابهام فلا تقتضي الخصوص فأما نكرة
الجمع في النفي كقوله ما رأيت رجالا قال القاضي هو للاستغراق كنكرة الوحدان
بل هو أولى وقال أبو هاشم لا يقتضيه بدليل قوله ما لنا لا نرى رجالا ووجهته
ظاهرة إذ يحسن ان يقال ما رأيت رجالا لكني رأيت رجلا ولا تقول ما رأيت رجلا
ثم تقول رأيت لأن فيهم رجلا مسالة 6 قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه الاسم
المشترك اذا ورد مطلقا كالعين والقرء عمم في جميع مسمياته اذا لم يمنع منه
قرينه وكذا اللفظ الذي يستعمل مجازا في محل وحقيقة في محل يعمم كلفظ اللمس
يحمل في نقض الطهارة على اللمس باليد والجماع
قال القاضي والجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز تناقض إذ المجاز ما تجوز به عن
محله فكيف يجمع بينه وبين الحقيقة وهذا إعتراض على اللفظ فإنه لا يجمع
بينهما في محل واحد ولكنه يقول يعمم مفهومه في محلين والمختار خلاف ما قاله
الشافعي رضي الله عنه لان لفظ العين ما وضعته العرب لعموم جملة مسمياته
فإنه لا يطلق لفظ العين لإرادة جملتها كما يطلق لفظ الرجال لإرادة الجمع بل
وضعت لآحادها على البدل فهو عند الإطلاق عندنا مجمل ولا يجمع أيضا بين
الحقيقة والمجاز ولكنه يحمل على الحقيقة على إنفرادها أو على المجاز على
حياله لعلمنا بأن العرب لا تطلق لفظ الأسد وتعني به الجمع بين الأسد
والشجاع نعم يشتمل الجماع على لمس فيكون التعميم لذلك مسألة (7) أقل الجمع
ثلاثة عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه
وقال مالك إثنان وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لعثمان رضي الله عنه ليس
في الأخوين إخوة لما أن رد الأم من الثلث إلى السدس  بهما فقال حجبها قومك
يا غلام وابن مسعود أحب للمقتدين أن يقف أحدهما على اليمين والآخر على
الشمال فإذا كانوا ثلاثة اصطفوا
وهذا مشعر من مذهبهما بأنهما وافقا الشافعي رضي الله عنه ولا شك أن حكاية
الضمير متصلا كقولنا فعلنا ومنفصلا كقولك نحن فعلنا يعبر عن إثنين والعضوان
أيضا يجوز إضافتهما بلفظ الجمع إلى الجملة كقوله فقد
صغت قلوبكما وذلك لاستثقالهم الجمع بين تثنيتين مع انطباق صيغة القلوب
على لفظ الوحدان في بعض المواضع ومحل الخلاف في لفظ الرجال والمختار عندنا
أن أقل ما يتناوله ثلاثة بدليل تفرقتهم بين التثنية والجمع وتسميتهم
الرجلين تثنية لا جمعا مع حصول ضم أحدهما إلى الآخر وفائدة هذا المذهب
عندنا أنا نحوج لا بروم رد الجمع إلى اثنين إلى دليل أوضح مما يحتاج إليه
عند رده إلى ثلاثة ونسميه أيضا نصا في الثلاثة ظاهرا فيما عداه وليس من
فائدته المنع من الرد إلى اثنين إذ الرجال قد يطلق ويراد به واحد عند
القرينة كقول الرجل لزوجته أتخرجين وتكلمين الرجال ويعني به رجلا واحدا وقد
أجمع الفقهاء على أن المقر بدراهم لا تفسر بأقل من ثلاثة فهذا مفروع عنه
مسألة (8) إذا قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أفطر فلان بالجماع فقال
فليعتق
رقبة فيختص ذلك بالجماع خلافا لمالك رضي الله عنه لان ما عداه ليس في
معناه واللفظ غير مستقل فارتبط بالمذكور وإنما لم يختص بالسائل لاستواء
جميع العالمين في التكليف شرعا مسألة (9) إذا قيل لرسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم أفطر فلان فقال ليعتق قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه يتعلق العتق بكل إفطار
لأن حكايات الأحوال إذا تطرق إليها الاحتمال وأضرب الشرع عن الاستفصال
فمطلق كلامه لعموم المقال والأمر على ما قال إن تبينا عدم إحاطة رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم بسبب الإفطار وإن توقعنا علمه فلا نتمسك بعمومه ولا
يكفي في قطع التوهم عدم النقل من الراوي
مسألة (10) اللفظ الذي لا يستقل إذا ورد في سبب خاص فهو مختص به كما  لو
قيل أحلال فقال نعم واللفظ المستقل بعمومه الوارد على سبب لا نظر إلى سببه
عندنا كقوله عليه السلام أيما إهاب دبغ فقط طهر وقيل إنه يختص لاحتمال أنه
أراد بيان هذه الواقعة وهو باطل لأنه يعارضه احتمال إرادة تمهيد الشرع فبقي
عموم اللفظ بعد تعارض الاحتمالات
وليس من محل الخلاف قوله انما الأعمال بالنيات لانه انعطف على الواقعة
وخصصها بحكمها فقال فمن هاجر الحديث مسالة 11 عزي إلى ابي حنيفة رضي الله
عنه تجويز اخراج السبب عن عموم اللفظ
استنباطا من مصيره إلى ان الحامل لا يلاعن عنها مع ان الاية وردت في
امرأة العجلاني وكانت حاملا ومن مصيره إلى أن ولد المشرقية يلحق بفراش
المغربي مع عدم الاحتمال تليقا من قوله عليه السلام الولد للفراش وقد ورد
في عبد بن زمعة إذ تداعى ولد وليدة أبيه وكانت رقيقة ولدت على فراش أبيه
وعنده ان الامة اذا أتت بولد لا يلحق بالسيد وان أقر بوطئها
وهذا أسوأ رأي له في المسألتين جميعا فلا ينبغي ان يتخيل من عاقل مصيره
إلى تجويز اخراج السبب عن قضية اللفظ مسالة 12 العام اذا دخله التخصيص كان
مجملا في الباقي ان كان المخصص عنه مجهولا وان كان معلوما فهو حقيقة في
الباقي يجب العمل به إلا انه مجاز في الانحصار عليه لان اللفظ تناول الكل
فإن اخرج البعض بقي الباقي على اصله وقال القاضي هو مجاز يجب العمل به فإن
عني به ما ذكرناه فذاك
إلا فما ذكرناه رد عليه
وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه حقيقة في الباقي يجب العمل به وقال ابو هاشم:
نتمسك به في واحد، ولا نتمسك به جميعا.
وقال جمهور المعتزلة هو مجمل لا نتمسك به وقال ابو هاشم نتمسك به في واحد
ولا نتمسك به جميعا وهذا محال لا المخرج عنه معلوم فكيف يصير الباقي مجملا
نعم لو كان مجهولا فلا نتمسك به كما لو تمسك متمسك في مسألة الوتر بقوله
وافعلوا الخير لا يجوز لان المستثنى عن  عموم هذا الأمر غير معلوم
القول في الإستثناء وفيه اربعة فصول
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-م-م (ʿ-m-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of encompassing, covering all parts; al-ʿāmm is that which comprehends its referents without exclusion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, al-ʿumūm denotes the extension of a ruling to every individual falling under a lexically general term, as opposed to al-khuṣūṣ (specification).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) when the term's form (e.g., jamʿ, aṣl al-jamʿ) indicates totality; metaphorical (majāz) when a general term is restricted by context (qarīnah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Number and Gender Agreement (al-muṭābaqah fī al-ʿadad wa al-jins) — Arabic distinguishes singular, dual, and plural in verbal and nominal morphology, which al-Ghazālī exploits to prove that jamʿ (plural) is not reducible to ithnān (dual).
chapters.translation:
I say: Those who suspended judgment (al-mutawaqqifūn) regarding the imperative form also suspended judgment regarding the form of generality (ṣīghat al-ʿumūm). Our teacher Abū al-Ḥasan [al-Ashʿarī] arrived at this position, and it was necessitated for him by the questions of the Waʿīdiyyah — those who hold that the believer is punished for disobedience — and by the statements of the Jahmiyyah-Murjiʾah who say the believer is not punished for disobedience, and of the Khawārij who held that whoever commits a sin is eternally in the Fire, while claiming there is no minor sin (lā ṣaghīrah), since any violation of a command, however it occurs, is major. Among them were those who affirmed the minor sin but ruled that it is nullified (yuḥbaṭ) unless persisted upon. Then the suspensionists (al-wāqifiyyah) differed: some said the general term is shared (mushtarak) between the one and the many, like the word ʿayn (eye/spring); others suspended judgment on this as well.

The refutation of their doctrine is what we mentioned regarding the imperative form — namely, that we know with certainty the Arabs' differentiation between rajul (a man), rajulān (two men), and rijāl (men), and their distinguishing the singular from the plural and the plural from the dual. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: The general term is a definitive text (naṣṣ) regarding everything that is fit to fall under it. It was attributed to our teacher Abū al-Ḥasan that he said: Even if corroborating contextual indicators (qarāʾin muʾakkidah) are attached, it remains suspended. This transmission is not sound.

It was also said that he did not suspend judgment regarding the conditional particle (adāt al-sharṭ) when connected to speech, as in their saying: "Whoever enters the house, give him a dirham."

The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that [the plural] is a definitive text (naṣṣ) regarding the minimum plural (aqall al-jamʿ), as we mentioned, and evident (ẓāhir) regarding what is beyond it. Its proof is clear.

Our purpose regarding plural forms will be clarified by division. I say: Generality is derived from conditional particles and from plural forms. As for conditional particles, like their saying: "Whoever enters the house, give him a dirham," and "Whoever revives a dead land, it is his." The word man is a noun that entails ambiguity (ibhām), and thus entails total inclusion (istighrāq). It may also be derived from a time adverb, like his saying: "Whenever (matā) you honor me, I honor you," and from a place adverb, like his saying: "Wherever (ḥaythu) you are, I attend you." Al-Qāḍī [Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī] said: Likewise if he says "if (in) you honor me," because in entails ambiguity. But in our view, it does not entail total inclusion, because the ambiguity reverts to the verbal noun (al-maṣdar). Its meaning is: "If there is from you an honoring, there will be from me an honoring." This is a definitive text regarding the first honoring; as for the second and third, we suspend judgment.

As for the plural form, it divides into the sound plural (jamʿ salāmah) — where the singular's structure remains intact — and the broken plural (jamʿ takhsīr) — where the singular's structure is altered. The sound plural divides into the masculine plural, like muslim and muslimūn, whose basis is the addition of wāw-nūn or yāʾ-nūn, and the feminine plural, which divides into what shows no feminine marker, like Hind and Daʿd, pluralized by adding alif-tāʾ; and what shows the feminine marker with tāʾ, like muslimah, pluralized by adding alif-tāʾ while deleting the tāʾ of femininity — so you say raʾaytu al-muslimāt — because the tāʾ was not part of the noun's original constitution. Among them is what shows the marker with the elongated alif, like ṣafrāʾ and ḥamrāʾ; the correct method is to substitute the second alif (which is the hamzah) with wāw, then add alif-tāʾ. What has a maqṣūrah alif, like al-ḥublā and al-sukrā, substitutes the final alif with yāʾ and adds alif-tāʾ.

As for the broken plural — where the singular's structure is broken by adding a letter, like rajul and rijāl; or by deletion, like kitāb and kutub; or by changing a vowel, like asad and usud — he said: The sound plural in the language is for the small quantity (al-taqlīl), i.e., ten and below. What is of the broken plural on the pattern of afʿāl, like al-athwāb; or afʿilah, like arghifah; or afʿul, like aklub; or fiʿlah, like ṣibyah — these are for the small quantity. What is beyond that is for the large quantity (al-takthīr). As for al-muʾminūn and al-kāfirūn wherever they occur in the Qurʾān, they are definitively for the large quantity. It is possible this is due to the authority of the Sacred Law (taḥakkum al-sharʿ), just as it exercised authority over the words al-ṣawm and al-ṣalāh. It is also possible it is as Sībawayh said: Any noun for which the Arabs did not permit a form of abundance, its form of scarcity is carried over to abundance, seeking the multiplicity of benefits — like their saying in the plural of rajul: arjul, which is for abundance.

In sum, we know that the Companions (may Allāh be pleased with them) did not hesitate in this, but rather understood abundance. Know also that the verb and particle are not pluralized; only the noun is pluralized. Your saying qāmā and qāmū is not a plural of the verb; it is merely a counting of the agent. If you wish to pluralize the verb, you revert it to the noun and say: qāma qawmatān.

**Issue 2:** The word al-muslimūn is fit to include al-muslimāt under it, by way of predominance of the masculine over the feminine (taghlīb al-tadhkīr ʿalā al-taʾnīth). But in its original constitution, it is not set for that — contrary to some people — as His saying: {«وَكَانَتْ مِنَ الْقَانِتِينَ»} ("And she was among the devoutly obedient") [Q. 66:12], because the plural of muslimūn is specific to men. The word al-nās in its constitution includes women with men, since one says for her: insān. This too has been contested. And slaves (al-ʿabīd) are included under the word al-muʾminūn in the tongue of the Lawgiver, and there is no avoiding a proof for their exclusion — because one says of their individuals: ʿabd muʾmin. It was said they are not included, because they occur as an exception from some expressions; this is corrupt, because that [exception] was due to a proof establishing their exclusion.

**Issue 3:** Some said: The addressed person (al-mukhāṭab) is not included under the absolute address, as evidenced by His saying: {«اللهُ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ»} ("Allāh is the Creator of all things") [Q. 13:16], and the speaker's saying: "Whoever enters the house, give him a dirham." The chosen position is that he is included, because the expression is general, and it is the contextual indicator (al-qarīnah) that excluded the addressed person from the purport of the address in what they mentioned. It is countered by His saying: {«وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ»} ("And He is Knowing of all things") [Q. 2:29] — for He is knowing of His own essence.

**Issue 4:** The singular noun (ism al-fard) when the definite article alif-lām attaches to it entails total inclusion, like their saying: "The dīnār is better than the dirham." The chosen position: What distinguishes the singular form from the generic noun by the tāʾ marbūṭah, like tamrah and tamr — when stripped of the tāʾ, it entails inclusion of the genus. Al-Farrāʾ denied this, arguing by the permissibility of pluralizing it as tumūr. But this is a pluralization of the wording, not of the meaning. As for what does not admit the tāʾ for unitization, it divides into what is neither individuated nor multiple, like al-dhahab (gold) — it is for inclusion of the genus, since one does not express its parts as "one gold." And what is multiple, like al-dīnār and al-rajul — it does not apply except to the one. The alif-lām in it is for definition (al-taʿrīf); if attached to rajul or dīnār, it entails definition of the genus, with no effect on specification or inclusion. The genus is only understood from their saying "the dīnār is better than the dirham" by the contextual indicator of valuation (qarīnat al-tasʿīr).

**Issue 5:** The indefinite singular (nakirat al-waḥdān) in negation entails inclusion, like his saying: "I have not seen a man" (mā raʾaytu rajulan). In affirmation, it entails specification, like his saying: "I saw a man" (raʾaytu rajulan) — because negation is general, having no particularity with respect to specific groups, and the indefinite in it is ambiguous, so it does not cut off the generality of negation. Affirmation is particular, since sight's generality over everything visible is impossible, and the indefinite entails a specification and an ambiguity. When attached to affirmation, it entails its specification to an unspecified ambiguous [individual]. If attached to affirmation is a conditional particle, like his saying: "Whoever revives a dead land, it is his," it is for inclusion — because the particle man in it has ambiguity, so it does not entail particularity.

As for the indefinite plural in negation, like his saying: "I have not seen men" (mā raʾaytu rijālan) — al-Qāḍī said: It is for inclusion, like the indefinite singular; rather, it is more so. Abū Hāshim said: It does not entail it, as evidenced by his saying: {«مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَى رِجَالًا»} ("What is [the matter] with us that we do not see men?") [Q. 7:46]. Its proof is evident, for it is proper to say: "I have not seen men, but I saw a man," and you do not say: "I have not seen a man," then say: "I saw," because among them is a man.

**Issue 6:** Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: The homonymous noun (al-ism al-mushtarak) when it occurs absolutely, like ʿayn and qarʾ, is generalized over all its referents when no contextual indicator prevents it. Likewise, the expression used metaphorically in one locus and literally in another is generalized — like the word lams (touch), which in nullifying ablution is carried over both to touch by hand and to intercourse. Al-Qāḍī said: Combining the literal and the metaphorical is contradictory, for the metaphorical is that which is transposed from its locus; how can it be combined with the literal? This is an objection to the expression — for it does not combine them in one locus, but rather says: It generalizes its concept over two loci.

The chosen position is contrary to what al-Shāfiʿī said, because the word ʿayn was not set by the Arabs for the totality of its referents. For the word ʿayn is not uttered intending its entirety, just as the word rijāl is uttered intending the plural. Rather, it was set for its individuals on an alternative basis (ʿalā al-badal). Thus, at absolute utterance, it is in our view ambiguous (mujmal). Nor is the literal and metaphorical combined; rather, it is carried on the literal alone or on the metaphorical alone — because we know the Arabs do not utter the word asad intending thereby the combination of the lion and the brave man. Yes, intercourse includes touching, so the generalization is for that reason.

**Issue 7:** The minimum plural is three according to al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him). Mālik said: Two. Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them both) said to ʿUthmān (may Allāh be pleased with him): "There is no 'brothers' (ikhwah) in the two brothers," when he returned the mother from one-third to one-sixth by them; he said: "Your people have prevented her, O boy." Ibn Masʿūd preferred that for those following [the imam], one stand on the right and the other on the left; when they are three, they align in a row. This indicates from their doctrine that they agreed with al-Shāfiʿī. There is no doubt that the attached pronoun, like our saying faʿalnā, and the detached, like naḥnu faʿalnā, expresses two. The two body parts also may be added with the plural form to the whole, like His saying: {«فَقَدْ صَغَتْ قُلُوبُكُمَا»} ("For your hearts have inclined") [Q. 66:4] — because they found it heavy to combine two duals, while the form of qulūb coincides with the singular form in some places. The locus of dispute is the word rijāl. The chosen position in our view is that its minimum application is three, by the evidence of their distinguishing between the dual and the plural, and their calling rajulān a dual, not a plural, despite the joining of one to the other. The benefit of this doctrine in our view is that we do not require, for reducing the plural to two, a proof more evident than what is required for reducing it to three. We also call it a definitive text (naṣṣ) regarding three, and evident (ẓāhir) regarding what is beyond it. It is not its benefit to prevent reduction to two — for rijāl may be uttered intending one, given a contextual indicator, like a man's saying to his wife: "Do you go out and speak to the men?" meaning one man. The jurists have unanimously agreed that one who acknowledges dirhams is not interpreted as less than three. This is settled.

**Issue 8:** If it was said to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him): "So-and-so broke his fast by intercourse," and he said: "Let him free a slave" — this is specific to intercourse, contrary to Mālik (may Allāh be pleased with him) — because what is other than it is not in its meaning, and the expression is not independent, so it is tied to what was mentioned. It is not specific to the questioner, because all people are equal in legal obligation (al-taklīf) by law.

**Issue 9:** If it was said to the Messenger of Allāh (peace be upon him): "So-and-so broke his fast," and he said: "Let him free [a slave]" — al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: The freeing attaches to every breaking of the fast, because when reports of circumstances are susceptible to probability and the Lawgiver refrains from further inquiry (al-istifṣāl), his absolute speech is for the generality of the statement. The matter is as he said, if we ascertain the Messenger's (peace be upon him) lack of knowledge of the cause of the fast-breaking. But if we expect his knowledge, we do not cling to its generality; nor is the absence of transmission from the narrator sufficient to cut off conjecture.

**Issue 10:** The expression that is not independent, when it occurs for a specific cause, is specific to it — as if one said: "Is it lawful?" and he said: "Yes." The expression independent in its generality, occurring upon a cause, has no regard to its cause in our view — like his saying (peace be upon him): "Any hide that is tanned is purified." It was said it is specific, due to the probability that he intended to clarify this particular incident. This is false, because it is countered by the probability of intending to establish the general law (tamhīd al-sharʿ); so the generality of the expression remains after the probabilities conflict. Not from the locus of dispute is his saying: "Actions are but by intentions," because it turned upon the incident and specified it with its ruling, saying: "So whoever emigrated..." — the ḥadīth.

**Issue 11:** It was attributed to Abū Ḥanīfah (may Allāh be pleased with him) the permissibility of excluding the cause from the generality of the expression — deduced from his position that the pregnant woman is not subject to liʿān, although the verse occurred regarding the wife of al-ʿAjlānī and she was pregnant; and from his position that the child of the eastern woman is attached to the bed of the western man, despite the absence of probability — following from his saying (peace be upon him): "The child belongs to the bed," which occurred regarding ʿAbd ibn Zamʿah when the child of his father's slave-girl was disputed, and she was a slave who gave birth on his father's bed. In his view, when a slave-girl produces a child, it is not attached to the master, even if he acknowledged intercourse with her. This is his worst opinion in both matters. It should not be imagined from a rational person his inclination to permit excluding the cause from the purport of the expression.

**Issue 12:** When a general term is subject to specification (takhṣīṣ), it becomes ambiguous (mujmal) regarding the remainder if the excluded [class] is unknown. If it is known, it is literal (ḥaqīqah) regarding the remainder, and acting upon it is obligatory — except that it is metaphorical (majāz) in its restriction to it, because the expression applied to the whole; when part is excluded, the remainder stays on its original [generality]. Al-Qāḍī said: It is metaphorical, and acting upon it is obligatory. If he means what we mentioned, then that is it; otherwise, what we mentioned refutes him. Al-Shāfiʿī (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: It is literal regarding the remainder, and acting upon it is obligatory. Abū Hāshim said: We cling to it for one [individual], and we do not cling to it for all. The majority of the Muʿtazilah said: It is ambiguous; we do not cling to it. Abū Hāshim's statement — "we cling to it for one and not for all" — is impossible: when the excluded is known, how does the remainder become ambiguous? Yes, if it were unknown, we would not cling to it — as if one clings, in the matter of the witr prayer, to His saying: {«وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ»} ("And do good") [Q. 22:77] — that is not permissible, because what is excepted from the generality of this command is unknown.

**The Discourse on Exception (al-istithnāʾ), containing four chapters.**
