chapters.title_en: Section 28 — On the Infallibility of Prophets and the Legal Import of Prophetic Acts
chapters.arabic_text:
لا يتوصل إلى ذلك إلا بذكر مقدمة في عصمة الأنبياء عن المعاصي وهي منقسمة
إلى الصغائر والكبائر وقد تقرر بمسلك النقل كونهم معصومين عن الكبائر وأما
الصغائر ففيه تردد العلماء والغالب على الظن وقوعه وإليه يشير بعض الآيات
والحكايات هذا كلام في وقوعه أما جوازه فقد أطبقت المعتزلة على وجوب عصمة
النبي عليه السلام عقلا عن الكبائر تعويلا على أنه يورث التنفير وهو مناقض
لغرض النبوة وهذا يبطل بكون الحرب سجالا بينه وبين الكفار وبه اعتصم بعض
اليهود في تكذيبه والمختار
ما ذكره القاضي وهو أنه لا يجب عقلا عصمتهم إذ لا يستبان استحالة وقوعه
بضرورة العقل ولا بنظر العقل وليس هو مناقضا لمدلول المعجزة فإن مدلوله صدق
اللهجة فيما يخبر عن الله تعالى فلا جرم لا يجوز وقوع الكذب فيما يخبر به
عن الرب تعالى
لا عمدا ولا سهوا ومعنى التنفير باطل فإنا نجوز أن ينبئ الله تعالى كافرا
ويؤيده بالمعجزة والمعتزلة يأبون ذلك أيضا والذين أوجبوا عصمته عن الكبيرة
اختلفوا فمنهم من قال كل مخالفة كبيرة بالنسبة إلى عظمته فلا صغيرة أصلا
وكل مخالفة كبيرة
وهذا كما أن رفع الصوت فوق صوت من يماثل الإنسان قد يعد صغيرة وهو بعينه
في مجلس الملوك كبيرة دونه تحز الرقاب فللنسبة بعد تأثير في تعظيم أثر
المخالفة والذين أثبتوا الصغيرة اضطربوا ومثار الاضطراب في أنه هل يورث
التنفير أما النسيان فلا يجب كونه عندنا معصوما عنه في أفعاله وأقواله إلا
فيما يخبر عن الله تعالى لأن تجويزه مناقض مدلول المعجزة ونرجع إلى المقصود
فإذا نقل فعل عن رسول الله عليه السلام فهل يتلقى منه حكم أما الواقفية فقد
توقفوا فيه وعزي إلى أبي حنيفة وابن سريج وأبي علي بن أبي هريرة رضي الله
عنهم أنه يتلقى منه الوجوب مطلقا
والمختار عندنا وهو مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه إن اقترن به
قرينة الوجوب كقوله صلوا كما رأيتموني أصلي  فهو الوجوب وإن لم يقترن نظر
فإن وقع من جملة الأفعال المعتادة من أكل وشرب وقيام وقعود واتكاء واضطجاع
فلا حكم له أصلا وظن بعض المحدثين أن التشبه به في كل أفعاله سنة وهو غلط
وإن تردد بين الوجوب والندب فإن اقترنت به قرينة القربة فهو محمول على
الندب لأنه الأقل والوجوب متوقف فيه وإن تردد بين القربة والإباحة فيتلقى
منه رفع الحرج وليس هذا متلقى من صيغة الفعل إذ الفعل لا صيغة له ومستنده
مسلك الصحابة فإنا نعلم أن الممنوع من فعل فيما بينهم لو نقل عن الرسول صلى
الله عليه وسلم فعله لفهموا منه رفع الحرج
وأما الإباحة فلا نتلقاه فإنه حكم يقتضي التخيير مع تساوي الطرفين وهو
يناقض الندب والفعل متردد بينه وبين رفع الحرج فأقل الدرجات رفع الحرج فإن
تمسك أبو حنيفة رحمه الله بإجماع الأمة على كون النبي عليه السلام أسوة
وقدوة ومطاعا وشرطه الاقتداء به في كل ما يأتي ويذر قلنا معناه أن أمره
ممتثل كما يقال الأمير مطاع في قومه لا يراد به أنهم يتربعون إذا تربع أو
ينامون إذا نام فإن تمسك بقوله تعالى وما آتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نهاكم عنه
فانتهوا وقوله فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره وقوله فاتبعوني يحببكم الله
فكل ذلك محمول على الأمر وهو الذي أتانا به دون الفعل مسألة (1) إذا نقل عن
الرسول عليه السلام فعلان مختلفان في واقعة واحدة وعدل الرواة كما نقل في
صلاة الخوف قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه يتلقى منها جواز الفعلين
والمختار في ذلك أن نقول إن اتفق الفقهاء على صحة الفعلين واختلفوا في
الأفضل توقفنا في الأفضل فإن ادعى كل فريق يتمسك برواية بطلان مذهب صاحبه
فيتوقف ولا يفهم الجواز فيهما فإنهما متعارضان ونعلم أن الواقع من رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحدهما ولا يترجح وإن اتفقوا على صحة واحد فنحكم
به ونتوقف في الآخر والشافعي رضي الله عنه إنما قال ذلك في صلاة الخوف وقد
رجح إحدى الروايتين على  الأخرى لقربه إلى أبهة الصلاة مسألة (2) إذا نقل عن
رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فعل حمل على الوجوب بقرينة أو على غيره ثم
نقل فعل يناقضه قال القاضي لا يقطع بكونه نسخا لاحتمال أنه انتهى لمدة
الفعل الأول وإن كنا نعلم أن الفعل الأول لو بقي لاقتضى الحكم على التأبيد
ولكنه لا صيغة له
وهذا محتمل فيتوقف في كونه ناسخا ونعلم انتهاء ذلك الحكم قطعا فإن
النسخ رفع للشئ بعد الثبوت عندي وأما اللفظ فإنه بصيغته يتضمن إثبات
الحكم إطلاقا وابن مجاهد صار إلى أنه نسخ ويتردد في القول الطارئ على الفعل
ولا وجه لهذا الفرق والأصح ما ذكره القاضي مسألة (3) قال الشافعي رضي الله
عنه استبشار رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وسروره بالشئ يدل على كونه حقا
وتمسك بسروره في قصة مجزز المدلجي وإلحاقه زيدا بأسامة في إثبات القيافة
وقال لا يسر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلا بالحق ولا يستبشر بالباطل
وهذا ضعيف فإنما سر بكلمة صدق صدرت ممن هو مقبول القول في ما بين الكفار
على مناقضة قولهم لما قدحوا في نسب أسامة إذ كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم قد نادى به
فإن قيل لو كان باطلا لرد فإنه حكم على الغيب قلنا من نسب ابنا إلى أبيه
الذي شهر به لا يمنع منه والفاسق إذا شهد على النسب لا يزجر وإن لم يقبل
منه ولا يقال هذا حكم على الغيب مسألة (4)
تقرير رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مسلما على فعل وتركه النكير عليه مع
فهمه الواقعة وعدم ذهوله عنه يتمسك به في جواز التقرير إذا كان الفعل بحيث
لو قدر الإقدام عليه لكان كبيرة إذ كان يتحتم عليه بيان الحكم فسكوته مع
العيان دل على الجواز وإن كان الفعل صغيرة لو قدر محرما وكنا لا نجوز
الصغيرة على الرسول عليه السلام تمسكنا به
وإن جوزنا فلا نتمسك به إلا أن يتكرر في مجلسه ذلك ولا ينكر إذ الإصرار
على الصغيرة  كبيرة ولا يقرر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصغائر
والذي أراه والعلم عند الله قطع القول بجواز التمسك به من غير تفصيل بين
الصغيرة والكبيرة فإنا نعلم ان الصحابة رضي الله عنهم كانوا يفهمون منه
الجواز وإن كان الفعل من جملة الصغائر لو قدر محرما وإن تمسك متمسك به في
إثبات عصمة النبي عليه السلام عن الصغيرة لقبول الصحابة ذلك من غير تفصيل
فله وجه وأما تقريره الكافر فلا تمسك فيه لأنه كان يعرض عنهم وفي تقرير
المنافق خلاف لأنه كان ينحو بهم نحو المسلمين فإن قيل إذا قرر مسلما فيحتمل
أنه كان ينتظر الوحي قلنا لو كان كذلك لأمر بالتوقف كما نقل عنه في بعض
الوقائع والله اعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ص-م (ʿ-ṣ-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To protect, defend, or preserve; the core sense is prevention from harm or error, hence 'infallibility' (ʿiṣmah) as divine preservation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿiṣmah denotes God's safeguarding of the prophet from sin and error, a necessary condition for the veracity of prophetic conveyance (tablīgh).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is physical protection; metaphorical (majāz) extension applies to moral and legal immunity from transgression.
- Root: ن-ق-ل (n-q-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To transmit, convey, or carry; in legal theory, it signifies the transmission of reports (naql) establishing prophetic precedent.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Naql is the vehicle of authoritative knowledge (ʿilm) from revelation and prophetic practice, distinct from rational inference (naẓar).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical carrying; metaphorical use denotes the chain of transmission (isnād) in hadith and legal evidence.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To join or couple; a 'qarīnah' is an accompanying indicator that determines the meaning of an ambiguous term or act.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, qarīnah contextualizes whether a prophetic act signals obligation (wujūb), recommendation (nadb), or permissibility (ibāḥah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal conjunction of things; metaphorical extension to contextual clues in discourse and action.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Element) — When a verbal form lacks explicit syntactic force, its legal import is inferred from contextual governors (qarāʾin), analogous to how omitted operators are reconstructed in Arabic syntax.
chapters.translation:
I say: One cannot attain that end except by mentioning a preamble concerning the infallibility of the prophets from sins, and this is divided into minor sins (ṣaghāʾir) and major sins (kabāʾir). It has been established by the path of transmitted evidence (naql) that they are infallible from major sins. As for minor sins, there is hesitation among the scholars, and the predominant opinion is that they occur, and some verses and narratives allude to this. This discourse concerns their actual occurrence. As for their permissibility, the Muʿtazilites have unanimously affirmed that the infallibility of the prophet, peace be upon him, from major sins is rationally obligatory, relying on the claim that it engenders aversion (tanfīr), which contradicts the purpose of prophethood. This is refuted by the fact that war is a fluctuating contest between him and the disbelievers, and by this some Jews clung in their denial of him. The chosen position is what al-Qāḍī mentioned: that their infallibility is not rationally obligatory, for the impossibility of its occurrence is neither evident by necessity of reason nor by rational reflection, nor is it contradictory to the import of the miracle (muʿjizah). For the import of the miracle is the truthfulness of his utterance in what he reports concerning God, exalted be He. Hence, it is not permissible for falsehood to occur in what he reports about the Lord, exalted be He — neither deliberately nor by forgetfulness. The meaning of aversion is invalid, for we deem it permissible that God, exalted be He, might inform a disbeliever and support him with a miracle, and the Muʿtazilites also reject this.

Those who made his infallibility from major sins obligatory differed. Among them are those who said: every act of disobedience is major relative to his greatness, so there is no minor sin at all, and every disobedience is major. This is like how raising one's voice above that of a peer among humans may be deemed minor, yet the very same act in the court of kings is major, such that necks are struck for it. Thus, relativity has an effect in magnifying the impact of disobedience. Those who affirmed minor sins were perturbed, and the source of perturbation is whether it engenders aversion. As for forgetfulness (nisyān), we do not hold that he must be infallible from it in his acts and statements, except in what he reports about God, exalted be He, because deeming it permissible contradicts the import of the miracle. We now return to the intended purpose.

When an act is transmitted from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, is a ruling derived from it? As for the Wāqifiyyah, they suspended judgment. It is attributed to Abū Ḥanīfah, Ibn Surayj, and Abū ʿAlī ibn Abī Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them, that obligation is derived from it absolutely. The chosen position with us — and it is the school of al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him — is that if an indicator of obligation (qarīnah al-wujūb) accompanies it, such as his saying: «Pray as you have seen me praying» (ṣallū kamā raʾaytumūnī uṣallī), then it is obligation. If no indicator accompanies it, then we consider: if it falls among the customary acts of eating, drinking, standing, sitting, reclining, and lying down, then it has no ruling at all. Some traditionists (muḥaddithūn) supposed that imitating him in all his acts is a sunnah, and this is an error. If it wavers between obligation and recommendation (nadb), then if an indicator of devotional proximity (qurbah) accompanies it, it is carried upon recommendation, because it is the lesser [degree], and obligation is suspended. If it wavers between devotional proximity and permissibility (ibāḥah), then the removal of restriction (rafʿ al-ḥaraj) is derived from it. This is not derived from the form of the act, for the act has no linguistic form. Its basis is the path of the Companions, for we know that if a prohibited act among them were transmitted as performed by the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, they would understand from it the removal of restriction. As for permissibility, we do not derive it, for it is a ruling that entails choice with equivalence of the two sides, and it contradicts recommendation. The act wavers between it and the removal of restriction, so the least of the degrees is the removal of restriction.

If Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, clings to the consensus of the ummah that the prophet, peace be upon him, is an exemplar (uswah), a model (qudwah), and obeyed (muṭāʿ), and he conditions emulation of him in everything he does and leaves, we say: its meaning is that his command is complied with, just as it is said, 'the commander is obeyed among his people,' not meaning that they sit when he sits or sleep when he sleeps. If he clings to His saying, exalted be He: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it} (wa-mā ātākumu al-rasūlu fa-khudhūhu wa-mā nahākum ʿanhu fa-intahū), and His saying: {So let those who oppose his command beware} (fa-l-yahdhar alladhīna yukhālifūna ʿan amrihi), and His saying: {Follow me, and God will love you} (fa-ittabiʿūnī yuḥbibkumu Allāh) — all of this is carried upon the command, which is what he brought to us, not upon the act.

Issue (1): If two differing acts are transmitted from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in a single incident, and the transmitters are equitable, as transmitted in the prayer of fear (ṣalāt al-khawf), al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said: permissibility of both acts is derived from them. The chosen position in this is that we say: if the jurists agree upon the validity of both acts but differ over which is more virtuous, we suspend judgment over the more virtuous. If each faction claims to cling to a narration that invalidates the position of its opponent, then suspension applies, and permissibility of both is not understood, for they are contradictory, and we know that one of them actually occurred from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, without preponderance. If they agree upon the validity of one, we rule by it and suspend judgment over the other. Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, only said this in the prayer of fear, and he preponderated one of the two narrations over the other due to its closer affinity to the solemnity of prayer.

Issue (2): If an act is transmitted from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, carried upon obligation by an indicator or upon something else, then an act contradicting it is transmitted, al-Qāḍī said: it is not definitively judged to be abrogation (naskh), due to the possibility that the duration of the first act had ended. Even though we know that had the first act remained, it would have entailed the ruling perpetually, yet it has no linguistic form. This is possible, so suspension applies regarding its being an abrogator, while we know with certainty the termination of that ruling. For abrogation, in my view, is the removal of a thing after its establishment. As for the verbal statement, it entails the affirmation of the ruling absolutely by its form. Ibn Mujāhid held that it is abrogation, and he wavered regarding a statement supervening upon the act, and there is no basis for this distinction. The more correct position is what al-Qāḍī mentioned.

Issue (3): Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said: the Messenger of God's, peace be upon him, rejoicing (istibshār) and delight in a thing indicates its being true. He clung to his delight in the story of Mujazziz al-Mudlijī and his attributing Zayd to Usāmah in affirming physiognomy (qiyāfah), and he said: the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, does not rejoice except in truth and does not delight in falsehood. This is weak, for he only rejoiced at a word of truth uttered by one whose word was accepted among the disbelievers, contradicting their claim when they impugned Usāmah's lineage, since the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, had proclaimed it. If it is said: had it been false, he would have rejected it, for it is a judgment upon the unseen, we say: one who attributes a son to his father, who is publicly known as such, is not prevented from it. And a sinner who testifies to lineage is not rebuked, even if his testimony is not accepted, and it is not said this is a judgment upon the unseen.

Issue (4): The Messenger of God's, peace be upon him, confirming (taqrīr) a Muslim upon an act and his leaving off censure of it, with his comprehension of the incident and his lack of heedlessness of it, is used as evidence for the permissibility of confirmation when the act is such that, were one to proceed upon it, it would be a major sin, since it would be incumbent upon him to clarify the ruling. Thus, his silence despite witnessing it indicates permissibility. If the act were a minor sin, were it presumed forbidden, and we do not deem minor sins permissible upon the Messenger, peace be upon him, we use it as evidence. If we deem them permissible, we do not use it unless it recurs in his assembly without censure, for persistence upon a minor sin is a major sin, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, does not confirm minor sins. What I see — and God knows best — is the definitive assertion of the permissibility of using it as evidence without differentiation between minor and major sins. For we know that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, understood permissibility from it, even if the act were among minor sins were it presumed forbidden. If one uses it as evidence for affirming the prophet's, peace be upon him, infallibility from minor sins, due to the Companions' acceptance of that without differentiation, it has some basis. As for his confirming a disbeliever, there is no evidence in it, for he used to turn away from them. Regarding his confirming a hypocrite, there is disagreement, for he used to incline them toward the Muslims. If it is said: when he confirmed a Muslim, it is possible he was awaiting revelation, we say: had it been so, he would have commanded suspension, as transmitted from him in some incidents. And God knows best.

chapters.title_en: Section 29 — On the Laws of Those Before Us; and the Book of Reports (Kitāb al-Akhbār)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | القول في شرائع من قبلنا

ونقدم عليه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن أوحي إليه هل كان على
شرعة رسول أجمعت المعتزلة انه لم يكن على شرعة رسول فأنه يورث التنفير فإن
التابع لا يكون متبوعا واختلف أصحابنا فمنهم من قال كان على شرعة نبي فإن
الانسلال عن ربقة التكاليف والخروج من ضوابط الشرائع يزري بمنصبه ثم
اختلفوا فقيل كان على شرعة نوح عليه السلام بدليل قوله تعالى شرع لكم من
الدين ما وصى به نوحا وقيل كان على شرعة إبراهيم عليه السلام بدليل قوله
تعالى إن أولى الناس بإبراهيم الاية.
وقيل على شرعة عيسى عليه السلام فإنه الناسخ المتأخر فإن قيل كانت محرفة
مغيرة قلنا كان منهم أحبار يعرفونها على وجهها فتحريف بعضهم لا يرفع الشرع
كاتفاق فترة في شرعنا فإن قيل للذين قالوا كان على شرعة إبراهيم شريعة عيسى
ناسخة أجابوا بأنه لا يثبت كونه مبعوثا إلى الجميع فلعل ملة إبراهيم
استرسلت على ذريته فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم منهم
وأما القاضي فإنه قال أقطع بأنه لم يكن على شريعة نبي إذ لو كان لتواتر
فإن أحوال الرجل العظيم في مثل هذا تتوافر البواعث على نقله نعم كان على
عقد التوحيد والمختار التوقف  فيه وما ذكره القاضي يعارضه أنه لو كان منسلا
عن التكليف أربعين سنة متميزا عن أصناف الخلائق بأجمهم لتوفرت البواعث على
نقله فإذا لم ينقل هذا ولا ذاك توقفنا ولعل الله تعالى قطع بواعث الخلق على
نقله
ولعل الله تعالى قطع بواعث الخلق وطمس حالته والتحق هذا بمعجزاته الخارقة
للعادة رجعنا إلى المقصود قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه في كتاب الأطعمة الرجوع
في استحلال الحيوانات إلى النصوص وآثار الصحابة رضي الله عنهم فإن لم يكن
فإلى استخباث العرب واستطابتها يقول فإن لم يكن فما صادفنا حراما أو حلالا
في شرع من قبلنا ولم نجد ناسخا له اتبعناه وعضد هذا المذهب بالدليل أن يقال
نفس بعثة الرسول لا تتضمن نسخ الشرائع إذ أصحاب الملل من الشرائع ستة آدم
ونوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى عليهم السلام ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فلا
بعد في التظاهر على دين واحد فكان في زمان موسى عليه السلام ألف نبي يحكمون
بالتوراة
ولم ينقل من الرسول عليه السلام نص في نسخ شريعة من قبلنا وقد عجزنا عن
مأخذ من شريعتنا رجعنا إليه
ثم اختلفوا فيمن يتبع شريعته ورددوه الذي بين نوح وإبراهيم وعيسى كما
ذكروه في دين الرسول قبل النبوة والمختار أن لا رجوع إلى دين أحد من
الأنبياء إذ لو كان من مآخذ الشريعة لبين لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
كما بين القياس وغيره من المآخذ ورجع إليه واحد من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم
مع طول الدهور وكثرة الوقائع وشدة ترويهم فيها ورجوعهم في الاشتوار إلى
الجماعة وكان فيهم كعب الأحبار ولم يراجع قط فاستبان بهذا أنه لا حكم له
أصلا

### | كتاب الأخبار

والكلام يقع في هذا الكتاب في قسمين الأول أخبار التواتر وفيه أربعة
أبواب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش ر ع (sharʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To lay down a path or law; sharīʿah as a clear, trodden way of divine ordinance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Sharʿ denotes divine legislation revealed through prophets; technical term for revealed law (sharīʿah) as opposed to rational judgment.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) — a water-source or path; metaphorical (majāz) — the revealed code of a prophet.
- Root: ن س ل (nasala)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To slip out, detach, or emerge; insilāl — extraction or withdrawal from a binding.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for disengagement from obligation (taklīf); implies a rupture of covenantal bond.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — drawing a sword from a sheath; metaphorical — being freed from legal constraint.
- Root: ت و ر (tawātara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Successive, uninterrupted coming; tawātur — report transmitted by such multiplicity as precludes collusion.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Epistemic criterion for certain knowledge (ʿilm) in uṣūl al-fiqh; yields necessary assent.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — sequential arrival; technical — mass transmission.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — parsing of "law kāna... la-tawātara" (counterfactual conditional) and "illā annahu" (exceptive clause) to distinguish hypothetical from categorical assertion.
chapters.translation:
I say: We preface this discussion with the following. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before revelation was sent down to him — was he upon the law of a messenger? The Muʿtazilites have unanimously agreed that he was not upon the law of any messenger, for that would engender aversion (tanfīr); since the follower would then be a followed one. Our companions (the Ashʿarites) differed. Among them it was said: He was upon the law of a prophet. For slipping out of the yoke of obligations (takālīf) and exiting the constraints of the laws disparages his station. Then they differed further. It was said: He was upon the law of Noah, peace be upon him, by the proof of His saying, the Exalted: {«شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ الدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِ نُوحًا»} ("He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah"). And it was said: He was upon the law of Abraham, peace be upon him, by the proof of His saying, the Exalted: {«إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ»} ("Indeed, the most worthy of people of Abraham...") — the verse. And it was said: He was upon the law of Jesus, peace be upon him, for it is the abrogating (nāsikh) and the later one. If it is said: But it was altered and changed (muḥarrafah mughayyarah), we reply: There were among them rabbis (aḥbār) who knew it in its proper form; the alteration by some of them does not nullify the law, just as a period of intermission (fatrah) occurs in our own law. If it is said to those who held he was upon the law of Abraham: The law of Jesus is abrogating, they answer: It is not established that he (Jesus) was sent to all; perhaps the creed of Abraham continued (istarsalat) upon his progeny, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was among them.

As for the Judge (al-Qāḍī, i.e., Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī), he said: I assert categorically that he was not upon the law of any prophet. For had he been, it would have been transmitted by tawātur (mass transmission), since the circumstances of a great man in such a matter would have abundant motives (dawāʿī) for its transmission. Yes, he was upon the creed of monotheism (ʿaqd al-tawḥīd). The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is to suspend judgment (tawaqquf) therein. What the Judge mentioned is countered by the fact that had he been detached from obligation (munsal ʿan al-taklīf) for forty years, distinguished from all classes of creatures in their entirety, the motives would have abounded for its transmission. So when neither this nor that was transmitted, we suspend judgment. Perhaps God, the Exalted, cut off the motives of creation from transmitting it, and perhaps God, the Exalted, cut off the motives of creation and obliterated his state — and this attaches to his miracles that break the customary (khāriqah lil-ʿādah).

We return to the intended purpose. Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said in the Book of Foods (Kitāb al-Aṭʿimah): In the permissibility (istihlāl) of animals, one reverts to the texts and the reports of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. If there is none, then to the Arabs' estimation of what is foul (istikhbāth) and what is wholesome (istitābah). He said: If there is none, then whatever we find as forbidden or permissible in the law of those before us, and we find no abrogator for it, we follow it. This position was reinforced by the proof that one says: The very sending of a messenger does not entail the abrogation of the laws. For the possessors of laws among the religions are six: Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, peace be upon them, and the Messenger of God, peace be upon him. There is no improbability in their successive appearance upon one religion. Thus in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, there were a thousand prophets judging by the Torah. And no explicit text (naṣṣ) has been transmitted from the Messenger, peace be upon him, regarding the abrogation of the law of those before us, while we have failed to find a source (maʾkhadh) in our own law, so we revert to it.

Then they differed concerning whose law is to be followed, and they restricted it to that between Noah, Abraham, and Jesus, as they mentioned regarding the religion of the Messenger before prophethood. The chosen position (al-mukhtār) is that there is no reversion to the religion of any of the prophets. For had it been among the sources of the law, the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, would have clarified it for us, just as he clarified analogy (qiyās) and other sources. And not a single one of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, reverted to it, despite the length of eras, the multitude of events, and their intense deliberation therein, and their reversion in consultation to the community. Among them was Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, and he was never consulted on it. So it became clear by this that it has no ruling (ḥukm) at all.

### | The Book of Reports (Kitāb al-Akhbār)

The discussion in this book falls into two divisions. The first: Reports of tawātur (mass transmission), and it contains four chapters.

chapters.title_en: Section 30 — On Establishing That the Mutawātir Report Yields Necessary Knowledge
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الباب الأول في إثبات كون الخبر المتواتر مفيدا للعلم الضروري

وقد أنكرت السمنية كونه مفيدا للعلم فنقول لهم إن استربتم أن في الدنيا
بلدة يقال لها بغداد فقد جحدتم وإن اعترفتم فلم تناطقكم البلدة ولا
رأيتموها فلم  تعرفوه إلا بالتواتر كيف ولولا التواتر لما ميز المرء بين أمه
وسائر نساء العالمين
وإن اعترف الكعبي بأصل العلم ولكنه ادعى أنه نظري فقيل نرى الصبيان
يعلمون ما يخبر عنه العدد المتواتر ولم يهيئوا للنظر ودرك المعقولات
بالتأمل ثم يقال لهم نظر أفضى إلى أن في الدنيا بلدة تسمى بغداد سوى
الضرورة الحاصلة من الأخبار فإن قالوا علمنا بأن الجمع الذي أخبروا عنه في
العادة لا يتواطؤون على الكذب قلنا ولم علمتم ذلك ولم أحلتم الكذب منهم وهو
جائز الوقوع من حيث التصور فلا نزال نطالبهم إلى أن يعجزوا عن إبداء مسلك
نظري فيبوحوا علي بما إليه ذهبنا وغايتهم أنه لا بد من أدنى تأمل ليعرف أن
هؤلاء لا يكذبون ولو صار العلم نظريا بمثله لقيل المدركات معلومة بالنظر إذ
لا بد فيها من فتح الجفون والتحديق وارتفاع الموانع وغيرها
تمسك الكعبي على أصحابنا بأن قال أعلمتم كون هذا العلم ضروريا بالضرورة
أم بالنظر فإن علمتموه ضرورة فمحال لأنا لا نعلمه
وإن ادعيتم النظر فكيف يتصور أن يعلم الشئ ضرورة ثم يعلم كونه ضروريا
بالنظر وهذا العلم أولى بأن يكون معلوما ضرورة وهو قائم بنفس العالم بما
أخبر عنه المخبرون ولا يتعلق به إدراك أجاب القاضي بأن هذا استبعاد مجرد
فإنا نعلم كون بغداد بالضرورة ونعلم بالنظر كونه ضروريا ووجه النظر أن نبطل
كل مسلك يتصور إحالة العلم عليه وهذا يلزمه أن يقول بالنظر يعلم أن العلم
المتعلق باستحالة المتضادات ضروري عند إبطال مسالك النظر فيه وهذا لا وجه
له ثم يقال للقاضي العلم المتعلق بهذا العلم يزيد عليه أم هو عينه إن كان
لا يزيد عليه فلا وجه لتنويعه
فإن زاد عليه فهذا محال إذ يلزم عليه إثبات علوم لا نهاية لها أو إثبات
علم لا يعلمه العالم وهذا محال والمختار عندنا في هذه المسألة وفيه الجواب
عن السؤال أن نقول الذي نعتقده أن العلم لا يتلقى من أقوال المخبرين إنما
يتلقى من القرائن الدالة على الصدق الحاسمة حتى  لخيال الكذب ولذلك يجوز
اقترانه بقول واحد على انفراده فإذا ثبت هذا فنقول ورآه الكعبي علم ما
علمناه ضرورة من صدق المخبرين ومن كون العلم ضروريا نعم نوافقه في أن العلم
يتلقى من القرائن
فإن كان يعنى بالنظر توقفه على الاطلاع على القرائن بالبحث والتأمل فهذا
مسلم له ووراء الاطلاع على القرائن يحصل العلم ضروريا من غير نظر وتوقف
وهذا لا ينكره الكعبي فقد التقت المذاهب وعاد الخلاف إلى لفظ والله أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ب-ر (khabara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Reportage conveying information from a source; khabar is that which is transmitted and received as news.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl, khabar is the vehicle of testimony (shahādah) and grounds epistemic obligation; mutawātir is that which reaches the degree of certainty through mass transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of actual conveyance; metaphorical (majāz) when used for mere hearsay without binding force.
- Root: ض-ر-ر (ḍarra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Harm, necessity, compulsion; ḍarūrī is that which imposes itself without choice.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī) is that which the mind grasps without acquisition or deliberation, as opposed to naẓarī (theoretical).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical compulsion; metaphorical for epistemic immediacy—knowledge that overwhelms the soul like an unavoidable force.
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (naẓara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Looking, examining, deliberating; naẓar is the act of intellectual scrutiny.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Theoretical knowledge (ʿilm naẓarī) is that attained through reflection and inference, contrasted with ḍarūrī.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for visual sight; metaphorical for rational consideration—the "gaze" of the mind upon evidence.
- Root: ق-ر-ن (qarana)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Joining, coupling; qarīnah is that which is joined to something else and indicates it.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In epistemology, qarāʾin (indications) are the circumstantial evidences that render a report truthful and cut off the possibility of falsehood.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for physical conjunction; metaphorical for evidential linkage—the sign that accompanies and reveals.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs repeated conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-qad...) and exceptive phrases (illā bi-al-tawātur) to structure dialectical refutation, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis for logical force.
chapters.translation:
I say: The Sumaniyyah have denied that the mutawātir report yields knowledge. So we say to them: If you doubt that there exists in the world a city called Baghdad, then you have committed sheer denial. But if you acknowledge it, then neither have you conversed with that city nor have you seen it—so you have only come to know it through tawātur. How could it be otherwise? For were it not for tawātur, a man would not be able to distinguish his own mother from all the other women of the world.

And if al-Kaʿbī acknowledges the principle of knowledge but claims that it is theoretical (naẓarī), then it is said: We observe that children come to know what the mutawātir number reports to them, without having prepared themselves for reflection or for grasping intelligibles through deliberation. Then it is said to them: Is this "reflection" that led you to know that there is a city called Baghdad anything other than the necessity (ḍarūrah) arising from the reports? For if they say: "We know that a multitude, by custom, does not conspire upon falsehood," we reply: And how did you come to know that? And why did you deem falsehood impossible from them, when it is possible in terms of conceptual permissibility? So we keep pressing them until they are unable to produce any theoretical path, and thus they are compelled to concede what we have maintained. Their ultimate recourse is that some minimal reflection is needed to recognize that these people do not lie. But if knowledge were rendered theoretical by virtue of such a thing, then it would equally be said that perceived objects are known by reflection, since they require opening the eyelids, focusing the gaze, removal of obstacles, and other such conditions.

Al-Kaʿbī argued against our companions by saying: Do you know that this knowledge is necessary (ḍarūrī) by necessity, or by reflection? If you know it by necessity, that is impossible, for we do not know it. And if you claim it is by reflection, then how can it be conceived that a thing is known necessarily, and then its being necessary is known by reflection? This knowledge is more fitting to be known necessarily—it resides in the very self of the knower regarding what the reporters have conveyed, and no perception attaches to it.

The Judge (al-Qāḍī) answered that this is mere improbability-mongering. For we know Baghdad's existence by necessity, and we know by reflection that it is necessary. The mode of reflection is that we invalidate every path by which the knowledge could conceivably be referred to something else. But this obliges him to say that, by reflection, one knows that the knowledge pertaining to the impossibility of contradictories is necessary only upon invalidating the reflective paths concerning it—and this has no basis.

Then it is said to the Judge: The knowledge pertaining to this knowledge—does it exceed it, or is it identical to it? If it does not exceed it, then there is no point in differentiating them. But if it exceeds it, then this is impossible, for it would entail either positing infinite sciences, or positing a knowledge that the knower does not know—and both are impossible.

The chosen position for us in this matter—and in it lies the answer to the question—is to say: What we hold is that knowledge is not received from the utterances of the reporters; rather, it is received from the indications (qarāʾin) that point to truthfulness and decisively sever the imagination of falsehood. For this reason, it is permissible for it to accompany a single speaker in isolation. Once this is established, we say—and al-Kaʿbī saw it—that the knowledge we have of the truthfulness of the reporters, and of the knowledge being necessary, is itself necessary. Indeed, we agree with him that knowledge is received from indications.

If by "reflection" he means its dependence upon discerning the indications through investigation and deliberation, then this is granted to him. And beyond the discernment of the indications, knowledge arises necessarily, without reflection or dependence. This al-Kaʿbī does not deny. Thus the schools converge, and the dispute reverts to a mere verbal difference. And God knows best.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الباب الثاني في العدد

وقد أجمع أصحابنا على اعتبار أصل العدد وإن اختلفوا في أقله وقد أحالوا
تلقي العلم الضروري من شخص واحد خلافا للنظام وتمسكوا بأن قول الواحد وإن
انضمت إليه القرائن فاعتماده الكذب في العرف ممكن لا استحالة فيه بخلاف
اعتماد الجمع العظيم بالتواطئ فإن ذلك يحيله العقل في اطراد العرف وعلمنا
به كعلمنا باستحالة إجماع أهل الدنيا في وقت واحد على أكل الزبيب وهذا لا
يطرد في الواحد وحققوا ذلك بأن الشرع تعبد القضاة ببناء الحكم على قول
الشهود وهم على طوال دهورهم لم يبنوا قط قضاياهم على علم ضروري مستفاد من
قول الشهود ولو تصور لوقع لا محالة تمسك النظام بأن قال إذ فرضنا رجلا من
أهل المروءة والسيرة المرضية
استمرت عادته على أن لا يخرج من داره إلا راكبا محفوفا بحشده تعالى وخدمه
لا يلتفت إلى أحد ولا يتكلم فرأيناه خرج من داره وقد مزق ثوبه حاسر الرأس
حافي الرجل يضرب صدره وينتف شعره رافعا عقيرته بالويل
مخبرا عن موت ابنه يعلم على الضرورة صدقه ولا نتمارى فيه فناكره فإن
أصحابنا وقالوا لعله أخبره كاذب أو اعتور ابنه سكتة فظنه ميتا وهذا مزيف
والمختار أن العلم قد يستفاد من القرائن المنضمة إلى قول واحد كما فرضناه
نعم زل النظام حيث قال يتلقى العلم من قوله وما ذكروه من السكتة وتوهمه
يرتفع بإخباره عن الدفن وذلك ممكن تقديره وما ذكروه من عدم قطع القضاة بقول
شاهد قط تحكم على الغيب
مسألة اختلف المعتبرون في  أقل عدد التواتر فقال القاضي أقطع أن الأربعة
ليسوا عدد التواتر وتردد في الخمسة لأن الشرع رقى الشهادة إلى الأربعة ولم
يكلف إلا غلبة الظن وقال ملقى مجلس أبي الهذيل عبد الرحمن الخمسة اقل عدد
التواتر من غير تردد وقال قائلون أقله عشرون تلقيا من قوله تعالى إن يكن
منكم عشرون صابرون وقال آخرون أربعون تلقيا من قوله تعالى حسبك الله ومن
اتبعك من المؤمنين وقد كانوا أربعين
وقيل أقله سبعون تلقيا من قوله تعالى واختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا
لميقاتنا وقال آخرون ثلاثمائة وثلاثة عشر وهو عدد المحاربين يوم بدر إذ بهم
استقر الدين وظهر وهذه أعداد يضرب البعض منها بالبعض ونقول العقل لم يهد
إلى التقدير وهذه الآيات لا تناسب الغرض والحكم بتقدير محال فإن قيل كأنكم
جهلتم أقل العدد قلنا هذا مرتبط بالعرف والقرائن فلا ضبط لها وهي مختلفة
باختلاف أحوال المخبرين والمخبر عنه فيجب على كل عاقل أن يضرب عن التقدير
فيه إذ العرف لا ينضبط نعم نشير إلى تزاحم شرائط الخبر فنقول إذا بلغوا
مبلغا في العدد يبعد منهم في العرف التواطؤ على الكذب في مثل ما أخبروا عنه
وعلم على القطع خروجهم عن ضبط ضابط وإيالة ذي إيالة لأجل مصلحة علم على
القطع الصدق وهذا قد يحصل بقول الواحد
وقد لا يحصل بقول عسكر عظيم إذ توهم انسلاكهم عمر تحت سياسة سايس وذهبت
الرافضة إلى أن العلم متلقى من قول الإمام المعصوم إلا أنه مشتبه بالمخبرين
النبي ولو انفرد وتعين لعلم على الضرورة صدقه وهذا محال إذ عصمته لم
يعلموها بالضرورة ولا يثر على عصمة الأنبياء ولم
يعرف صدقهم بالضرورة كيف وقد أخبر علي كرم الله وجهه في زمانه عن أمور
واختلفوا في صدقه وهو معصوم عندهم

### | الباب الثالث في شرائط التواتر

قال علماء الأصول شرطه استواء الطرفين والواسطة والحديث المتواتر عن رسول
الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في عصر الصحابة ينبغي أن يتواتر عنهم في العصر
الثاني فلو نقل الآحاد كونه متواترا لم  يكف وهذا خطأ فإن خبر الواحد ليس له
طرف وواسطة وكل من ينقل عنه قول وإن كان راويا فهو خبر في نفسه ولا بد من
التواتر فيه فهذه أخبار لا بد من تواتر كل واحد منها والشرط الذي لا بد منه
لتحصيل العلم أن يستند علم المخبرين إلى الحس والضرورة فأما ما علموه
بالنظر كحدث العالم وغيره لا يعلم صدقهم فيه وإن بلغوا عدد التواتر
فإن قال قائل ما سببه والعلوم عندكم كلها ضرورية فأي فرق بين الإدراك
ببصيرة العقل وبين الإدراك بالبصر
قلنا العرف فارق بينهما فإن العلم لا يحصل بحدث العالم بسبب الخبر بخلاف
المحسوسات فلعل السبب فيه أن المعتقد لحدث العالم لم يميز نفسه عن العالم
به وكل يظن أنه عالم وهو معتقد مخمن ولا قرينة تميزه وما من مخبر إلا
ويتصور كونه معتقدا وهو يظن أنه عالم وعلى هذا شأن النظريات جميعا دون
المحسوسات قال الأستاذ أبو اسحق الخبر ينقسم إلى متواتر ومستفيض وآحاد
فالمستفيض ما اشتهر فيما بين أئمة الحديث وذلك يورث العلم كالتواتر وليس
الأمر كذلك فإن المستفيض إذا لم يتواتر تصور فيه التواطؤ والغلط إذ العدل
لا يستحيل منه الكذب

- Root: ع-د-د (ʿadad)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Enumeration, counting, numerical quantity; the root denotes the act of reckoning discrete units.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, ʿadad signifies the stipulated numerical threshold for epistemic certainty in transmission (tawātur).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally here as a technical term for a fixed count, not metaphorically.
- Root: ت-و-ا-ت-ر (tawātur)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Succession, following one after another without interruption.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for a report transmitted by a multitude whose agreement on falsehood is rationally impossible, yielding necessary knowledge (ʿilm ḍarūrī).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of consecutive succession; metaphorical extension to epistemic certainty through collective transmission.
- Root: ق-ر-ء-ن (qarāʾin)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Indications, contextual evidence, accompanying circumstances.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In epistemology, circumstantial indicators that, when conjoined with a single report, may generate certainty.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: ropes binding something; metaphorical: evidential ties that bind a report to truth.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (e.g., "if we suppose... then we see...") and exceptions ("except that...") requiring careful parsing of protasis and apodosis for accurate rendering.
chapters.translation:
I say: Our companions (aṣḥābunā) have unanimously affirmed the consideration of the principle of number [for tawātur], though they differed regarding its minimum. They deemed it impossible to receive necessary knowledge (al-ʿilm al-ḍarūrī) from a single person, contrary to al-Naẓẓām. They argued that the statement of one individual, even if conjoined with circumstantial indicators (qarāʾin), remains in customary practice susceptible to falsehood—there being no impossibility therein—unlike the reliance upon a great multitude [conspiring] in collusion, for reason deems that impossible in the continuity of custom. Our knowledge of this is like our knowledge of the impossibility of all the people of the world agreeing at one time to eat raisins. And this [impossibility] does not hold for the single individual. They further verified this by [noting] that the Law (al-sharʿ) has obligated judges to base their rulings on the testimony of witnesses, yet throughout their long ages they have never once based their judgments on necessary knowledge derived from the testimony of witnesses; had such [certainty] been conceivable, it would inevitably have occurred.

Al-Naẓẓām countered, saying: Suppose we posit a man of probity (murūʾah) and commendable conduct, whose habit has continued such that he never leaves his house except mounted, surrounded by his retinue and servants, not looking at anyone, nor speaking. Then we see him emerge from his house with his garment torn, bare-headed, barefoot, striking his chest, pulling out his hair, raising his voice in lamentation, informing [us] of the death of his son. We would know with necessity his truthfulness and would not doubt it. We refuted him, saying: Perhaps he was informed falsely, or his son was struck by a seizure and he supposed him dead. But this [refutation] is weak.

The correct position (al-mukhtār) is that knowledge may indeed be derived from circumstantial indicators conjoined to the statement of a single person, as in the case we have posited. Yes, al-Naẓẓām erred where he claimed that knowledge is received from his [mere] statement [per se]. And what they mentioned regarding the seizure and his supposition [of death] is removed by his informing [us] of the burial, and that [scenario] is possible to conceive. As for their claim that judges never decide with certainty upon the word of a single witness—that is a judgment upon the unseen [i.e., an unwarranted generalization].

**Issue**: The [scholars] who considered [this matter] differed regarding the minimum number of tawātur. Al-Qāḍī [Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī] said: I am certain that four is not the number of tawātur, and he hesitated regarding five, because the Law elevated testimony to four [witnesses] and required only predominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) [thereby]. And the one who succeeded the council of Abū al-Hudhayl, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, said: Five is the minimum number of tawātur without hesitation. Some said: Its minimum is twenty, derived from His saying {«If there be among you twenty steadfast, they shall overcome two hundred»} (Q 8:65). Others said: Forty, derived from His saying {«Sufficient for you is Allah and those who follow you among the believers»} (Q 8:64), and they were forty. And it was said: Its minimum is seventy, derived from His saying {«And Moses chose seventy men from his people for Our appointment»} (Q 7:155). And others said: Three hundred and thirteen, which is the number of the fighters at Badr, for through them the religion was established and became manifest. These are numbers, some of which strike against others.

I say: Reason has not guided [us] to a fixed determination, and these verses do not correspond to the purpose [at hand]. The judgment of a specific number is impossible. If it is said: It seems you have ignored the minimum number, I say: This is tied to custom (al-ʿurf) and circumstantial indicators, which admit of no precise regulation; they vary according to the differing conditions of the reporters and the reported matter. Thus it is incumbent upon every rational person to refrain from determining it, since custom cannot be delimited. Yes, we may indicate the accumulation of the conditions of the report, saying: When [the reporters] reach a number such that, in customary practice, collusion upon falsehood is improbable from them regarding the like of what they report, and it is known with certainty that they have escaped the control of any controller and the governance of any governor for the sake of some interest—then truthfulness is known with certainty. And this may be attained by the statement of a single person, and it may not be attained by the statement of a vast army, when one conceives of their being drawn along under the policy of a single director.

The Rāfiḍah went so far as to hold that knowledge is received from the statement of the infallible Imam (al-imām al-maʿṣūm), except that he is likened to the reporters [of the Prophet]. Had the Prophet been alone and specified, his truthfulness would be known by necessity. But this is impossible, for his infallibility (ʿiṣmah) is not known by them through necessity, nor does it yield evidence for the infallibility of the prophets, nor is their truthfulness known by necessity. How [could it be], when ʿAlī—may Allah honor his face—in his own time reported matters, and they differed regarding his truthfulness, while he is infallible in their view?

### | The Third Chapter on the Conditions of Tawātur

The scholars of legal theory (uṣūl) said: Its condition is the equivalence of the two ends and the middle [i.e., all generations]. A ḥadīth transmitted by tawātur from the Messenger of Allah—peace be upon him—in the era of the Companions must be transmitted by tawātur from them in the second era. If a solitary report (khabar al-āḥād) claimed that it was mutawātir, that would not suffice. But this is an error, for a solitary report has no [distinct] end and middle; rather, everyone from whom a statement is transmitted—even if he is a transmitter—[his report] is itself a report, and tawātur is required in it. Thus these are reports, and each one of them must itself be mutawātir.

The condition indispensable for the attainment of knowledge is that the knowledge of the reporters be grounded in sense-perception (al-ḥiss) and necessity (al-ḍarūrah). As for what they know through rational reflection (al-naẓar)—such as the temporal origination of the world (ḥudūth al-ʿālam) and the like—their truthfulness therein is not known [through their report], even if they reach the number of tawātur.

If someone says: What is the cause of this? For all knowledges in your view are necessary—so what difference is there between perception by the insight of the intellect and perception by sight? I say: Custom (al-ʿurf) differentiates between them, for knowledge of the origination of the world is not attained through [mere] report, unlike sense-perceived matters. Perhaps the cause therein is that the one who believes in the origination of the world has not distinguished himself from the one who knows it; each supposes he is knowing while he is merely conjecturing (mukhammim), and no indicator distinguishes him. And there is no reporter but that it is conceivable he is merely a conjecturer while supposing himself knowing. And such is the case with all theoretical matters (al-naẓariyyāt), unlike sense-perceived matters.

Al-Ustādh Abū Isḥāq [al-Isfarāyīnī] said: The report is divided into mutawātir, mustafīḍ (widely circulated), and āḥād (solitary). The mustafīḍ is that which is famous among the imams of ḥadīth, and it yields knowledge like tawātur. But the matter is not so, for the mustafīḍ, if it has not reached tawātur, collusion and error are conceivable in it, since falsehood is not impossible from the just [transmitter].

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الباب الرابع في تقسيم الآحاد

قال علماء الأصول الآحاد ينقسم إلى ما يعلم صدقه وإلى ما يعلم كذبه وإلى
ما يتردد فيه أما ما يعلم صدقه ينقسم إلى ما يعلم بضرورة العقل كإخبار
المخبر عن استحالة اجتماع المتضادين وإلى ما يعلم بنظر العقل كإخبار المخبر
عن حدث العالم وإلى ما يعلم بالسمع كإخبار من قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم هو صادق
وإخبار الرسول عليه السلام عن الصراط والجنة والنار قالوا ومن هذا القسم
خبر الواحد إذا عمل بموجبه أهل الإجماع وأما ما يعلم كذبه فينقسم إلى هذه
الأقسام وهو الإخبار عن عكس هذه الأمور
وهذا وإن كان صحيحا فلا فائدة له في كتاب الأخبار فإن غرض الكتاب بيان ما
يتلقى علمه من الخبر وهذه الأمور معلومة لا من الخبر وما ذكروه  من انعقاد
الإجماع على العمل وكونه دليلا على صدق خبر الواحد ليس كذلك فان قيل لا
تجتمع الأمة على الضلالة قلنا ما اجتمعوا على صدقه بل اجتمعوا على العمل به
فنقول العمل واجب ومستنده هذا الحديث المتردد بين الصدق والكذب والمختار في
التقسيم ان يقال الخبر المعلوم صدقه على القطع ما استجمع شرائط التوتر وذلك
لا ضابط له والمعلوم كذبه اقسام منها تحدي الرجل بالنبوة مع العجز عن اقامة
المعجزة يدل على كذبه إذ لو كان رسولا لأيد وإن بمعجزة
فإن تكليف الإتباع من دونه مما لا يطاق وهذا محال هذا إن قال انا نبيكم
فأما اذا ادعى بانه يوحى اليه في نفسه فيما يؤمر به وينهى عنه فلا يعلم
كذبه بذلك وكذلك اذا قال معجزتي ان الله تعالى ينطق هذا الحجر فنطق بتكديبه
فيعلم كذبه إذ لو كان صادقا لما اظهره على هذا الوجه بخلاف ما لو قال
معجزتي ان احي هذا الميت فأحياه فنطق بتكذيبه لانه ذو اختيار كسائر الخلق
والاعجاز في احيائه ومما يعلم كذب المخبر فيه انفراد الرجل بالاخبار عن
واقعة عظيمة تتوفر البواعث على نقلها وتواتر الخبر فيها كانفراد رجل واحد
بالاخبار
عن برزة الخليفة على هيئة خارقة للعادة على ملا من الناس في مفرق الطرق
ومزدحم الخلق فيعلم كذبه إذ لو كان لتوفرت الدواعي على نقله ولإستحال كما
انفراده به وسكوت الباقين عن نقله فإن قيل فلم اختلف الناس في النبي عليه
السلام انه دخل مكة صلحا او عنوة وقد كان في مزدحم الخلق وقد تمسكتم فيها
بأخبار الآحاد قلنا تواتر كونه صلى الله عليه وسلم شاكا في السلاح متهيئا
لاسباب الحرب وانما الخلاف في جريان امان لهم وذلك مما يخفي فلا يبعد
انفراده الآحاد به فإن قيل لم لم يتواتر قران رسول الله ص أو افراده في
الحج وقد كان احرم على الملأ من الناس قلنا لأن الميز بين الأفراد والقران
مما يخفى ولا يدركه إلا الخواص
فلا يبعد استبهامه هو فإن قيل  انشقاق القمر لم يتواتر
قلنا أنكره الحليمي لذلك واعتذر القاضي بأنها كانت آية ليلة أظهرت في جنح
الليل ولم يكن مع النبي ص إلا أشخاص معدودة في وقت استرسال ثوب الغفلة على
الناس فلذلك لم يتواتر فإن قيل الإقامة من شعائر الإسلام فهلا تواتر
الأفراد إذا كان واقعا
قال القاضي اقطع بأن بلالا كان يثني ويفرد فلم يطرد الإفراد على التجرد
دون التثنية فلذلك تعارضت الأخبار فإن قيل لم لم يتواتر التثنية والافراد
جميعا قلنا لضعف اعتناء الناس به فانه كان يخفض الصوت بها نهارا والمختار
في الجواب القطع بان الافراد كان متواترا في العصر الاول إلا ان النقلة
اضربوا عن نقله استغناء بالاستفاضة والاجماع من حيث الفعل وحيث انقرض العصر
احدث بعض التابعة التثنية ولم يبق ممن عاين عصر رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم سوى الآحاد ولا يبعد ان يتواتر خبر عظيم ثم تنحبس الدواعي على ممر
الايام وتندرس فقد تقررت هذه القاعدة واستمرت وعليه بنينا الرد على الروافض
حيث ادعوا نصا من الرسول على امامة علي كرم الله وجهه
فان الصحابة اشتوروا بعد وفاة الرسول عليه السلام واضطربو وسلم فيمن ينصب
له حتى اتفقوا على أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ولم ينقل احد عن الرسول عليه
الصلاة والسلام النص ولو كان لتوفرت الدواعي على ابدائه ونقله وكذلك اليهود
إذ نقلوا عن موسى عليه السلام انه خاتم النبيين قيل لهم تحدى رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم على اليهود وكانوا ينازعونه في بعثه ولم ينقل احد من
احبارهم ذلك ولو كان لتوفرت الدواعي على نقله وايضا فلا يمكنهم انكار معجزة
عيسى عليه السلام من احياء الموتى وغيره ولو صدقوا لما ظهرت المعجزة بعد
وأما المتردد فيه فجملة اخبار الآحاد وكل ما لم يستجمع شرط التواتر وأمكن
وقوعه ومن هذا القسم انفراد رجل واحد ينقل حالة لرجل عظيم اذا تخيلنا
استناد سكوت الباقين إلى سياسة واياله عنه ذي اياله إن هذا تمام الكلام في
هذا القسم والله اعلم

### | القسم  الثاني في إخبار الآحاد

وفيه خمسة ابواب
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ق-س-م (q-s-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Division, apportionment, distribution into parts
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Categorical partitioning of epistemic objects into mutually exclusive classes
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal here — actual logical division, not metaphorical
- Root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Report, news, information conveyed from one to another
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A statement (khabar) that admits of truth or falsehood; the epistemic vehicle for transmitted knowledge
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal — the report as a linguistic act; metaphorical extension to "report of the heart" (iʿtiqād) is excluded here
- Root: ت-و-ت-ر (t-w-t-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Succession, following one after another
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Technical term for a report transmitted by such a multitude that collusion on falsehood is impossible
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in the technical sense — the multiplicity itself is the operative cause of certainty
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — the protasis "if it is said..." (fa-in qīla) introduces an objection, and the apodosis "we say..." (qulnā) delivers the rebuttal; this dialectical structure governs the entire section.
chapters.translation:
I say: The scholars of legal theory (uṣūliyyūn) have stated that the isolated report (al-āḥād) divides into: that whose truth is known, that whose falsehood is known, and that which is subject to hesitation.

As for that whose truth is known, it divides into: that which is known by the necessity of the intellect (ḍarūrat al-ʿaql) — such as the reporter's informing about the impossibility of two contradictories coexisting; that which is known by the reflection of the intellect (naẓar al-ʿaql) — such as the reporter's informing about the temporal origination of the world (ḥudūth al-ʿālam); and that which is known by audition (al-samʿ) — such as the report of one who says: "The Messenger of God — may God's peace and blessings be upon him — is truthful," and the Messenger's — peace be upon him — informing about the Bridge (al-ṣirāṭ), Paradise, and the Fire.

They said: And belonging to this category is the isolated report (khabar al-wāḥid) when the people of consensus (ahl al-ijmāʿ) have acted upon its implication.

As for that whose falsehood is known, it divides into these same categories — namely, the reporting of the inverse of these matters.

And this, although correct, has no benefit in a book on reports (akhbār), for the purpose of the book is to elucidate that whose knowledge is received from the report, whereas these matters are known not from the report. And what they mentioned — regarding the formation of consensus upon acting upon it and its being evidence for the truthfulness of the isolated report — is not as they claim. For if it is said: "The community does not unite upon error," we say: They did not unite upon its truthfulness; rather, they united upon acting upon it. So we say: The action is obligatory, and its basis is this very report that is subject to hesitation between truth and falsehood.

The preferred view (al-mukhtār) in the division is to say: The report whose truth is known with certainty is that which has gathered all the conditions of tawātur — and there is no exhaustive criterion for that.

And that whose falsehood is known has several categories. Among them: a man's challenging (taḥaddī) with prophethood while being incapable of producing a miracle — this indicates his falsehood, for had he been a messenger, he would have been supported, even if by a miracle. For to obligate following him without that would be an unbearable burden (taklīf mā lā yuṭāq), and this is impossible. This applies if he says: "I am your prophet."

But if he claims that revelation comes to him inwardly (fī nafsihi) regarding what he is commanded and forbidden, his falsehood is not known by that. Likewise, if he says: "My miracle is that God — exalted — will make this stone speak," and it then speaks to declare him a liar, his falsehood is known — for had he been truthful, God would not have manifested it in that manner. This differs from his saying: "My miracle is that I revive this dead person," and he revives him, and then the revived one speaks to declare him a liar — for the revived one possesses free choice (ikhtiyār) like the rest of creation, and the miraculous aspect lies in his revival itself.

And among that by which the falsehood of the reporter is known: a single man's being alone in reporting a momentous event whose transmission motives (al-bawāʿith) would be strongly incited, and whose report would be expected to reach tawātur — such as a single man's being alone in reporting about the appearance of the Caliph in an extraordinary manner (hayʾa khāriqa lil-ʿāda) before a large assembly of people at a crossroads and amidst a thronging crowd. His falsehood is known, for had it occurred, the motives would have been incited to transmit it, and its being confined to him alone — with the rest remaining silent about transmitting it — would be impossible.

If it is said: Then why did the people differ concerning the Prophet — peace be upon him — as to whether he entered Mecca by treaty (ṣulḥan) or by force (ʿanwatan), given that it was amidst a thronging crowd, and you yourselves have relied therein upon isolated reports? We say: The tawātur established that he — peace be upon him — entered armed and prepared for the means of war; the disagreement is only concerning the occurrence of a safe-conduct (amān) granted to them — and that is something hidden, so it is not improbable that isolated individuals alone transmit it.

If it is said: Why was the Prophet's — God's peace be upon him — performance of the pilgrimage as an individual (ifrād) or as a qirān not transmitted by tawātur, given that he entered the state of iḥrām before a multitude of people? We say: Because the distinction between ifrād and qirān is something subtle that only the elite perceive, so its being obscure is not improbable.

If it is said: The splitting of the moon (inshiqāq al-qamar) was not transmitted by tawātur? We say: Al-Ḥalīmī denied it for that reason. And al-Qāḍī excused it by saying that it was a sign shown in the dead of night, and there were only a few persons with the Prophet — peace be upon him — at a time when the garment of heedlessness had been cast over the people; therefore it did not reach tawātur.

If it is said: The iqāma is among the public rites of Islam (shaʿāʾir al-islām) — why then was the ifrād not transmitted by tawātur if it actually occurred? Al-Qāḍī said: I affirm with certainty that Bilāl used to perform the iqāma sometimes with the dual form (tathniya) and sometimes with the single form (ifrād); the ifrād was not consistently maintained to the exclusion of the tathniya, and therefore the reports conflicted.

If it is said: Why were neither the tathniya nor the ifrād transmitted by tawātur? We say: Due to the weakness of people's attention to it, for he used to lower his voice with it during the day.

The preferred view in the answer is: The affirmation with certainty that the ifrād was transmitted by tawātur in the first generation — except that the transmitters refrained from transmitting it, deeming the widespread practice (al-istifāḍa) and consensus by way of actual conduct (min ḥaythu al-fiʿl) sufficient. And when that generation passed away, some of the Followers (tābiʿūn) introduced the tathniya, and none remained of those who had witnessed the era of the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — save isolated individuals. And it is not improbable that a momentous report reaches tawātur, then the motives become arrested with the passage of days and it becomes effaced.

This principle has been established and has continued, and upon it we have based our refutation of the Rāfiḍa (Shīʿa) where they claimed an explicit designation (naṣṣ) from the Messenger concerning the imāmate of ʿAlī — may God honor his face. For the Companions deliberated after the death of the Messenger — peace be upon him — and were agitated and consulted concerning whom to install, until they agreed upon Abū Bakr — may God be pleased with him — and no one transmitted from the Messenger — peace and prayer be upon him — any explicit designation. Had it existed, the motives would have been incited to its disclosure and transmission.

And likewise the Jews, for they transmitted from Moses — peace be upon him — that he was the seal of the prophets. It was said to them: The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — challenged the Jews while they were disputing with him concerning his mission, and none of their rabbis transmitted that. Had it existed, the motives would have been incited to its transmission. Moreover, they cannot deny the miracle of Jesus — peace be upon him — of reviving the dead and other things; had they been truthful, the miracle would not have appeared after him.

As for that which is subject to hesitation (al-mutaraddad fīhi): it is the totality of isolated reports (akhbār al-āḥād) — everything that has not gathered the conditions of tawātur and whose occurrence is possible. And belonging to this category is a single man's being alone in transmitting a state of a great man, when we conceive that the silence of the rest is attributable to political prudence (siyāsa) and to one in authority shielding him.

This is the completion of the discourse on this section. And God knows best.

### | The Second Section on the Reports of Isolated Individuals (Akhbār al-Āḥād)

It contains five chapters.

### | الباب الأول في اثبات كون المخبر الواحد مفيدا للعمل

وذهب بعض المحدثين إلى انه يفيد العلم وهذا محال إذ لا يجب صدقه عقلا ولا
نقلا واذا جاز كذبه فلا علم بالصدق وكيف وما من شخص إلا ويتصور ان يرجع عما
ينقله وقد عهد مثله وبعد فلو تعارض نقل عدلين فليت شعري يجعل العلم بهما
على التناقض او بأحدهما ولا تمييز ولا ترجيح
فإن قيل لو لم يوجب العلم لما اوجب العمل قلنا عن هذا صار الروافض إلى
انه لا يعمل بأخبار الآحاد ونحن نبطل الان مذهبهم فنقول ان أحلتم وقوعه
وزعمتم انه لا يتصور فوجه تصوره ان يقول السيد لغلامه اعمل بما ينتهي اليك
من امري على لسان الآحاد وان احالوا لاستقباح او لاستصلاح فنحن لا نساعدهم
في ذلك ثم قلب كل خيال يبدونه في اثبات القبح ونقيض الصلاح ممكن عليهم وان
تلقوا منعه من السمع فلا بد من نقله قالوا ودليله قوله تعالى إن بعض الظن
إثم قلنا خصص البعض وليس هذا منه ودليله بناء القاضي قضاءه على ظن صدق
الشهود بالإجماع فإن قيل لا نعلم وجوب العمل به بضرورة العقل ولا يدل عليه
دليل فلا يعمل به
قلنا دليله امران قاطعان أحدهما علمنا بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
يبعث ولاته ورسله إلى البلاد ويفرقهم في الأقطار وهم آحاد وكان يضم اليهم
الصحائف ويأمر بإتباعه الحاضر والبادي ولو توقفوا إلى التواتر لحزت رقابهم
المسلك الثاني علمنا بان الصحابة رضي الله عنهم اجمعين ان ارتبكوا إلا في
واقعة فنقل اليهم الصديق رضي الله عنه قولا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه
وسلم على انفراده اتبعوه وقولهم انه لا يورث العلم يبطل بالشهادة والله
أعلم
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ب-ر (khabara)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "to inform" or "to report" — the conveyance of a statement from one party to another, whether true or false in itself.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, khabar denotes a report whose epistemic value is assessed by its chain (sanad) and content (matn); it stands in contrast to ʿilm (certain knowledge) and is tied to ẓann (conjecture) when from a single source.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage refers to actual informing; metaphorical (majāz) usage extends to any transmitted assertion, including those whose veracity is not guaranteed.
- Root: ع-م-ل (ʿamila)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To act, to perform, to do — physical or practical engagement with a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, ʿamal signifies the practical compliance (imtithāl) required by a legal command, distinct from theoretical assent (taṣdīq).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical exertion; metaphorical: the obligation to follow a directive in practice, even absent certainty.
- Root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓanna)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To conjecture, to hold an opinion without full certainty; also to suspect.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ẓann is the middle epistemic state between ʿilm (certainty) and shakk (doubt); in legal methodology, it is the basis for action when certainty is unattainable.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: a belief with preponderance (tarjīḥ) but not certainty; metaphorical: in the Quranic verse cited, it denotes sinful suspicion, a specific subset.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs "لو" (if) for hypothetical impossibility and "إلا" (except) for exclusion, requiring precise parsing to distinguish universal from particular claims, as in "إن بعض الظن إثم" (indeed some conjecture is sin) where "بعض" restricts the scope.
chapters.translation:
I say: Some of the traditionists (al-muḥaddithūn) have held that the single reporter's report yields certain knowledge (al-ʿilm). But this is impossible, for neither reason nor revelation necessitates its truthfulness. And if its falsehood is possible, then there is no knowledge of its truth. How could there be, when there is no person but that it is conceivable he might retract what he reports — and indeed the like of this has been witnessed? Moreover, if two reports from two just narrators were to conflict, then I wonder: would knowledge be attached to both of them, which is a contradiction, or to one of them, when there is no distinguishing mark (tamyīz) nor preponderating factor (tarjīḥ)?

If it is said: "If it did not necessitate knowledge, it would not necessitate action," we reply: It is on account of this that the Rāfiḍah have come to hold that one must not act upon reports of single narrators (akhbār al-āḥād). And we now refute their doctrine, saying: If you deem its occurrence impossible and claim it is inconceivable, then the manner of its conceivability is this — that the master says to his slave: "Act upon whatever of my command reaches you through the tongue of single reporters." And if they deem it impossible on grounds of repugnance (istiqbāḥ) or of seeking what is salutary (istiṣlāḥ), then we do not assist them in that. Then every fancy they put forth in affirming repugnance or the contrary of the salutary can be turned back upon them. And if they receive its prohibition from revelation, then it must be transmitted — and they have no transmission for it.

They said: Its proof is the saying of God the Exalted: {«إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ»} ("Indeed, some conjecture is sin"). We reply: He specified "some" (al-baʿḍ), and this [report] is not of that kind. And its proof is that the judge builds his judgment upon the conjecture of the truthfulness of witnesses, by consensus (ijmāʿ).

If it is said: "We do not know the obligation to act upon it by necessity of reason, nor does any proof indicate it, so we do not act upon it," we reply: Its proof is two decisive matters (amrān qāṭiʿān). The first: We know that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) dispatched his governors and messengers to the lands and dispersed them across the regions, and they were single individuals (āḥād). He attached to them written documents (ṣuḥuf) and commanded both the present and the distant to follow them. Had they waited for mass transmission (tawātur), their necks would have been severed.

The second path: We know that the Companions (may God be pleased with them all) — even if they differed, except in one incident — when al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) conveyed to them a saying from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in his sole capacity, they followed it. And their claim that it does not yield knowledge is refuted by the case of testimony (al-shahādah). And God knows best.
