- Root: ن-ق-ح (n-q-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To refine, purify, or perfect something by removing defects; to sift thoroughly.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Intellectual refinement of a doctrinal matter, stripping it of ambiguities to reach certitude (yaqīn).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of cleansing; here used metaphorically (majāz) for dialectical polishing of a legal-theoretical position.
- Root: م-ص-ل-ح (m-ṣ-l-ḥ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: What is sound, upright, or beneficial; the opposite of corruption (fasād).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, a maṣlaḥah is that which secures a divine purpose (maqṣūd al-Shāriʿ) in preserving religion, life, intellect, lineage, and property.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally "setting aright"; technically, an interest not attested by a specific textual proof (naṣṣ) but consistent with the aims of the Law.
- Root: ط-ر-د (ṭ-r-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To be continuous, regular, or unbroken in course.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The property of a legal ratio (ʿillah) that applies uniformly across all cases without exception.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "running" or "flowing"; metaphorically, the consistent operation of a legal cause in all analogous instances.
- Root: ع-ك-س (ʿ-k-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reverse, invert, or turn something back.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The converse of a legal cause — i.e., if the cause is absent, the effect (ruling) is negated.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "turning upside down"; technically, the implication of a ruling's negation when its ratio is negated (ʿaks al-ʿillah).
- Root: ق-ص-د (q-ṣ-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To intend, aim, or direct oneself toward a goal.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The divine intention (qaṣd al-Shāriʿ) behind a ruling, discerned through textual indicators.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "straight path to a target"; here, the inferred legislative purpose from explicit texts.
- Root: ج-ر-ب (j-r-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To test, try, or experience; a scabby camel (ajrab) whose mange spreads.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In ʿUmar's dictum, a metaphor for the ruler's comprehensive responsibility over even the most trivial affairs.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "mangy camel"; metaphorical (majāz) for total custodial accountability.
- Root: ه-ذ-ر (h-dh-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To talk nonsense, babble, or speak excessively without restraint.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Frivolous speech that the Law deters but does not punish with fixed penalties (ḥudūd).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "idle chatter"; used to illustrate the Companions' refusal to punish mere suspicion.
- Root: س-د-د (s-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To plug, block, or close an opening; to set aright.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The principle of blocking pretexts (sadd al-dharāʾiʿ) that lead to prohibited ends.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "stopping a breach"; technically, averting means that facilitate corruption.
- Root: ر-م-ق (r-m-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The last breath of life; the remaining spark of vitality.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The minimal sustenance (sadd al-ramaq) that preserves life from imminent death.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal "final breath"; metaphorically, the bare subsistence level in necessity (ḍarūrah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-Sharṭ wa al-Istithnāʾ) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (in qīla... qulnā) and exceptive particles (illā, ghayr) to structure dialectical objections and responses, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis to preserve the logical force of each argument.
chapters.translation:
I say: We refine this doctrine by directing objections against it and then disentangling ourselves from them. Thus we state: Every meaning (maʿnā) that is suitable (munāsib) to a ruling, that runs consistently (muṭṭarid) through the rulings of the Sacred Law, that is not repelled by any definitively established principle (aṣl maqṭūʿ bihī) taking precedence over it from the Book, the Sunnah, or consensus (ijmāʿ) — such a meaning is to be adopted (maqūl bihī), even if no specific textual origin (aṣl muʿayyan) testifies to it. Then, its divisions cannot be encompassed, for no enumeration can contain them, nor can any definition delimit them. For it may happen that an unrestricted interest (maṣlaḥah mursalah) yields a universal matter (amr kullī) in a general way, or it may yield a particular ruling (ḥukm juzʾī) in a specific case. It may also be elicited from the converse of a cause (ʿaks al-ʿillah), for in our view the converse of causes negates the ruling, just as their consistent application (ṭard) suggests it, as will come later. And it may be understood from the intention of the Lawgiver (qaṣd al-Shāriʿ), as when he, peace be upon him, said: «لا نكاح إلا بولي وشهود» ("No marriage except with a guardian and witnesses") — from which the requirement of probity (ʿadālah) is understood, because his intention is the establishment [of the marriage]. And so on, to the rest of its divisions.

If it is said: What is the difference between your doctrine and that of Mālik, may God be pleased with him, whose pursuit of interests (maṣāliḥ) led him to killing in discretionary punishment (taʿzīr), beating on mere suspicion (tuhmah), killing a third of the community to reform its two-thirds, and confiscating the wealth of the rich when [he deemed it] an interest? And what prevented you from following these [practices], given that need may arise for discretionary punishment based on suspicion? For wealth is protected (maḥqūnah), the thief does not confess, and proving [theft] through circumstantial evidence (bayyinah) is difficult — there is no way to expose it except through beating, and this is a manifest interest. And so on, beyond what we have mentioned.

We say: The difference between us is that we have attended to a great principle (aṣl ʿaẓīm) to which Mālik paid no heed — namely, that we give precedence to the Companions (al-ṣaḥābah) over the dictates of interest. Every interest that we know with certainty (qaṭʿan) occurred during the era of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and [yet] they refrained from adjudicating according to its requirement — that [interest] is abandoned. And we know with certainty that eras are never free of theft, and this was frequent in the Companions' era, yet they never administered discretionary punishment on suspicion, nor did they ever cut off a tongue for idle chatter (hadhar), despite the abundance of babblers. Nor did they confiscate the wealth of any rich person, despite the abundance of the rich and the pressing of needs. Thus, whatever they refrained from, we refrain from. And Mālik did not attend to this principle.

If it is said: It is narrated that ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, confiscated from Khālid and ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ half of their wealth, and said to a man who extended his hand to his beard to remove a speck of dust from it: "Son of the one who grew it! If you do not remove [your hand], I shall sever your hand." Yet you do not mandate cutting the hand in such a case, nor confiscation — and he did both.

We say: We know that had he not removed what he removed, he would not have cut his hand. Rather, he mentioned this as intimidation (tahwīl) and deterrence (takhwīf), and to magnify the awe (haybah) of the imamate, lest [people] become overly familiar and his dignity weaken in their breasts. As for the confiscation of Khālid's wealth, it does not indicate the permissibility of confiscation absolutely, because ʿUmar was most knowledgeable of their circumstances. He would spy on [the people] by day and patrol by night, and he had appointed Khālid as governor over some lands, upon which [Khālid] amassed great wealth. Perhaps ʿUmar had learned of a hidden matter that necessitated that [confiscation]. And that [kind of action] is permissible for one like him — he who used to say: "Were I to leave a mangy camel (jarbāʾ) on the bank of a valley, I would be answerable for it on the Day of Judgment." Thus, this should not be taken as a pretext (dharīʿah) for confiscating the wealth of the rich absolutely. How [could it be], when the rich multiplied in the era of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and this [confiscation] never occurred with anyone other than those two? And adhering to this definitive [principle] is more appropriate.

If it is said: The prescribed limit for theft (ḥadd al-sariqah) was legislated for deterrence (zajr). A man may steal less than a quarter of a dīnār by a single grain, and thus needs deterrence. Why, then, do you not deter him?

We say: The determinations (taqdīrāt) of the Sacred Law are to be followed; they are not to be altered. And the hem of prevention (sadd) is dragged over the details of cases. This is among the greatest interests, for pursuing the particulars of circumstances is impossible. Thus we followed the determination in this matter and did not analogize (qisnā).

If it is said: How is it that ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, analogized in the prescribed limit for drinking (ḥadd al-shurb), which is determined [by the Law]? For he said: "Whoever drinks becomes intoxicated; whoever becomes intoxicated raves; whoever raves slanders (iftarā). Thus I see that I should impose upon him the prescribed limit of the slanderer (ḥadd al-muftarī)" — and he raised the limit to eighty [lashes] for the sake of interests.

We say: The limit for drinking was not determined by the Lawgiver. Rather, he, peace be upon him, used to order beating with sandals and the ends of sleeves. Abū Bakr, may God be pleased with him, determined it as forty, and that was within the domain of ijtihād. It is for this reason that ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, said: "I never imposed a prescribed limit upon a man who died, and found in myself [any remorse], except the limit for drinking — for it is something we innovated after the Messenger of God, peace be upon him."

If it is said: Has it not been narrated that ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, used to split the fingers of boys for the sake of an interest — and you have abandoned this interest?

We say: This matter falls within the domain of ijtihād, for a slight splitting is close to beating in terms of intimidation, and boys are beaten for theft. We saw a more apparent meaning (maʿnā azhar) than it, and therefore we abandoned it.

If it is said: If an unprecedented case (wāqiʿah) arose, with no parallel in the era of the early [generations], and a fresh interest (maṣlaḥah ḥadīthah) presented itself that no principle repels, but it is novel — would you follow it?

We say: Yes. And for this reason we say: If we suppose that the wealth of the entire world were to become forbidden (muḥarram) in its entirety — due to the abundance of corrupt transactions, the confusion of usurped property with other property, and the difficulty of reaching pure lawful [sustenance] — and [the means of livelihood] had been lifted, then what is our position? We would permit every needy person to take the amount sufficient for his sustenance (kifāyah) from any wealth, because prohibiting consumption would lead to death, while permitting luxurious enjoyment would be indulgence in what is forbidden. And restricting him to the amount that merely sustains life (sadd al-ramaq) would turn people away from their religious and worldly transactions, leading to the corruption of the world and the ruin of its inhabitants. For they would remain in their state, on the brink of death, unable to attend to their crafts and occupations — and the Sacred Law would certainly not be pleased with such a state. Thus, it would be permitted for every rich person to take from his wealth the amount of his sufficiency, without luxury and without restricting himself to bare subsistence; and it would be permitted for every poor person to take from surplus wealth beyond that amount, likewise. This is attested by a principle (qāʿidah): when a single person is compelled (uḍṭurra) to another's food or to carrion (maytah), he is permitted the amount that sustains him, in preservation of the soul. So the preservation of souls is more fitting and more worthy.

Likewise, we say regarding one who is fortified by his power (shawkah), who has overcome the people, and is obeyed among them — while the age is devoid of anyone who combines the conditions of the imamate whose command is executed — [we say] that [his authority is valid], because [denying it] would lead to great corruption were we not to affirm it.

chapters.title_en: Section 51: On Istishāb (Presumption of Continuity), Istihsān (Juridical Preference), and Qiyās al-Shabah (Analogical Reasoning by Resemblance)
chapters.arabic_text:
### | الباب الخامس في الاستصحاب

ليس من الاستصحاب المقول به استدامة الحكم مع تبدل الصورة كما استصحب أبو
حنيفة رضي الله عنه وجوب الحقتين في المائة والعشرين فيه إذ زادت واحدة لأن
الصورة قد تبدلت فلا بد من دليل على النفي
وكذلك لو سئل عن النكاح بلا ولي مثلا فقال الأبضاع أصلها على التحريم فهو
مستصحب إلى أن يلوح دليل في الإباحة لأنه مطالب بإقامة الدليل على فساد
العقد المعقود بشرائطه وأن الولي شرط فيه فالاستصحاب لا يغني وإنما
الاستصحاب الصحيح ما نذكره في منع وجوب الوتر والأضحية بعد سبر مدارك
الوجوب وإبطال كل قياس يذكرونه
فبعد ذلك نقول الحال لم تتبدل ولا مأخذ للوجوب وبراءة الذمة يشهد لها
العقل والسمع فيستصحب هذا الأصل المستقر فلابد من دليل وقد بطل مأخذ الوجوب
وبالله التوفيق

### | الباب السادس في الاستحسان

قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه من استحسن فقد شرع
ولا بد أولا من بيان حقيقة الاستحسان وقد قال قائلون من أصحاب ابي حنيفة
رضي الله عنه الاستحسان مذهب لا دليل عليه وهذا كفر ممن قاله وممن يجوز
التمسك به ولا حاجة فيه  إلى دليل وقال قائلون هو معنى خفي تضيق العبارة عنه
وهذا أيضا هوس فإن معاني الشارع إذا لاحت في العقول انطلقت الألسن بالتعبير
عنها فما لا عبارة عنه لا يعقل والصحيح في ضبط الاستحسان ما ذكره الكرخي
وقد قسمه أربعة أقسام منها اتباع الحديث وترك القياس كما فعلوا في مسألة
القهقهة ونبيذ التمر ومنها اتباع قول الصحابي على خلاف القياس كما قاله في
تقدير أجرة
رد العبد الآبق بأربعين اتباعا لابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وتقدير ما يحط
عن قيمة العبد إذا ساوى دية الحر أو زاد بعشر اتباعا لابن مسعود ومنها
اتباع عادات الناس وما يطرد به عرفهم كمصيرهم إلى أن المعطاة صحيحة لأن
الاعصار لا تنفك عنه ويغلب على الظن جريانه في عصر الرسول ومنها اتباع معنى
خفي هو اخص بالمقصود وامس له من المعنى الجلي فنقول أما اتباع الخبر تقديما
له على القياس فواجب عندنا ابو حنيفة لم يف به في مسألة المصارة والعرايا
وخيار المتبايعين ولم يستحسن اتباع هذه الاحاديث مع اتفاق ائمة الحديث على
صحتها وضعف حديث القهقة واما قول الصحابي اذا خالف القياس فهو متبع عندنا
وخالفه ابو حنفية في مسألة تغليظ الدية مع ما نقل فيه عن الصحابة وتقدير
ابن عباس أجرة رد الأبق بأربعين يحتمل ان يكون بحكم مصالحة او مصلحة
اقتضاها نزاع في تلك الحالة
وقول ابن مسعود في قيمة العبد يلتفت على قياس الذمية ومراعاتها وتقدير
الحط ملاحظة لنصاب السرقة فإنه عظيم في الشرع يظهر التفاوت فيه فلذلك لم
نتبعه وأما دعواه بأن عمل الناس متبع في المعاطاة لأن الأعصار فيه لا
تتفاوت تحكم فإنا نعلم ان العقود الفاسدة والربويات في عصرنا أكثر منه في
إبتداء الإسلام وصفوته وعوام الناس لا مبالاة بأجماعهم حتى يتمسك بعملهم
واما اتباع المعنى الخفي اذا كان اخص فهو متبع لان الجلي الذي لا يمس
المقصود باطل معه او مقدم عليه ولكن أبا حنيفة لم يف بموجبه حتى أتى
بالعجائب والآيات وسماه استحسانا فقال يجب  الحد على من شهد عليه اربعة
بالزنا في اربع زوايا كل واحد منهم يشهد عليه في زاوية وقال لعله كان يزحف
في زنية واحدة في الزوايا واي استحسان في سفك دم مسلم بمثل هذا الخيال مع
انه لو خصص كل
شهادة بزمان وتقاربت الازمنة واحتمل استدامة الزنا في مثلها لا حد وذلك
اغلب في العرف من تخيل سحبها في زوايا البيت بزنا واحد فهذا ونحوه من
الاستحسانات الباطلة وما استند إلى مأخذ مما ذكرناه صحيح فهو مقول به والله
اعلم بالصواب

### | الباب السابع في ذكر قياس الشبه وفيه فصلان
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ص-ح-ب (Ṣ-Ḥ-B)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Companionship, adherence, and the state of being inseparably attached to something; istishāb denotes the continuation of a prior state.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, it signifies the presumption of the persistence of an established legal status (ḥāl) until a countervailing evidence (dalīl) overturns it — a principle rooted in the Quranic norm of non-burdening beyond capacity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) in the sense of 'keeping company with' a ruling; metaphorical (majāz) when applied to the legal maxim 'certainty is not removed by doubt' (al-yaqīn lā yazūl bi-al-shakk).
- Root: ح-س-ن (Ḥ-S-N)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Beauty, goodness, and what the intellect or custom deems commendable; istihsān is 'deeming something good' in the absence of a clear textual proof.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A contested source of law — al-Shāfiʿī condemns it as 'legislating' (tashrīʿ) without divine warrant, while the Ḥanafīs defend it as a subtle preference for the stronger indicant (dalīl) over apparent analogy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Rhetorically, it is a metonymy (majāz mursal) for abandoning an evident qiyās in favor of a hidden but more purposive meaning (maʿnā khafī aqrab ilā al-maqṣūd).
- Root: ش-ب-ه (Sh-B-H)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity, and ambiguity; shabah is the middle ground between two conflicting analogical bases.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyās al-shabah applies when a case resembles two distinct origins (aṣlān) — the jurist must weigh which resemblance is more appropriate to the divine purpose (munāsabah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for visual similarity; metaphorical for juridical attribution of a branch (farʿ) to the origin whose attributes (awṣāf) most closely align with the ratio legis (ʿillah).
- Sībawayh Rule: Taqdīr al-ʿāmil (Ellipsis of the Governing Operator) — In the phrase "ليس من الاستصحاب المقول به استدامة الحكم مع تبدل الصورة," the nominal predicate is governed by an implicit operator (mubtadaʾ maḥdhūf), requiring the reader to supply "المقصود" (the intended meaning) for syntactic completion.
chapters.translation:
I say: Know that the fifth chapter concerns istishāb (presumption of continuity). It is not part of the valid istishāb, as commonly claimed, to affirm the continuation of a ruling when the underlying case (ṣūrah) has changed — as Abū Ḥanīfah (may God be pleased with him) presumed the continued obligation of two shares (ḥaqqān) in a flock of one hundred and twenty sheep when it increased by one, for the case has indeed changed, and thus a proof (dalīl) is required to establish the negation [of the new obligation].

Similarly, if one were asked, for instance, about a marriage contracted without a guardian (walī), and he replied, 'The wombs (abḍāʿ) are originally upon prohibition,' this is a valid istishāb until evidence of permissibility (ibāḥah) appears — but he is still required to produce proof of the invalidity of the contract concluded with its conditions, and that the guardian is a condition therein. Thus, istishāb does not suffice [to establish invalidity]. Rather, the correct istishāb is what we shall mention regarding the denial of the obligation of the witr prayer and the sacrificial animal (uḍḥiyyah): after surveying all the indicants (madārik) of obligation and refuting every analogy (qiyās) they adduce, we then say: the case has not changed, there is no source for obligation, and the exoneration of the conscience (barāʾat al-dhimmah) is attested by both reason (ʿaql) and revelation (samʿ). Hence, this established principle is presumed to continue, and a proof is required [to overturn it] — yet the source of obligation has been nullified. And with God is success.

I say: The sixth chapter concerns istihsān (juridical preference). Al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him) said: 'Whoever practices istihsān has legislated (sharraʿa).' It is necessary first to clarify the reality (ḥaqīqah) of istihsān. Some of Abū Ḥanīfah's companions (may God be pleased with him) have said: 'Istihsān is a doctrine without proof (madhhab lā dalīl ʿalayhi)' — this is unbelief (kufr) on the part of the one who says it and the one who permits adherence to it without need for proof. Others said: 'It is a subtle meaning (maʿnā khafī) that language is too narrow to express' — this too is delusion (hawas), for when the meanings of the Lawgiver become manifest to intellects, tongues are unleashed to express them; what cannot be expressed cannot be comprehended.

The correct definition of istihsān is what al-Karkhī mentioned, for he divided it into four categories: (1) Following the hadith and abandoning analogy — as they did in the case of laughter in prayer (al-qahqahab) and the nabīdh of dates; (2) Following the statement of a Companion against analogy — as he said in estimating the reward for returning a runaway slave at forty [dirhams], following Ibn ʿAbbās (may God be pleased with them both), and estimating the reduction from the slave's value when it equals or exceeds the blood-money (diyah) of a free man by one-tenth, following Ibn Masʿūd; (3) Following the customs of people and what their prevailing practice (ʿurf) establishes — such as their ruling that the exchange transaction (muʿāṭāh) is valid, because the ages (aʿṣār) have never been free of it, and it is overwhelmingly probable (ghalabat al-ẓann) that it occurred in the Prophet's era; (4) Following a subtle meaning that is more specific to the intended purpose and more attached to it than the evident meaning (maʿnā jaliyy).

We say: As for following the report (khabar), giving it precedence over analogy, it is obligatory in our view — yet Abū Ḥanīfah did not adhere to it in the cases of muṣārāh (milking-animal deception), ʿarāyā (fresh-fruit sales), and the option of the two contracting parties (khiyār al-mutabāyiʿayn), nor did he deem it good (istahsana) to follow these hadiths despite the agreement of hadith scholars on their authenticity, while the hadith of al-qahqahab is weak. As for the Companion's statement when it contradicts analogy, it is followed in our view — yet Abū Ḥanīfah opposed it in the case of intensifying the diyah (taghlīẓ al-diyah), despite what is transmitted from the Companions therein. Ibn ʿAbbās's estimation of the reward for returning a runaway slave at forty may be by way of a settlement (muṣālaḥah) or a public interest (maṣlaḥah) necessitated by a dispute in that particular situation. Ibn Masʿūd's statement on the slave's value hinges on the analogy of the dhimmiyah (protected woman) and its observance, while the estimation of the reduction observes the nisāb (threshold) of theft — for it is significant in the Law, and disparity appears therein — therefore we did not follow him.

As for his claim that people's practice is followed in muʿāṭāh because the ages do not differ therein — this is arbitrary (taḥakkum), for we know that invalid contracts and usurious transactions (ribawiyyāt) in our era are more numerous than in early Islam and its purest period, and the common masses (ʿawāmm) are not heeded such that their practice is clung to.

As for following the subtle meaning when it is more specific, it is indeed followed — for the evident meaning that does not touch the intended purpose is nullified by it or superseded. But Abū Ḥanīfah did not adhere to its requirement, until he produced wonders and marvels and called it istihsān, saying: 'The prescribed punishment (ḥadd) is obligatory upon one against whom four witnesses testify to adultery (zinā) in four corners [of a house], each testifying against him in a corner' — and he said: 'Perhaps he was crawling in a single act of adultery through the corners.' What istihsān is there in shedding the blood of a Muslim through such a fantasy? For if each testimony were restricted to a specific time and the times were close, and the continuation of adultery in such a period were possible, no ḥadd would apply — and that is more prevalent in custom than imagining his dragging through the house's corners in a single act of adultery. This and its like are among the invalid istihsānāt. Whatever is grounded in a valid source from what we have mentioned is indeed adopted. And God knows best what is correct.

I say: The seventh chapter concerns the mention of qiyās al-shabah (analogy by resemblance), and it contains two sections.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الاول في ذكر المذاهب وبيان ماهيته

وقد صار الشافعي رضي الله عنه وابو حنيفية ومالك واشياعهم في جملة
الفقهاء إلا ابا اسحق المروزي إلى قبول قياس الشبه وذهب القاضي في جمع من
الاصولين إلى رده مع الاتفاق على قبول ما في معنى الاصل كالحاق الأمة
بالعبد
وزعم القاضي ان الذرة في باب الربا في معنى البر المنصوص كالأمة في معنى
العبد وهذا فيه نظر فان الجنس مختلف ولهذا يجوز التفاضل بين الذرة والبر
وليس ذلك مما يبتدر إلى الفهم ابتدار الأمة مع العبد والقائلون بالشبه في
الاحكام اختلفوا في التشابه الخلقي كالحاق الولد يالقيافة قد بالوالد
والنظر في الخلقة في جزاء الصيد وإلحاق المني بالبيض في تولد الحيوان
الطاهر منه في اثبات طهارته ومثال قياس الشبه تردد العبد بين الحر والبهيمة
فشبه البهيمة في كونه
مملوكا فلا يملك ويشبه الحر في كونه متصرفا نافذ العبادة ومالكا للبضع
بالنكاح إذ شرط هذا الفن ان لا يبالغ في تقريره فليحلق بقياس المخيل عند
المبالغة فيه وربما يضعف مقرره فيضاهي الطرد فلا بد من الاقتصاد فيه
وعقد الباب تمييز الشبه عن الطرد ولا خفاء بتميزه عن المخيل فإن الشبه لا
يناسب الحكم ويتميز عما في معنى الأصل فان ذلك يعلم بالبديهة فنقول التشابه
المعتبر هو الذي يوهم الإجتماع في مخيل يناسب الحكم المطلوب وذلك المخيل
مجهولا لا سبيل إلى ابدائه فإذا قلنا العبد  يتصرف وتنفذ عبارته كالحر يشعر
ذلك باجتماعهما في المخيل الذي هو مناط الملك فكأنه يفضي إلى الحكم بواسطة
والطرد هو الذي لا يشعر بالحكم لا بنفسه ولا بواسطة والمخيل هو الذي يشعر
بنفسه فيمس المقصود على وجه المناسبة وان شئت قلت الشبه ما يغلب على الظن
كونه في معنى الاصل وهو مشابه لالحاق الشئ بما في معناه إلا ان ذلك مقطوح
وفي به وهذا غالب على الظن
ويظهر قبول الطرد والعكس في اثبات العلة اذا قبل قياس الشبه فإنه يغلب
على الظن كونه مناط الحكم ولذلك ردد القاضي فيه كلامه مع قطيعة برد الشبه
والشبه جار فيما لا يعقل معناه على معنى انه لا ينقدح فيه معنى مخيل فإن
قيل ما ذكره الشافعي رضي الله عنه من قياس تعيين لفظ التكبير على تعيين
السجود والركوع هل هو من فن التشبيه قلنا قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه ليس ذلك
من الشبه ولكنه ضرب مثلا ليبين ان المحل محل الاتباع ولا جريان للقياس كما
في السجود والركوع في ان مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه في هذه المسالة قريب من
القطع وليس للشبه هذه القوة فإن قيل قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه الشهيد اذا
لم يغسل لم يصل عليه شبه أم لا قلنا قال القاضي يكاد ان يكون شبها من حيث
ان الصلاة مترتبة على الغسل فإذا سقط الغسل اوشك سقوط الصلاة وابدي فيه
ترددا فلم يقطع بكونه شبها وهو شبه ضعيف في الجملة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ب-ه (sh-b-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, similarity, ambiguity; shared attribute between two entities.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Analogical semblance (shabah) as a non-definitive indicator in juristic reasoning, distinct from ratio legis (ʿillah).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in form (tashābuh), but metaphorically extended to denote a conjectural nexus in legal analogy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — governing the protasis "if it is said" (fa-in qīla) and apodosis "we say" (qulnā), with ellipsis of the copula in subordinate clauses.
chapters.translation:
I say: Al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — Abū Ḥanīfah, Mālik, and their followers among the jurists in general, except Abū Isḥāq al-Marwazī, have come to accept the analogy of semblance (qiyās al-shabah). The Judge (al-Qāḍī), however, along with a group of legal theorists, has gone to rejecting it — despite the agreement upon accepting what falls within the meaning of the original (mā fī maʿnā al-aṣl), such as annexing the slave-woman (al-amah) to the slave (al-ʿabd).

The Judge claimed that rice (al-dhurah) in the chapter of usury (ribā) falls within the meaning of the textually-designated wheat (al-burr), just as the slave-woman falls within the meaning of the slave. But there is consideration in this, for the genus differs; hence disparity (tafāḍul) between rice and wheat is permissible. And this is not something that springs immediately to the understanding as the slave-woman springs with the slave.

Those who affirm semblance in legal rulings have differed regarding the semblance of constitution (al-tashābuh al-khilqī) — such as annexing the child through physiognomy (al-qiyāfah) to the parent, and the consideration of physical constitution in the compensation for game (jazāʾ al-ṣayd), and annexing semen to the egg in the generation of an animal that is pure from it, in establishing its purity.

An example of the analogy of semblance: the slave oscillates between the free man and the beast. He resembles the beast in being owned — hence he does not own; and he resembles the free man in being a disposer whose acts of worship are effective and who possesses the right of marriage (al-buḍʿ) through wedlock. The condition of this art is that one not exaggerate in establishing it, lest it attach to the analogy of persuasive suitability (qiyās al-mukhayyal) when exaggerated therein. And perhaps its proponent weakens it, such that it approximates mere formal coincidence (al-ṭard). Thus moderation in it is indispensable.

The chapter's purpose is to distinguish semblance from formal coincidence. There is no obscurity in distinguishing it from the persuasive-suitable (al-mukhayyal), for semblance does not appropriately correspond to the ruling. And it is distinguished from what falls within the meaning of the original, for that is known by intuition (al-badīhah). We therefore say: the semblance that is considered is that which suggests a commonality in a persuasive-suitable attribute (mukhayyal) that corresponds to the sought ruling. That persuasive-suitable attribute is unknown, with no way to disclose it. So when we say "the slave disposes and his utterance is effective, like the free man," this suggests their commonality in the persuasive-suitable attribute that is the nexus (manāṭ) of ownership — as if it leads to the ruling by means of an intermediary.

Formal coincidence (al-ṭard) is that which suggests the ruling neither by itself nor by an intermediary. The persuasive-suitable (al-mukhayyal) is that which suggests it by itself, touching the intended object in the mode of appropriateness (munāsabah). If you wish, you may say: semblance is what predominates in conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) to be within the meaning of the original — and it resembles the annexation of a thing to what is within its meaning, except that the latter is certain (maqṭūʿ) while this is predominant in conjecture.

The acceptance of formal coincidence and inversion (al-ʿaks) in establishing the cause (al-ʿillah) becomes apparent when the analogy of semblance is accepted, for it predominates in conjecture to be the nexus of the ruling. For this reason, the Judge vacillated in his speech regarding it, despite his categorical rejection of semblance.

Semblance operates in what is not rationally comprehensible in its meaning — in the sense that no persuasive-suitable meaning (maʿnā mukhayyal) strikes therein. If it is said: what al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — mentioned regarding the analogy of specifying the utterance of the takbīr upon the specification of prostration and bowing — is that of the art of semblance? We say: al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — said that this is not of semblance; rather, he struck an example to clarify that the locus is a locus of following (ittibāʿ), with no room for analogy — just as in prostration and bowing. In this matter, the school of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — approaches certainty (al-qaṭʿ), and semblance does not possess this strength.

If it is said: the statement of al-Shāfiʿī — may God be pleased with him — that "the martyr, if not washed, is not prayed over" — is it semblance or not? We say: the Judge said it is almost semblance, in that the prayer is ordered upon the washing; so when the washing falls away, the prayer nearly falls away. He exhibited hesitation therein and did not definitively affirm it as semblance — and it is a weak semblance, in sum.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في ذكر ادلة الفريقين

قال القاضي اقول للمتمسك بالشبه اعلمت انه مناط الحكم او ظننته
فان علمته فبالضرورة ام بالنظر لا وجه لإدعاء واحد منهما وان ظننت فما
مستند ظنك والظن في هذا المقام كالعلم وان ابان مستندا لظنه بابداء الا
خالة فذاك وان لم يبد اخالة عجز عن اثبات مستنده فلا نزال نطالبه حتى نتبين
تحكمه وعضد هذا بأن المنقول عن الصحابة النظر إلى المصالح فأما الشبه فلم
ينقل عنهم
وقولك ان العبد اذا نفذت عبارته  ملك تحكم فإن نفوذ العبارة اشارة إلى
انتظامها وصحتها وهذا لا يناسب الملك وان قلت يوهم الإجتماع في مخيل قلنا
أبد ذلك المخيل وإلا فلا يتمسك بالمجهول فإن قلت ملك البضع فملك الأعيان
كان ذلك تحكما إذ لا مناسبة بينهما على انه ينقدح في النكاح مصلحة واضحة
وهي محاذرة الإضرار بالعبيد في سد باب النكاح ولا ضرار فيما دونه من
الأملاك والمختار عندنا أن الشبه مقبول وهو ما غلب على الظن كونه في معناه
فنقول للقاضي قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه طهارتان فكيف تفترقان وعني به
الوضوء والتيمم في حكم النية أيغلب على ظنك كون الوضوء في
معنى التيمم في حكم النية وكل واحد منهما طهارة عن حدث لا يعقل معناه
ويغلب عليه التعبد وقد عسر ذلك الفرق بينهما فإن أنكر غلبة الظن فقد عاند
وإن اعترف به فيطالب بمستنده وينعكس عليه الأمر ولا خفاء بظهور الظن
ويعلم أن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم لو عدموا قياس المعنى لتمسكوا بمثل هذه
الظنون قطعا فإن جملة المسائل لا ينقدح فيها معنى مخيل والصحابة استرسلوا
على الفتاوى فيعلم أنهم اعتمدوا الشبه الشبه نعم يشترط أن لا ينقدح في
الأصل معنى مخيل فلو اتجه بطل التشبيه إذ الحكم منوط به ولم يجر ذلك في
الفرع فلا يوهم الإجتماع في مخيل موهوم وقد رأينا المخيل المعلوم فيه لم
يطرد كما ذكره القاضي في قياس ملك العين على ملك النكاح ثم المعلل المتمسك
بالشبه لو قال هذا يشبه ذاك ولم يبين وجه التشبيه قال قائلون يكتفي به وعلى
السائل قطع التشبيه
والمختار أنه لا بد من الإيماء إلى جهة المشابهة وبيان أن الفرق عسر
فلعسر الفرق وتحقق المشابهة غلب على الظن الحكم حتى يكون مناسبا كما إذا
ألحق الذرة بالبر فيقربه منه في مقصود الطعم وغيره مما يتشابهان
فيه

### | الباب الثامن فيما لا يعلل من الأحكام

لا يطمع في تعليل كل حكم في الشرع ولكنها منقسمة والضابط أن كل ما انقدح
فيه معنى مخيل مناسب مطرد  لا يصدمه أصل من أصول الشرع فهو معلل وما لم يتجه
ذلك فيه كالعبادات والمقدرات فيجري فيه قياس ما في معنى الأصل وقياس الشبه
إن أمكن تشبيه يورث غلبة الظن وقال ابو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يجري القياس في
الحدود والكفارات والمقدرات والرحض ثم أفحش القياس في درء الحدود في السرقة
والقصاص حتى أبطل قاعدة الشرع وفي إثباتها حتى أوجب في شهود الزوايا
وأوجب قطع السرقة بشهادة شاهدين شهدا أحدهما على أنه سرق بقرة بيضاء وشهد
الآخر على بقرة سوداء لإحتمال أن البقرة كانت ملمعة وقاسوا غير الجماع على
الجماع في الصوم في إيجاب الكفارة والخطأ في قتل الصيد على العمد في إيجاب
الجزاء مع اختصاص النص بالعمد وقدر نزح ماء البئر عند نجاسته بثلاثين دلوا
قياسا ولا ينفعهم قولهم إنا قلدنا الأوزاعي فإنهم أبوا عن تقليد الصحابة في
مسائل فكيف قلدوه وقدروا العفو عن النجاسة بربع الثوب والمسح على الرأس
بربعه
وقاسوا في الرخص في سائر النجاسات على مقدار ما عفي عنه على محل النجو
رخصة فقد خبطوا هذه الأصول مسألة إذا وردت قاعدة خارجة عن قياس القواعد
كالكتابة والإجارة قال قائلون لا يجري القياس لا في أصلها ولا في فرعها
وقال آخرون يجري في فروعها ولا يقاس عليه أصل آخر والمختار أن إطلاق
الأمرين سقيم فإن القواعد وإن تباينت في خواصها فقد تتلاقى في أمور جميلة
كملاحظة كل النكاح والبيع والإجارة في كونه معاوضة وإن باينها في مقصوده
فيمتنع الاعتبار في المقصود الذي فيه التباين لا فيما فيه التلاحظ والتناسب
ومثاله من الكتابة أن أبا حنيفة رحمه الله يقيس الشراء الفاسد على الكتابة
الفاسدة ولو استقام له استنباط معنى يجعل الفاسد في مقصود الكتابة
كصحيحه فيبني عليه أن فاسد البيع بالنسبة إلى صحيحه في مقصوده الخاص
كفاسد الكتابة فيستقيم هذا القياس إلا أنه لم يتمكن منه فرد عليه قياسه
لتحكمه في قياس فاسد البيع على فاسد الكتابة مع تباين مقصوديهما فلا وأما
فروع الكتابة يجري فيها القياس ولولاها  لما اتسعت فروعها
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ش-ب-ه (Sh-B-H)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Resemblance, ambiguity, or similarity between two things in their attributes or states.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In legal theory, al-shabah denotes a semblance that yields predominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) regarding the ratio legis (ʿillah) of a ruling, though not a verified meaning (maʿnā mukhīl).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in describing visual or conceptual similarity; metaphorical when applied to juridical analogy where the resemblance is inferred, not directly perceived.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-taqsīm) — The text employs repeated conditional clauses (fa-in... fa-dhāka) and disjunctive alternatives (immā... wa-immā) to structure dialectical refutation, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say — addressing the one who clings to semblance (al-shabah): Do you know with certainty that it is the ratio of the ruling, or do you merely conjecture it? If you know it, then either by necessity or by theoretical reflection — and there is no ground for claiming either. And if you merely conjecture, then what is the basis of your conjecture? For conjecture in this station is like knowledge. If you disclose a basis for your conjecture by manifesting an indicant (ikhālah), then that is acceptable. But if you do not manifest an indicant, you have failed to establish your basis — and we shall not cease demanding it from you until your arbitrary judgment (taḥakkum) becomes evident. This is reinforced by the fact that what is transmitted from the Companions is their consideration of interests (maṣāliḥ); as for semblance, nothing is transmitted from them.

And your statement that when a slave’s manumission is executed, he acquires the power of disposal (taḥakkum) — the execution of the manumission formula indicates its proper ordering and validity, and this does not suit the acquisition of ownership. If you say it suggests a convergence in the imagination (makhīl), we reply: manifest that imagined point, otherwise you may not cling to the unknown. If you say that ownership of the marriage-bond (milk al-buḍʿ) is analogous to ownership of chattels, that is arbitrary judgment, for there is no suitability between them. Moreover, in marriage a clear interest does suggest itself — namely, averting harm to slaves by closing the door of marriage — and there is no harm in what is lesser among properties.

The chosen position with us is that semblance is acceptable — namely, what predominates in conjecture as being within its meaning. So we say to the Judge (al-Qāḍī): Al-Shāfiʿī, may God be pleased with him, said, “Two purifications — how can they differ?” — meaning by that ablution (wuḍūʾ) and dry ablution (tayammum) regarding the ruling of intention. Does it predominate in your conjecture that ablution is within the meaning of dry ablution regarding the ruling of intention? For each of them is a purification from ritual impurity whose meaning is not rationally grasped, and devotional submission (taʿabbud) predominates over it — and the differentiation between them has become difficult. If he denies the predominance of conjecture, he is obstinate; and if he concedes it, he is then demanded for its basis, and the matter reverses upon him. There is no obscurity in the emergence of conjecture, and it is known that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, had they lacked analogy of meaning (qiyās al-maʿnā), would certainly have clung to such conjectures. For a host of cases admit no imagined meaning, yet the Companions proceeded freely in issuing legal verdicts — so it is known that they relied upon semblance. Yes, it is conditioned that no imagined meaning suggest itself in the root (al-aṣl); for if one did suggest itself, the comparison would be void, since the ruling is attached to it — and if that does not run in the branch, then no convergence in an imagined point arises. We have seen that the known imagined meaning did not run uniformly, as the Judge mentioned in the analogy of owning chattels upon owning the marriage-bond. Then, if the one who clings to semblance says, “This resembles that,” without clarifying the aspect of resemblance, some say he is sufficient, and the burden falls upon the questioner to sever the resemblance. The chosen position is that he must gesture toward the dimension of similarity and demonstrate that the differentiation is difficult — for by the difficulty of differentiation and the verification of resemblance, conjecture predominates regarding the ruling, such that it becomes suitable — as when one annexes a grain of wheat to wheat itself, bringing it near in the purpose of taste and other aspects in which they resemble each other.

### | The Eighth Chapter on What is Not Rationally Grounded (lā yuʿallal) Among Rulings

One should not aspire to ground every ruling in the Sacred Law with a ratio (ʿillah); rather, they are divided. The controlling principle is: everything in which an imagined, suitable, uniform meaning suggests itself, not colliding with any root of the roots of the Sacred Law, is rationally grounded. As for that in which no such meaning suggests itself — like devotional acts (ʿibādāt) and fixed measures (muqaddarāt) — then analogy of what is within the meaning of the root and analogy of semblance may run therein, if a comparison is possible that yields predominance of conjecture. Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, said: Analogy does not run in penal limits (ḥudūd), expiations (kaffārāt), fixed measures, and... Then he went to excess in applying analogy in averting penal limits in theft and retaliation, until he nullified a principle of the Sacred Law; and in affirming them, until he imposed [liability] upon witnesses of contradiction, and imposed amputation for theft upon the testimony of two witnesses — one testifying that he stole a white cow, the other that he stole a black cow — due to the possibility that the cow was piebald. And they analogized other-than-intercourse upon intercourse in fasting regarding the obligation of expiation, and error in killing game upon intentional [killing] regarding the obligation of the penalty, despite the text being specific to the intentional. And they fixed the drawing of water from a well upon its impurity at thirty buckets by analogy. Nor does their saying “We have followed al-Awzāʿī” avail them — for they refused to follow the Companions in certain cases, so how could they follow him? And they fixed the pardon for impurity at a quarter of the garment, and the wiping over the head at a quarter of it. And they analogized in the concessions (rukhaṣ) regarding the rest of impurities upon the amount pardoned — upon the locus of impurity being a concession — so they have confounded these roots.

**Issue:** When a rule comes that is outside the analogy of the rules — like kitābah (contract of manumission) and ijārah (hire) — some say analogy does not run in its root nor in its branches. Others say it runs in its branches, but no other root is analogized upon it. The chosen position is that the absolute assertion of either matter is unsound. For the rules, though they differ in their specific properties, may converge in common aspects — like the consideration of marriage, sale, and hire in being commutative transactions (muʿāwaḍah), even if each differs in its specific purpose. So consideration is barred in the purpose wherein lies the difference, not in that wherein lies mutual regard and proportionality. An example from kitābah: Abū Ḥanīfah, may God have mercy on him, analogizes the corrupt sale upon the corrupt kitābah. Had he succeeded in extracting a meaning that makes the corrupt [contract] in the purpose of kitābah like its valid one, then he could build upon it that the corrupt sale relative to its valid one in its specific purpose is like the corrupt kitābah — and this analogy would be sound. But he did not achieve that, so his analogy was refuted against him for his arbitrariness in analogizing the corrupt sale upon the corrupt kitābah despite the divergence of their two purposes. As for the branches of kitābah, analogy runs therein — and were it not for that, its branches would not have expanded.

### | فصل

قال القاضي من الأحكام ما يعلل جملة بعلة لا تطرد في التفاصيل وذكر ثلاثة
أمثلة أحدها أنه قال لا يستقيم قول أبي حنيفة إن رفع الحدث لا يعقل معناه
فلا يقاس عليه إزالة النجاسة لأن الغرض منه معقول وهو الوضاءة فلهذا اختص
بالأعضاء البادية غالبا واكتفى في الناصية بالمسح لأن الغالب عليه الستر
ويشهد لهذا إيماء الشارع من قوله ولكن يريد ليطهركم
ويدل عليه أن الإنسان في حالاته في ترددات لا تخلوا من غبرات تلحقه
والشرع يستحب مكارم الأخلاق والتنقي عن الدنس والدرن من أحبها نعم اختص
بحالة خروج الحدث فوقت وجوبه غير معقول كاختصاص وجوب إزالة النجاسة بوقت
الصلاة لا يعقل معناه ولكن أصله معقول والمثال الثاني أن الشرع قدر الحدث
مانعا من الصلاة وهو غير معقول ولكن بعد اعتقاده يعقل كون الوضوء رافعا له
وإذا ارتفع فلا مانع من الصلاة إلى أن يعود ولم يفهم ذلك في التيمم فإنه لا
يرفعه وإنما هو استباحة مع حدث فيجب أن يتيمم لكل صلاة إذ قال رسول الله
صلى الله عليه وسلم أينما أدركتني الصلاة تيممت وصليت
وقياسه يقتضي ان لا يتنفل به لعدم الضرورة فلعل ذلك من وقفات معاني الشرع
أو يقال النوافل جبران الفرائض وقد خففه الشرع حتى جوز القعود فيه للقادر
على القيام حثا عليه فلا يليق به تغليظ أمره فإن ذلك إضرار بالمسافر المثال
الثالث أن الحد شرع للزجر وعقل على قياسه أصل تفرقة الشارع بين ما دون
النصاب وبين النصاب لأن النفوس لا تتحمل الأضرار لأجل مال نزر ولكن لا يطرد
في التفاصيل لأنه قد يتشوق الشخص إلى ربع دينار دون حبة ولكن لا نظر إليه
وذلك لا يخرم أصل المعنى المعقول والربع وإن كان قليلا في الهمم العالية
فالغالب أنه لا يهجم على السرقة إلا الأرذال من الناس وخساسهم منه فيكثر
ذلك عندهم ووجة الإشكال أنا نرى الروح تسفك في مقابلة الصيال على حبة ولكن
ذلك مما لا رادع منه في  الطبع بحيث يعظم وقعه فما دام المرء مواظبا
على هتك الحرمة كان مدفوعا عن هتكه لا كوزن المال وههنا يجب بسرقة المال
عند اقتحام الغرر وقال القاضي فكان يليق به الفرق بين قليل الخمر وكثيرة
لنفرة الطبع عن قليله فلعل هذا من وقفات علة الشرع
والعلل الكلية قد يفرض وقوفها بأصل مقطوع به وإن كان لا يرد بغلبات
الظنون ولعل المعنى فيه أن قليل الخمر يدعو إلى كثيره والقدر المسكر لا
ينضبط مع تفاوت الطباع فحسم الباب حسما قال القاضي وإن عقلنا الفرق بين
القليل والكثير فلا يقاس به في هذا التقدير غيره ردا على مالك حيث قال بغلظ
اليمين في عظيم من المال وقدره بنصاب السرقة لأنه ينقدح معنى مخيل في
التقدير به ومسلك يشبه الإيمان بالسرقة غير منقدح

### | الباب التاسع في التركيب والتعدية

وفيه اربعة فصول

### | الفصل الأول بيان الجمع بين علتين متظاهرتين على حكم واحد

وقد منه القاضي تمسكا بأن الصحابة رضي الله عنهم لم ينقل عنهم ذلك
واعتصاما بإجماع القياسيين على إتحاد علة الربا مع إمكان الجمع وقال إذا
صادفنا علة منصوصا عليها من جهة الشارع فيغلب على الظن أنه المناط على
الخصوص وإن تعلق بغيره معه لذكره الشارع وقد تولى بيانه وكذا لو أجمعت
الأمة على التعليل به واقتصروا عليه إذ يبعد أن يذهل
أهل الإجماع عن علة صحيحة مع شدة بحثهم
وإن هجمنا عليه واستنبطناه فما هو أجلى تقدم على الآخر لا محالة والمختار
أن العلل قد تزدحم على حكم واحد ويعلم ان الصحابة رضي الله عنهم في
اشتوارهم كانت تتشعب أراؤهم إلى مصالح متظاهرة ولا يشتغلون بالترجيح ومسألة
الربا ليست معللة عندنا ولا هي مجمع عليها ولكن كل اعتقد أن علة خصمه باطلة
لا تستقل ولذلك لم يجمعوا ومسالك الترجيح فيها باطلة عندنا وما ذكره من نص
الشارع أو الإجماع لا ينكر أن ذلك ينتج خيالا ولكن لا بعد في وكول الشارع
الباقي إلى استنباط الأئمة واستغنى أهل الإجماع بإحدى العلتين عن الأخرى
وقوله إذا لاح أحدهما ينبغي أن يقدم قلنا لا نرى بعدا في اعتقاد ثبوت
المسألة بحديث وقياس وإن تفاوتت مراتبهما وإذا تعارضت المصالح من غير ترجيح
فلا وجه للقضاء بتساقطها: وإلحاق الحكم بالفذ غير الذي لا يعلل وليس بعضها
أولى من بعض ولا بعد في أن يحكم الشارع بحكم واحد لأجل مصلحتين ولا يلزم
على هذا أن يصحح قول القائل مس فصار كما لو مس وبال أو معتدة فصارت
كالمعتدة البائنة أو أنثى فصارت كالأنثى الصغيرة فهذا باطل قطعا لأن المعلل
يحتاج إلى أن يصرح بضم علة أخرى
إلى علته لو ألغاها لكان قياسا على نفس المسألة فلتكن العلة الجامعة بحيث
لو وقع الذهول عن الثانية لصح الجمع قال القاضي وقول الشافعي رضي الله عنه
في جزاء الأسد حيوان لا يجزى بقيمة ولا مثل فلا يجزى كالفواسق الخمس باطل
لأن معناه أن ما لا يجزى لا يجزى وهذا استدلال بنفس الحكم وهو مطالب بنصب
الدليل على نفي الضمان على الوجه الذي ذكروه وليس فيه ما يدل عليه
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع ل ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To give a reason, cause, or rationale; recurrent and repeated occurrence (as in a recurring illness); the underlying ground (ʿillah) that necessitates a judgment.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The ʿillah in legal theory is the effective attribute (manāṭ) that the Lawgiver makes the occasioning ground for a ruling, whether explicitly stated or inferred by juristic reasoning (ijtihād).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage denotes a genuine causal nexus; metaphorical usage (majāz) occurs when the "cause" is merely a sign (amārah) or occasion, not a true efficient cause.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — When multiple clauses are coordinated, the later clause may serve to clarify or restrict the scope of the earlier general statement, as seen in the juxtaposition of the three examples (amthilah) under a single general claim.
chapters.translation:
**Section**

The Judge (al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr al-Bāqillānī) said: Among the rulings (aḥkām) there are those whose rationale (ʿillah) is stated in general terms, yet that rationale does not run uniformly (lā taṭṭarid) across all the particular details. He mentioned three examples.

**The First Example:** He said that Abū Ḥanīfah's position is untenable when he claims that the lifting of ritual impurity (rafʿ al-ḥadath) has no intelligible meaning, and therefore it cannot be analogized to the removal of filth (izālat al-najāsah). For the purpose (gharaḍ) of the latter is intelligible — namely, cleanliness and comeliness (al-waḍāʾah). For this reason, it is restricted to the exposed body parts (al-aʿḍāʾ al-bādiyah) in most cases, and one suffices with wiping (al-masḥ) over the forelock (al-nāṣiyah) because the dominant condition there is concealment (al-satr). This is attested by the Lawgiver's allusion (īmāʾ al-shāriʿ) in His saying: {«وَلَٰكِن يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ»} ("But He intends to purify you") (Q 5:6). It is further indicated by the fact that a person, in his various states and fluctuations, is never free from dust and grime that cling to him; and the Law (al-sharʿ) recommends noble character traits (makārim al-akhlāq) and cleansing oneself from filth and dirt — whoever loves these things [is thereby purified]. Yes, it is restricted to the state of the emission of ḥadath, so the time of its obligation is not intelligible — just as the restriction of the obligation to remove filth to the time of prayer is not intelligible in its meaning, but its underlying principle (aṣl) is intelligible.

**The Second Example:** The Law (al-sharʿ) determined that ḥadath is a preventive barrier (māniʿ) to prayer, and this is not intelligible [in itself]. But once one affirms this [legal determination], it becomes intelligible that ablution (wuḍūʾ) lifts it; and when it is lifted, there is no barrier to prayer until it returns. This understanding, however, is not achieved in the case of tayammum (dry ablution), for it does not lift the ḥadath; rather, it merely permits [prayer] while the ḥadath remains (istibāḥah maʿa al-ḥadath). Therefore, one must perform tayammum for every [obligatory] prayer, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Wherever the prayer overtakes me, I perform tayammum and pray." Analogical reasoning (qiyās) would require that one not perform supererogatory prayers (tanafful) with it, due to the absence of necessity. Perhaps this is among the pauses (waqafāt) of the meanings of the Law — or it may be said that supererogatory prayers are complements (jabrān) to the obligatory ones, and the Law has made them light, even permitting sitting in them for one able to stand, as an encouragement toward them; hence it is not fitting that its matter be made stringent, for that would be harmful to the traveler.

**The Third Example:** The ḥadd (fixed corporal punishment) was legislated for deterrence (al-zajr), and its rationale is intelligible, measured by analogy upon its principle: the Lawgiver's differentiation between what is below the niṣāb (minimum threshold) and the niṣāb itself — because souls do not endure harms for the sake of a paltry sum of wealth. But this does not run uniformly across the particulars, for a person might covet a quarter of a dīnār more than a [whole] grain [of wheat], yet no consideration is given to that [individual inclination]. This does not vitiate the principle of the intelligible meaning. For although a quarter [dīnār] is little in lofty aspirations, the dominant case (al-ghālib) is that none rush into theft except the base and vile among people; and among them, that [amount] is considerable. The source of the difficulty (wajh al-ishkāl) is that we see the soul being shed in response to an assault over a single grain — but that [assault] is something that nature does not deter such that its impact is magnified. So long as a person persists in violating sanctity (hatk al-ḥurmah), he is restrained from his violation — not like the weight of wealth. And here, [the ḥadd] becomes obligatory for the theft of wealth when one ventures into risk (iqtiḥām al-gharar). The Judge said: It would have been fitting to differentiate between a small amount of wine and a large amount, given nature's aversion to a small quantity. Perhaps this is among the pauses of the Law's rationale (waqafāt ʿillat al-sharʿ).

The universal rationales (al-ʿilal al-kulliyyah) may be supposed to pause at a definitively established principle (aṣl maqṭūʿ bihi), even if they are not repelled by preponderant conjectures (ghalabāt al-ẓunūn). Perhaps the meaning therein is that a small amount of wine calls to a large amount, and the intoxicating quantity cannot be precisely fixed given the variation of temperaments — so the door was shut completely (ḥasm al-bāb ḥasman). The Judge said: Even if we understand the difference between the small and the large, one should not analogize to it in this particular estimation anything else — as a refutation of Mālik, who held that the oath is made stringent (taghlīẓ al-yamīn) in cases of great wealth and estimated it by the niṣāb of theft. For an evocative meaning (maʿnā mukhayyil) suggests itself in that estimation, and a path resembling faith [in the analogy] with theft is not suggested.

---

### Chapter Nine: On Composition (al-Tarkīb) and Transitivity (al-Taʿdiyah)

It contains four sections.

### Section One: Elucidation of Combining Two Rationales Converging upon a Single Ruling

The Judge (al-Bāqillānī) prohibited this, clinging to the fact that the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) did not transmit such [practice] from them, and seeking refuge in the consensus (ijmāʿ) of the analogists (al-qiyāsiyyīn) upon the unity of the rationale for ribā (usury), despite the possibility of combining [multiple rationales]. He said: When we encounter a rationale explicitly stated (manṣūṣ ʿalayhā) by the Lawgiver, the dominant conjecture (ghalabat al-ẓann) is that it is the operative ground (al-manāṭ) specifically — even if something else is attached to it along with it — because the Lawgiver mentioned it and undertook its elucidation. Likewise, if the ummah had agreed upon the rationale and restricted themselves to it — for it is unlikely that the people of consensus would overlook a sound rationale given the intensity of their investigation.

But if we arrive at it by our own inference (hajamnā ʿalayhi) and derive it (istinbaṭnāhu), then the more evident (ajlā) of the two must take precedence over the other, without question.

The chosen position (al-mukhtār), however, is that rationales may crowd together (tazdaḥim) upon a single ruling. It is known that the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), in their consultations, had their opinions branching into converging interests (maṣāliḥ mutaẓāharah) and did not occupy themselves with preponderance (al-tarjīḥ). The question of ribā is not, in our view, rationally grounded (muʿallalah), nor is it a matter of consensus; rather, each [scholar] believed that his opponent's rationale was invalid and could not stand independently — and for that reason they did not reach consensus. The paths of preponderance therein are invalid in our view. As for what he mentioned of an explicit text (naṣṣ) from the Lawgiver or consensus — it is not denied that this produces an evocative notion (khayāl), but there is no improbability in the Lawgiver delegating the remainder to the inference of the imams; and the people of consensus sufficed with one of the two rationales over the other.

As for his saying: "When one of the two becomes apparent, it should be given precedence" — we say: We see no improbability in holding the ruling to be established by both a ḥadīth and an analogy (qiyās), even if their ranks differ. And when interests conflict without preponderance, there is no basis for judging that they cancel each other out (tasāquṭ), nor for attaching the ruling to a single one (al-fadhdh) — that which is not rationally grounded — while none of them is more deserving than another. There is no improbability in the Lawgiver ruling by a single ruling for the sake of two interests (maṣlaḥatayn).

This does not entail validating the statement of one who says: "He touched [a woman], so he became like one who touched urine; or a menstruating woman, so he became like one who touched a divorced woman (bāʾinah); or a female, so he became like one who touched a minor female" — for this is absolutely invalid (bāṭil qaṭʿan). Because the one who gives a rationale (al-muʿallil) must explicitly state the addition of another rationale to his own; if he were to disregard it, it would be an analogy upon the very same question (qiyās ʿalā nafs al-masʾalah). The comprehensive rationale (al-ʿillah al-jāmiʿah) must be such that if one were to overlook the second [rationale], the combination would still be sound.

The Judge said: Al-Shāfiʿī's (may Allah be pleased with him) statement regarding the penalty for [killing] a lion — "It is an animal for which neither value nor equivalent is due, so it is not [subject to compensation], like the five corruptive creatures (al-fawāsiq al-khams)" — is invalid. For its meaning is: "What is not compensable is not compensable" — and this is an inference from the very ruling itself (istidlāl bi-nafs al-ḥukm). He is required to establish the evidence (naṣb al-dalīl) for negating liability (ḍamān) in the manner they mentioned, and there is nothing in it that indicates this.

chapters.arabic_text:
### | الفصل الثاني في بيان مراتب التركيب

وهو منقسم إلى التركيب في الأصل وإلى التركيب في الوصف فأما التركيب في
الأصل فمن أبعد أبوابه قول أصحابنا أنثى فلا تزوج نفسها كبنت خمس عشرة سنة
وهو باطل إذ للسائل أن يقول إن كانت هي في علم الله كبيرة فقد قست على نفس
المسألة وإن كانت صغيرة صرت كمن قال مس فصار كما لو مس وبال وأقرب منه
قليلا قولهم في البكر البالغ لم تمارس الرجال فتجبر كبنت خمس عشرة سنة فإن
جهة الفساد تتحد فيه
إذ لو قدرت صغيرة فالصغر ليس مستقلا عند الشافعي رضي الله عنه بإفادة
الإجبار، بدليل الثيب الصغيرة فإنها لا تجبر والتركيب في الوصف أبعده
كقولنا في قتل المسلم بالذمي لو قتل بالمثقل لم يقتل فكذا بالسيف ووجه بعده
أن النظر في الآلة لا يدل على معنى المكافأة وهو المقصود في المسألة وأقربه
قولنا في اندراج الثمار غير المؤبرة تحت مطلق  العقد ما يندرج تحت استحقاق
الشفيع يندرج تحت مطلق العقد ووجه قربه أنه يشير إلى الجزئية المؤثرة في
الاندراج إلا أنهم يقولون تخلينا الضرار سببا لإثبات الشفعة في الثمار لئلا
تنفى الداخلة لذلك طردنا في المؤبرة فإن صح علة الضرار بطل التعليل وإن بطل
الضرار لم نقض باندراجه تحت الشفعة

### | الفصل الثالث في ذكر ضابط الأدلة فيه

قال الأستاذ أبو اسحق في جماعة إن التركيب صحيح وغلا حتى قدمه على غير
المركب لأنه أبعد عن الاعتراضات ومنهم من رجح غيره ومنهم من سوى
قال القاضي أبو بكر التركيب باطل واستدل الأستاذ بأن الغرض في المناظرة
التضييق على الخصم وتنقيح الخاطر في المشكلات والتركيب أقوى في تحصيل الغرض
نعم لا يعول عليه في الاجتهاد كمناقضة الخصم يتمسك بها في المناظرة دون
الفتوى ولا خلل في التركيب إلا كون علة الأصل مختلفا فيها فهو مطالب
بإثباته وإن عجز فهو باطل لا لأجل التركيب
والمختار أن التركيب باطل لأنه فن من القياس لم ينقل عن الصحابة رضي الله
عنهم ولا كانوا يفهمونه وأحدث منذ خمسين سنة ولو كان قياسا صحيحا لتنبه له
الأولون وهو في رسم الجدال خروج عن مقصود المسألة فإن سن البلوغ وسببه لا
يثير نظرا في سلب عبارة المرأة وليس من فروع هذه المسألة ونتيجته فهو تمسك
بأمر ظاهر لا في محل السؤال والمناقضة قد لا يرى التمسك بها فيما قاله
القاضي أبو بكر وإن رأيناها فهي مورطة للخصم في فقه المسألة والتركيب مخرج
لهما عنها وما ذكره من أن علة الأصل أبدا هو مختلف فيها وهو متمكن من
إثباته فلم نرده لكون العلة مختلفا فيها ولكنه خروج عن المسألة ولو تمكن من
إثبات علة الأصل باخاله أحمد فقد استغنى عن الأصل وصار مستدلا وبطل تركيبه
وقوله إن الغرض تنقيح الخاطر قلنا نعم في المسألة لا في هوسات لا تعلق لها
بالمسألة

### | الفصل الرابع في التعدية

والقائلون بالتركيب اعتقدوا التعدية سؤالا صحيحا على المركب وصورته ان
يقول السائل عن قول  الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنثى فلا تزوج نفسها كبنت خمس
عشرة سنة إني استنبطت من الأصل الصغر فعديته بعد إلى منع سائر التصرفات
فيعارض ما استنبطه من الأنوثة ويستوي فيه الأقدام وكذلك اذا قال أنثى لم
تمارس الرجال فتجبر كبنت خمس عشرة سنة في مسألة إجبار البكر فيقول أنا
استنبطت الصغر وطردته في الثيب الصغيرة وزعموا أن هذه التعدية أقوى لأن
الصغر عند الشافعي قط لا يكون علة الإجبار بدليل الثيب الصغيرة فلا يمكنه
القول به والمختار أن سؤال التعدية باطل بعد قبول المركب لأن المعلل يقول
إن لم تسلم لي كون الأنوثة علة فأثبته وعليك إبطاله وإن سلمت فلا نعيد
كاستنباط المجبرة
أو يسلم المسئول له وجود الصغر جدلا في مسألة نكاح بلا ولي وكونه علة
ويقول ليجمع بين العلتين ويسلم وجوده في مسألة إجبار البكر وإن لم يعلل به
فلا يغنيه التعليل به وأما المركب الوصف زعموا أن التعدية علة في القبول
والرد مبني على قبول الفرق بين الوصف والحكم ورده كفرق السائل بين الطلاق
والظهار
إذا قال المعلل من صح طلاقه صح ظهاره كالمسلم والمختار أن التعدية لا ترد
على تركيب الوصف إذ من ضرورته أن يقع التركيب من حكم فيقول من لا يقتل إذا
قتل بالمثقل فكذا بالسيف فلا يمكنه إبراز معنى من القتل بالمثقل في معارضته
والمسئول لم يتعرض للمعنى ولا يمكنه المعارضة بحكم آخر نعم لو قال ذلك لخلل
في الآلة فهذا بيان منه لخروج المسئول عن مقصود المسألة وهو واقع وليس ذلك
من التعدية في شئ والله أعلم

### | الباب العاشر في الاعتراضات
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ر-ك-ب (r-k-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To mount, to join, to compound; al-rukūb is the act of riding, while al-tarkīb is the joining of one thing to another, forming a composite.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, al-tarkīb denotes the syllogistic combination of two premises—an original case (aṣl) and a descriptive attribute (waṣf)—to yield a ruling, a technical extension of the root's sense of "joining."
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literally, "mounting" (rukūb) a beast; metaphorically (majāz), the "superimposition" of one legal attribute onto another, as in the composite analogy.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf wa al-Taqsīm (Coordination and Division) — The text divides "composition" into two types (fī al-aṣl and fī al-waṣf) using the particle "ammā... fa-," requiring the reader to track the parallel syntactic structure for accurate rendering.
chapters.translation:
I say: The second chapter concerns the clarification of the degrees of composition (tarkīb). It is divided into composition in the original case (aṣl) and composition in the descriptive attribute (waṣf). As for composition in the original case, the most remote of its forms is the statement of our companions: "A female may not marry herself off," analogized to "a girl of fifteen years." This is invalid, for the questioner may say: "If she is, in God's knowledge, mature (kabīrah), then you have analogized the very same case; and if she is a minor (ṣaghīrah), you have become like one who says, 'He touched (mas) and thus [it is] as if he urinated (bāl).'" Slightly closer [to validity] is their statement concerning the mature virgin (al-bikr al-bāligh) who has not known men: "She is to be compelled (tujbar)," analogized to "a girl of fifteen years." For the aspect of corruption is unified therein—if you suppose her to be a minor, then minority (al-ṣighar) is not, according to al-Shāfiʿī (may God be pleased with him), an independent ground for effecting compulsion, as evidenced by the minor non-virgin (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah), who is not compelled.

As for composition in the descriptive attribute, its most remote form is our statement in the case of killing a Muslim by a dhimmī: "If he killed with a blunt instrument (al-muthqal), he would not be killed [in retaliation]; so likewise with the sword." The aspect of its remoteness is that consideration of the instrument (al-ālah) does not indicate the meaning of equivalence (al-mukāfaʾah), which is the intended point in the case. Its closest form is our statement concerning the inclusion of unpollinated fruits (al-thimār ghayr al-muʾabbirah) under the absolute contract (muṭlaq al-ʿaqd): "What falls under the preemption right of the co-owner (shafīʿ) falls under the absolute contract." The aspect of its closeness is that it points to the particularity (al-juzʾiyyah) effective in inclusion. However, they say: "We have abandoned [the notion of] harm (al-ḍarar) as a cause for establishing preemption in fruits, lest the included [fruits] be excluded thereby; so we extended [the ruling] to the pollinated ones (al-muʾabbirah). If the cause of harm is valid, the [original] reasoning is invalidated; and if harm is invalidated, we do not judge its inclusion under preemption."

The third chapter concerns the criterion of evidence regarding it. The Master Abū Isḥāq, among a group, held that composition is sound, and he even preferred it over the non-composite, because it is more remote from objections. Some favored the opposite; others deemed them equal. Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr held that composition is invalid. The Master argued that the purpose of disputation (al-munāẓarah) is to constrain the opponent and to refine the mind (tanqīḥ al-khāṭir) regarding problematic issues, and composition is stronger in achieving this purpose. Indeed, it is not relied upon in independent reasoning (ijtihād); rather, like a rebuttal (munāqaḍah) of the opponent, it is employed in disputation, not in legal verdicts (fatwā). There is no defect in composition except that the cause of the original case is disputed; thus, [the proponent] is required to prove it, and if he fails, it is invalid—not because of composition itself.

The chosen position is that composition is invalid, for it is a branch of analogy (qiyās) not transmitted from the Companions (may God be pleased with them), nor did they understand it; it was innovated some fifty years ago. Had it been a sound analogy, the early scholars would have attended to it. In the discipline of dialectic (jadal), it is an exit from the intended point of the case: for the age of majority (sin al-bulūgh) and its cause do not provoke consideration regarding the nullification of a woman's contractual expression (ʿibārah), nor is it a branch of this case or its result. Thus, it is a reliance on an apparent matter not in the locus of the question. As for rebuttal (al-munāqaḍah), one may not see fit to employ it, as al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr stated; and even if we see it, it entangles the opponent in the jurisprudence of the case, whereas composition extracts both from it. As for his claim that the cause of the original case is always disputed and he is able to prove it—we do not reject it because the cause is disputed, but because it is an exit from the case. If he could prove the cause of the original case by [the method of] al-Khalīl Aḥmad, he would have dispensed with the original and become an independent arguer (mustadill), and his composition would be nullified. As for his statement that the purpose is to refine the mind, we say: yes, within the case, not in fancies (hawasāt) unrelated to it.

The fourth chapter concerns transference (al-taʿdiyah). Those who affirm composition believed transference to be a valid question against the composite. Its form is that the questioner says, regarding al-Shāfiʿī's (may God be pleased with him) statement, "A female may not marry herself off," analogized to "a girl of fifteen years": "I have derived from the original the attribute of minority (al-ṣighar), and I transfer it thereafter to the prohibition of all other dispositions (taṣarrufāt)." Thus, he opposes what was derived from femininity (al-ʾunūthah), and both [parties] are equal in it. Likewise, when he says, "A female who has not known men is to be compelled," analogized to "a girl of fifteen years," in the case of compelling the virgin, he says: "I have derived minority and extended it to the minor non-virgin (al-thayyib al-ṣaghīrah)." They claimed that this transference is stronger, because minority, according to al-Shāfiʿī, is absolutely never a cause of compulsion, as evidenced by the minor non-virgin; thus, he cannot affirm it.

The chosen position is that the question of transference is invalid after accepting the composite, because the one who provides the cause (al-muʿallil) says: "If you do not concede that femininity is a cause, then I affirm it, and it is upon you to refute it; and if you concede it, we do not repeat [the derivation], like the derivation of the one who compels." Or the respondent concedes, for the sake of argument (jadal), the existence of minority in the case of marriage without a guardian and its being a cause, and says: "Let him combine the two causes"—and he concedes its existence in the case of compelling the virgin, even if he does not use it as a cause; thus, using it as a cause does not avail him.

As for the composite of the descriptive attribute, they claimed that transference is a cause for acceptance or rejection, built upon accepting the distinction between the attribute and the ruling, and rejecting it—like the questioner's distinction between divorce (ṭalāq) and ẓihār. When the one who provides the cause says, "Whose divorce is valid, his ẓihār is valid, like the Muslim," the chosen position is that transference does not apply to the composite of the attribute, for it is necessary that the composition occur from a ruling. Thus, he says, "Who is not killed if he kills with a blunt instrument, so likewise with the sword"—he cannot extract a meaning from killing with a blunt instrument to oppose it, and the respondent did not address the meaning, nor can he oppose with another ruling. Indeed, if he said that due to a defect in the instrument, this is an explanation by him that the respondent has exited the intended point of the case—and that is real—but it is not part of transference at all. And God knows best.

The tenth book concerns objections (al-iʿtirāḍāt).

chapters.arabic_text:
وهي تنقسم إلى صحيح وفاسد الصحيح منه ثمانية أنواع النوع الأول في المنع
وذلك إذا توجه على وصف التعليل لزم المعلل إثباتها ويتوجه على الأصل من
أربعة أوجه أن يمنع كونه معللا أو يمنع كون ما ذكره علة بعد ما سلم أصل
التعليل أو يمنع وجود ما نصبه علة أو يمنع الحكم ويكفي للمعلل بيان معنى
مخيل للحكم في الأصل فيندفع  به جميعها
ويثبت كونه معللا بهذه العلة وعليه يترتب الحكم إذا ثبت إخالته وله النقل
إلى الأصل إذا منع أو افتتاح الكلام فيه ابتداء إذا توقع المنع
وليس له نصب الدليل على نقض يورده إذا منع والفرق أن ذلك خروج من المسألة
إذ قد يورد مسألة من النكاح نقضا على مسألة في الكتابة وإما إثبات الأصل
إذا منع انتهاض الإثبات في الفرع تحقيقا وليس للسائل أن يدل على المنع
بخلاف المسئول للأمر الجدلي وهو أن المسئول لم يتطوق أن يعترض عليه فإن دل
فلا يصغى إليه لأنه لم يسأله وقال الأستاذ المنع ليس باعتراض لأن إثباته
ممكن للمسئول وقال القاضي هو اعتراض ولولا رسم الجدال لحكم بانقطاعه فإنه
إذا قاس على أصل ممنوع فكأنه ما دل بعد في المسألة ولكن الرجوع إلى الرسم
ولولاه لساغ للسائل ابتداء إبطال فتوى المستدل ولكن لا بد من اتباع الرسم
لينضبط الكلام ويتميز السائل عن المسئول النوع الثاني القول بالموجب من
الاعتراضات التي ينقطع المسئول فيها ويبطل به مقصوده وقد قيل لا يسمى
اعتراضا لأنه مطابقة للعلة والخلاف عائد إلى عبارة
ولا يتأتى القول بالموجب مع التصريح بالحكم الذي فيه النزاع فإن فيه رفعا
للخلاف وإنما يتوجه إذا أجمل الحكم وقال كان كذا فجاز أن يكون
كذا فيقول بموجبه في بعض الصور أو يتعرض لنفي علة الخصم فنقول ماء طاهر
خالطه طاهر فالمخالطة لا تمنع جواز التوضئ كما لو خالطه التراب فيقول أقول
بموجبه إذ المخالطة لا تمنع فينقطع المسئول فلو قال مع التغير فكذا نقول
بالموجب فلو قال منع مع التغير والاستغناء ينبغي أن لا يمنع لا يقال بموجبه
ولكن لا نجد أصلا نقيس عليه وهذا من ألزم أنواعه والذي دونه مما يخلص عنه
بتغيير عبارة كقولنا الجنون في أحد الواطئين لا يدرأ الحد كالجنون فيها
فيقول الجنون لا يدرؤه إذ الدافع خروجها عن كونها ممكنة من الزنا فلو قال
ينبغي أن لا يكون صبيا
قال قائلون يكفي أن يعدل إلى لفظ السبب  فيقول لا يكون الجنون سببا فيه
فإن ما ذكره أيضا مثارة الجنون وزعم آخرون أن السبب بمعنى العلة فلا غنية
فيه والخلاف فيه قريب المدرك وإنما يظهر العدول إلى لفظ السبب إذا تمكن
المسئول من بيان انحصار الحكم في هذا السبب على الخصوص حتى لو قدر اقتصار
أبي حنيفة في ذلك على الجنون دون تنزل الصبي والخرس منزلته لكان لفظ السبب
أقوى في درء هذا السؤال فهذه مراتب ثلاثة في القول بالموجب
النوع الثالث النقض ومعناه إبداء العلة مع تخلف الحكم ولا يورد على العلة
المجملة فإنها باطلة لإجمالها لا يعترض عليها بل يستفسر عنها ومعنى
الاستفسار طلب كشف عما استبهم على السائل لقصور فهمه
وقد انقسم الناس في النقض على ثلاثة مذاهب فقال قائلون ليس ذلك باعتراض
فإن العلل قابلة للتخصيص بمحل اطراده ومنع آخرون التخصيص إطلاقا وسوغ آخرون
تخصيص علة نصبها الشارع دون ما نستنبطه وتمسك المانعون من التخصيص بثلاثة
أمور أحدها أن قالوا الأدلة العقلية تطرد فكذا الشرعية وهذا فاسد فإنها
توجب مدلولاتها لذواتها وأعيانها وهذه أمارة لا يعد في تخصيصها قصور لا
مانع من طردها ثانيها أن ذلك إلى تكافؤ الأدلة فيقول أحد الخصمين مائع
فتزال به النجاسة كالماء ويقول الآخر مائع فلا تزال به النجاسة كالخمر
واللبن وكل لا يقبل النقض تخصيصا لعلته وهذا عندنا فاسد لكونهما طردين ولا
يقع التعارض قط في مخيلين على هذا الوجه وإن اتفق فالترجيح ممكن ولا يؤدي
إلى التكافؤ أصلا
ثالثها قال الأستاذ يقال للمعلل إن زعمت أنك أتيت بعلة عامة فقد كذبت وإن
أتيت بعلة خاصة فلا حاجة إلى التخصيص وهذا تلفيق عبارة لا خير فيه إذ له أن
يقول كنت أظن عمومه والآن إذ منع مانع فالتزم طرده حيث لا مانع والمخصصة
تمسكوا أيضا بثلاثة أمور أحدها أنه لو خصص العلة بالاتفاق بالزمان جاز فكذا
بالمسائل فإن من قال مشتد مسكر تنتقض علته بالخمر في ابتداء الاسلام ثم
يخصصه هذا الزمان وهذا فاسد فإن استيعاب الأزمنة لا  يشترط في العلل الشرعية
وهي لا تدل لذاتها وإنما تدل لظننا أنها منصوبة ولم ينصبها الشارع في
ابتداء الإسلام فإذا نصبها اقتضى وضعه العموم ثانيها أن عموم رسول الله صلى
الله عليه وسلم يخصص فكذا عموم علة المعلل وهذا فاسد
فإن العام عندنا لا يخصص بل نتبين خصوصه في وضعه وإنما لم نفهمه حتى
نتبينه لقرينة كيف وقد قيل إن الباقي من عموم الشارع يبقى مجملا
وقال القاضي يبقى مجازا وهذا لا يحتمل من المعلل ثالثها ما قال القاضي من
أن المعلل وان لم يصرح بتخصيص علة فيفهم من قرينة قوله أنه لا ينبغي طرد
العلة إلا إذا اطرد ولم يمنع منه مانع كالذي يقول المتردي من سطح مسقطه
الأرض يفهم منه عند الإطلاق إذا لم يختطفه مختطف والمختار أن مسألة النقض
إن انقدح فيه فرق مخيل فهو مبطل فإنه مشعر باقتصار المعلل على نصف العلة
وحقه أن يأتي بتمامها إذا طولب بإبداء العلة ولو كان مستثنى عن القياس وكان
من مناقضات الخصم فالعلة تبطل أيضا إذ حقه أن يطرد ولا مانع وإن كان مستثنى
بنص أو إجماع فالذي رآه القاضي أن هذا مجتهد فيه إذ يمكن أن يقال غلبة الظن
متبع إلا إذا منع نص يقدم عليه
ويمكن أن يقال طبع العلة العموم فإذا لم يعم دل ذلك على بطلانه وهذا الفن
من القياس عنده باطل لا لانتقاضه ولكنه يقول ما لا قاطع في قبوله فهو محكوم
ببطلانه قطعا وعندنا أن هذا القياس باطل في جوهره وان كنا لا نرى جعل عدم
القاطع على القبول قاطعا في البطلان ولكن هذه العلة إنما ينصبها المعلل
ظانا أنها منصوب الشارع مقتصرا على غلبة الظن فيها وإذا رأينا الشرع ينفي
الحكم مع وجودها كيف يغلب على ظننا كونها
علة وكيف يظن برسول الله أن يأتي بالمتناقض المتدابر يقول في نفسه وإذا
بطل غلبة الظن فلا مستند
فإن زعم المجتهد أن ظني وراءه باقي في هذه المسألة فيقال له إن تدبرت
استثنيت انتفاء  الظن عند الانتقاض والفاصلون الذي بين علتنا وعلة الشارع
يفرقون بأن له أن يحتكم وليس لنا ذلك فلا بد في تطرق التخصيص إلى علته
والمختار أن التخصيص لا يتطرق إلى جوهر علته فإنه من أعم الصيغ أعني صيغة
التعليل ولا يظن برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن ينصب الشئ علما ثم ينفي
الحكم مع وجوده من غير سبب نعم يتطرق إلى محله كلام فيخصص ببعض المحال
بدليل قوله تعالى والسارق والسارقة وقوله تعالى الزانية والزاني فيذكر
المحل دون العلة وفائدة الخلاف أن من منع التخصيص لا يجوز أصلا تطرقه إلى
ما نص الشارع على التعليل به وإن أومأ إليه يتبين أن ذلك لم يكن إيماء
على تعليل بورود التخصيص والمجوز للتخصيص يقول نبقي ذلك في محله
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ن-ع (manaʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prevention, prohibition, withholding; the act of rendering something forbidden or obstructing its occurrence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In juristic dialectic, al-manʿ denotes the opponent's denial of a premise or the validity of an inference, a procedural refusal rather than a substantive counter-argument.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense is physical obstruction; here it is metaphorical (majāz) for logical impediment — the denial that blocks the proponent's proof.
- Root: ن-ق-ض (naqaḍa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To unravel, break, or invalidate; the undoing of a woven structure.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In uṣūl al-fiqh, naqḍ is the objection that a stated ʿillah (ratio legis) fails to produce its ḥukm in a parallel case, thereby exposing its inconsistency.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal untying; rhetorically, it is the demonstration of a counter-instance that "unravels" the claimed universality of the cause.
- Root: ق-و-ل (qawla)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Speech, assertion, utterance.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): al-qawl bi-mūjab (conceding the implication) is a technical move in jadal where the respondent accepts the opponent's ʿillah but denies its applicability to the disputed case.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal saying; here it is a performative concession — the "saying" that grants the antecedent while contesting the consequent.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Conditionality (al-sharṭ wa al-jazāʾ) — The syntactic structure "if X, then Y" governs the logical dependence of the ḥukm on the ʿillah; the objection targets either the protasis (existence of the ʿillah) or the apodosis (the ḥukm itself), and the grammar of concession (al-istithnāʾ) is used to isolate exceptions.
chapters.translation:
I say: These objections divide into valid and invalid. The valid ones are eight types.

**The First Type: The Objection of Prevention (al-manʿ)**

This occurs when the objection is directed at the attribute of the ratio legis (waṣf al-taʿlīl), obliging the proponent (al-muʿallil) to establish it. The objection targets the original case (al-aṣl) from four angles: (1) that the original case is not legally effective (lā yuʿallal), (2) that what he mentioned as the ʿillah is not the ʿillah, after conceding the principle of taʿlīl, (3) that the existence of what he posited as the ʿillah is denied, or (4) that the ḥukm itself is denied. For the proponent, it suffices to demonstrate a suggestive meaning (maʿnā mukhayyal) for the ḥukm in the original case, and thereby all these objections are repelled. He thereby establishes that the original case is legally effective by this ʿillah, and upon this the ḥukm follows once its suggestive character (ikhālah) is established. He may also shift to another original case (al-naql) if prevention is raised, or initiate the discussion of the original case anew if he anticipates prevention.

He is not permitted, however, to adduce evidence against a counter-example (naqḍ) that the questioner raises when prevention is asserted. The difference is that this would be an exit from the disputed question (masʾalah), for one might raise a case from marriage law as a counter-example against a case in the law of manumission-by-contract (kitābah). Rather, he must establish the original case if the proof in the branch case is prevented from being effective, as a matter of verification (taḥqīq). The questioner is not entitled to demonstrate the prevention by means of a counter-example, unlike the respondent, due to the procedural rule of dialectic (al-rasm al-jadalī): the respondent has not undertaken to be objected to in that manner. If he does so, it is not heeded, because he was not asked to do so. The Master (al-Ustādh, i.e., al-Isfarāyīnī) said: "Prevention is not an objection, because its establishment is possible for the respondent."
